# opencode-rust — Fix & Feature Plan

A step-by-step work plan for the repository
[`Habibullah485044/opencode-rust`](https://github.com/Habibullah485044/opencode-rust),
written so a coding AI can follow it one task at a time.

- **Based on:** commit `1f9044215e63` (22 Oct 2026). All 51 files were read.
- **Size:** 92 tasks, about 30,000 lines. Nobody should read it in one go.
  Read one task at a time.
- **Checked against the real code:**
  - Every "Find this code" block matches that commit character for character.
    Blocks marked "(after X-NN)" match the code as it is once task X-NN is done.
  - Each task's code was applied straight from this text to a copy of the repo. That copy was compiled and the task's new tests were run.
  - All 92 tasks were then applied **together, in the recommended order**, to one copy. That copy builds with 0 warnings, with and without the GUI feature, and its full test suite passes on Linux: **387 tests, 0 failures** (the 185
    original tests plus 202 new ones). A few steps are written as plain
    instructions instead of code blocks; a small helper applied those exactly as written.
- **Not checked:**
  - Nothing was run on Windows or macOS. The Windows-only code in F-04 and F-13 was compiled for the Windows target but never run.
  - F-12 is an outline without full code.
  - A few small P3 polish steps written only as prose (parts of B-41 and B-49) were not compiled.
  - The manual checks listed in the tasks (real terminal, real desktop window, real model APIs) were not run.
- **Baseline at that commit:** `cargo build` gives 0 warnings. `cargo test` runs
  185 tests: on Linux 184 pass and 1 fails
  (`inline_edit::tests::resolve_rejects_absolute_and_parent_escapes`). That test
  only works on Windows, and task **B-17** fixes it.

## For the human: how to use this file

1. Save this file in the root of the repository as `FIX_PLAN.md` (next to `Cargo.toml`).
2. Give your AI **one task at a time**. Example message:

   > Read `FIX_PLAN.md`, section "Part 0 — Rules for the AI" (the short
   > version is enough). Then do task **B-01** only. Follow every rule. When
   > you are done, give me the report from Appendix C.

3. **If your AI has a small context window**, never paste the whole file.
   Your `kaggle_setup_cell.py` starts Ollama with an 8,192-token context.
   Give it only "Part 0 — short version" plus the one task section. Every task
   starts with `<!-- TASK:ID -->` and ends with `<!-- END TASK:ID -->`, so
   it can read just those lines.
4. Do the tasks in the order of **Part 2 — Recommended order**. Phase 1
   fixes the most dangerous problems and makes later work safer.
5. After each task, check the work yourself before you merge:
   - run `cargo test`
   - read `git diff`
   - make sure only the files named in the task changed.
6. Keep a list of finished tasks in `PLAN_PROGRESS.md`. The rules tell the
   AI to update it.

What is in this file:

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| Part 0 | Rules for the AI — how to work, step by step (short and full versions) |
| Part 1 | Project map — what each file does, how a prompt flows through the code |
| Part 2 | Task index and recommended order |
| Part 3 | **S** — Security hardening |
| Part 4 | **B** — Bugs |
| Part 5 | **P** — Ponytail integration fixes |
| Part 6 | **F** — New features |
| Part 7 | **H** — Project hygiene (README, LICENSE, CI, build features) |
| Appendices | Things that look odd but are intentional · commands cheat sheet · report template · glossary |

Priorities: **P0** = do first (security or data loss), **P1** = soon,
**P2** = normal, **P3** = nice to have.
Sizes: **S** = under 1 hour, **M** = 2–4 hours, **L** = a day or more.

## Part 0 — Rules for the AI

### Part 0 — short version (for small models — read this before EVERY task)

1. Do **one** task only: the ID the human gave you. Read only that task section:
   from the line that starts with `<!-- TASK:` plus your ID, to the line that
   starts with `<!-- END TASK:` plus your ID.
   - Find it with `grep -n "^<!-- TASK:B-01 -->" FIX_PLAN.md`, using your ID.
   - In PowerShell: `Select-String -Path FIX_PLAN.md -Pattern "^<!-- TASK:B-01 -->"`.
2. Before editing: run `git status` (it must be clean). Create a branch:
   `git checkout -b task/<id>`. Run `cargo build` and `cargo test` and note the result.
3. Read the files listed in "Read first". In big files read only the named
   functions: search for the name first, then read around it.
4. Find code by **searching for the quoted text**, never by line number.
   Line numbers in this plan are approximate.
5. Change **only** what the step says. No renaming, no reformatting, no extra
   "improvements". Never run `cargo fmt`.
6. After every step that changes Rust code: run `cargo build`. Fix the first
   error, build again. After 3 failed tries: **stop** and report.
7. Add the tests from "Tests to add". Run `cargo test`. Never delete, ignore or
   weaken an existing test.
8. Check every box in "Check you are done". Run `git diff --stat`: only the files
   listed in the task may appear.
9. Commit: `git add -A` then `git commit -m "<ID>: <task title>"`.
   Add one line to `PLAN_PROGRESS.md`. Then report to the human (Appendix C).
10. **Stop and ask** if:
    - the quoted code is missing,
    - a step does not match the code,
    - an old test fails,
    - the task needs a decision that is not written down.
11. Never: `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `cargo update`, change
    dependency versions, add dependencies the task does not name, commit secrets,
    or run `cargo build --release` while opencode-rust itself is running from
    `target/release` (Windows locks the running `.exe`).

### Part 0 — full version

#### 0.1 What you are doing

You are improving the Rust project **opencode-rust**, an AI coding agent with
a terminal UI, a headless mode and a Windows desktop app. This file is a list
of tasks. Each task is self-contained: it says what is wrong, where the code is,
exactly what to change, which tests to add and how to know you are done.

Do **one task at a time**. If the human did not name a task, take the first task
in "Part 2 — Recommended order" that is not listed in `PLAN_PROGRESS.md`.

#### 0.2 Reading only what you need

Your memory (context window) may be small. Do not read this whole file.

- Find the start of your task.
  - PowerShell: `Select-String -Path FIX_PLAN.md -Pattern "^<!-- TASK:B-01 -->"`
  - bash: `grep -n "^<!-- TASK:B-01 -->" FIX_PLAN.md`
  - The `^` means "at the start of a line". It makes sure you find the task itself, not this example.
- Read from that line down to the line that starts with `<!-- END TASK:` and
  the same ID. Use the same kind of search to find it, with `END TASK` instead of `TASK`.
- Read the files in "Read first". Some files are big: `src/server.rs` has about
  2,500 lines and `src/gui.html` about 2,150. Search for the function name first,
  then read only that region (about 80 lines around it).

#### 0.3 Before you change anything

1. Run `git status`. If it shows changes you did not make, **stop** and ask the human.
2. Make a branch for the task: `git checkout -b task/b-01` (use your task ID, lowercase).
3. Run `cargo build`. The first build can take 3–5 minutes.
4. Run `cargo test` and write down the result.
   - Expected: everything passes.
   - On Linux/macOS, `inline_edit::tests::resolve_rejects_absolute_and_parent_escapes`
     also fails until task B-17 is done.
   - If anything else fails before you start: **stop** and tell the human.

#### 0.4 How to find the code

- Line numbers in this plan come from commit `1f9044215e63`. After other tasks
  they move. **Always search for the quoted text.**
- A block that starts with "Find this code in `file`:" is an exact copy of the
  code. Search for its most unusual line, then compare the whole block.
- A block marked "Find this code in `file` (after X-NN):" only exists after task
  X-NN is done. If X-NN is not done yet, do X-NN first.
- If you cannot find the code:
  1. An earlier task may have changed it. Look in the same function for code
     that does the same job. Apply the same change there and say so in your report.
  2. If you still cannot find it: **stop** and report. Never guess where code goes.

#### 0.5 How to edit

- Change only what the step says. Do not tidy nearby code, rename things,
  reorder imports or reformat.
- **Never run `cargo fmt`.** The repository is not formatted with rustfmt, so it
  would change hundreds of unrelated lines.
- Edit with search-and-replace, using a search text that appears exactly once in
  the file. Never use an empty search text.
- Keep the file's indentation: 4 spaces in Rust; look at the surrounding lines in
  HTML/JS.
- "Add this at the end of `mod tests`" means: inside the `mod tests { ... }` block,
  just before its final closing `}`.
- "Replace it with" means: the whole found block goes away and the new block
  takes its place.
- Add a `use` line only when a step says so or the compiler says a name is not found.

#### 0.6 Build after every Rust change

Run `cargo build` after every step that changes a `.rs` file. If it fails, read
only the **first** error. Common errors and what they usually mean:

| Error text | Usual cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `cannot find value/function/type X in this scope` | missing `use`, or a typo | compare the name with the step; add the `use` the step gives |
| `no field X on type Y` / `missing field X` | a struct changed in an earlier step | check you did every earlier step of this task |
| `mismatched types` | wrong type in your edit | compare your code with the step letter by letter |
| `use of moved value` | value used after being moved | look for a `.clone()` in the step that you missed |
| `unused variable` / `unused import` (warning) | you added something that is not used | remove only what you added, or finish the step that uses it |

After 3 failed attempts on the same error: **stop**, run `git diff`, and report
both the diff and the error.

#### 0.7 Tests

- Add every test from "Tests to add" exactly where the task says.
- Run your new test first: `cargo test <test_name>`. Then run the full `cargo test`.
- **Never** delete a test, add `#[ignore]`, or weaken an assertion to make it pass.
  If an old test fails because the task changes behaviour on purpose, the task
  tells you how to update it. If it does not: **stop** and report.

#### 0.8 Finishing a task

1. Tick every box in "Check you are done". All of them must be true.
2. Run `git diff --stat`. Only the files listed in "Files to change" (and their
   tests) may appear. Undo changes to any other file.
3. Commit:
   ```
   git add -A
   git commit -m "B-01: edit tool rejects an empty old_str"
   ```
4. Add a line to `PLAN_PROGRESS.md` (create it if missing):
   `- [x] B-01 edit tool rejects an empty old_str — 2026-10-23 — cargo test: 186 passed`
5. Report to the human with the template in Appendix C.
6. Do not merge or push unless the human asks.

#### 0.9 Never do these

- Never `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, rewrite history, or delete branches you did not create.
- Never run `cargo update`, change versions in `Cargo.toml`, or add a dependency the task does not name.
- Never change the versions of `wry`, `tao`, `webview2-com` or `windows`. They must match each other.
- Never edit the text of `src/prompts/ponytail.md` or `src/prompts/ponytail-review.md`. They are third-party MIT text and their license header must stay.
- Never commit secrets: API keys, tokens, `.env`, `*.db`, `config.toml` with a real key.
- Never run `cargo build --release` while opencode-rust itself runs from `target/release` (Windows locks the running `.exe`). `cargo build` and `cargo test` use `target/debug` and are fine.
- Never start a server in the foreground without a timeout; it blocks you forever. Start servers (such as the mock LLM) in a separate terminal or in the background.
- Never do two tasks on one branch.

#### 0.10 When to stop and ask the human

- The quoted code does not exist and you cannot find code that does the same job.
- A step contradicts the code you see.
- The build still fails after 3 attempts.
- An existing test fails and the task does not say it should change.
- The task needs a choice that is not written down (a name, a default value, a design).

Stopping and asking is always better than guessing.

#### 0.11 If you are opencode-rust itself (running inside this program)

You are editing the program you run in. Your tools work like this (until the
tasks that change them are done):

- `read` — `offset` is the number of lines to **skip** (0-based) and `limit` defaults to 2000. The line numbers it prints start at 1. To read lines 300–380, use `offset: 299, limit: 81`. (After task B-30, `offset` is the first line to show, 1-based: `offset: 300`.)
- `glob` — prints paths relative to the folder you searched in. After task B-32 the paths are relative to the workspace, like `grep`.
- `edit` — `old_str` must match exactly and appear exactly once (or set `replace_all`). **Never send an empty `old_str`**: with `replace_all` it corrupts the file (bug B-01).
- `write` — replaces the **whole** file. Use it only for new files. For existing files use `edit`.
- `grep` — regex search, at most 200 results. `glob` — `*`, `?`, `**`; braces like `{rs,toml}` do **not** work.
- `bash` — default timeout 120 seconds, maximum 600. The first `cargo build` can take minutes: pass `timeout_secs: 600`.
- Keep Turbo mode **off**, so the human sees and approves your writes.
- After a change to the agent's own code, the running copy does not change. Your changes take effect only after a rebuild and restart, which the human does.

#### 0.12 Windows notes

- PowerShell: set env vars with `$env:NAME="value"`. In Windows PowerShell 5,
  chain commands with `;` (`&&` only works in PowerShell 7).
- Search: `Select-String -Path src\server.rs -Pattern "fn run_loop"`.
- In Rust code and in git commands, `/` works as a path separator on Windows too.
- `tests/gui/run.sh` needs Git Bash and Microsoft Edge (until H-05 makes it portable).

## Part 1 — Project map

### 1.1 What the program is

opencode-rust is an AI coding agent. It sends your request to a language model
through an **OpenAI-compatible** chat API. The model replies with text and
**tool calls**: run a command, read or edit a file, search, fetch a web page.
The program checks each tool call against **permission rules**, asks you when
needed, runs the tool and sends the result back to the model. That repeats
until the model stops calling tools.

You can drive it from three front-ends:

| Front-end | How to start | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal UI (default) | `opencode-rust` | `src/tui/` |
| Headless (one prompt, prints, exits) | `opencode-rust --headless "prompt"` | `src/main.rs` (`headless_run`) |
| Desktop app with a browser panel (Windows, WebView2) | `opencode-rust --gui` | `src/gui.rs`, `src/gui.html` |

All three share one in-process core: `AppState` in `src/server.rs`. The core
also serves a small HTTP API on `127.0.0.1` (the UIs do not use it; other
programs can).

### 1.3 How one prompt flows through the code

1. **The UI submits text.** The TUI or GUI calls `AppState::kick_run(session_id, text)`
   (`server.rs`). A new prompt on a busy session **replaces** the running run.
2. **`run_agent`**:
   - takes a git snapshot (`gitsnap::record_before_run`) so `/undo` works;
   - calls `agent_inner`;
   - afterwards may run the automatic ponytail review and the Turbo continuation.
3. **`agent_inner`**:
   - stores the user message in SQLite;
   - expands `.opencode/commands` templates;
   - builds the system prompt (`agents::compose_system`: base prompt, `AGENTS.md`, skills index, subagents, ponytail rules, plan-mode text);
   - calls `run_loop`.
4. **`run_loop`** repeats up to `agent.max_steps` (default 40) times:
   1. Build the tool list: `tools::tool_specs()`, plus browser tools if the GUI panel is open, plus MCP tools, plus `spawn`. Filter it by mode (plan mode = read-only tools).
   2. Rebuild the chat history from the DB (`build_chat_messages`) and stream a completion (`provider::Client::stream`).
   3. Collect text, reasoning and tool calls (`ToolCallAccumulator`). Store the assistant message.
   4. For each tool call:
      1. `tool_allowed` checks the mode and role.
      2. `check_permission` applies rules, then defaults, then mode. On "ask" it emits `ApprovalNeeded` and waits up to `approval_timeout_secs` (300).
      3. `execute_routed` runs the call: MCP, `spawn`, `todo`, browser, or `tools::execute`.
      4. `finish_tool_call` updates the Laziness Meter, detects dev servers and stores the result.
   5. Stop when the model makes no more tool calls.
5. **`RunFinished`** is emitted. The UI shows the result.

### 1.4 Events

`AppState.events` is a `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel with capacity 256.
Every UI subscribes:

- the TUI through a forwarder task;
- the GUI through a forwarder task;
- headless reads it directly;
- the HTTP route `GET /api/events` streams it as SSE.

The `ServerEvent` variants are:

| Group | Variants |
|---|---|
| Streaming | `AssistantDelta`, `ReasoningDelta` |
| Tool activity | `ToolStarted`, `ToolFinished`, `DevServer` |
| Approvals and run state | `ApprovalNeeded`, `RunFinished` |
| Sessions | `SessionCreated`, `SessionLoaded`, `SessionList`, `ModelInfo` |
| Inline edit | `EditPreview`, `EditApplied` |
| Other | `Heartbeat`, `Note`, `Stats`, `AgentStatus` |

Task B-10 adds `ApprovalResolved`.

### 1.5 Where things are stored

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Config file | `~/.config/opencode-rust/config.toml` (Windows: `C:\Users\<you>\.config\opencode-rust\config.toml`), or the path in `OPENCODE_RUST_CONFIG` |
| Env overrides | `OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_RUST_BASE_URL`, `OPENCODE_RUST_MODEL` (they win over the file) |
| State folder | Windows `%APPDATA%\opencode-rust`; elsewhere `~/.local/share/opencode-rust` |
| Database | `<state>/opencode.db`. Tables: `sessions`, `messages` (parts as JSON), `approvals` |
| Snapshots | `<state>/snaps_<hash>/...` with `undo.json` / `redo.json` stacks (max 20) |
| Crash log | `<state>/crash.log` |
| Skills | `<workspace>/.opencode/skills/` then `~/.config/opencode-rust/skills/` |
| Command templates | `<workspace>/.opencode/commands/` then `~/.config/opencode-rust/commands/` |
| Project instructions | `<workspace>/AGENTS.md` |

| | `api_key` | `""` | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` when not empty |

| | `rules` | `[]` | `{ tool, pattern, action }`, first match wins |
| | `approval_timeout_secs` | 300 | How long an "ask" waits before it becomes a deny |

### 1.7 Tests

- Unit tests sit at the bottom of each module (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`). Run them all with `cargo test`.
- Many tests start a small fake model server with `axum` inside the test. Look at them before writing a new one, and copy their pattern.
- GUI page tests are `tests/gui/panel.js` and `tests/gui/runtime.js`, run by `tests/gui/run.sh` in headless Edge.
- End-to-end runs use the mock model in `examples/mock_llm.rs` (Appendix B).

## Part 3 — S: Security hardening

These tasks close holes that let the model, a web page or another program on
the machine do more than you allowed. Do the P0 ones first.


<!-- TASK:S-01 -->
### S-01 · Require a token on the local HTTP API

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn router`, `fn health`, `fn serve`; `src/main.rs`: `fn run`, `fn print_help` |

#### What is wrong

At start the core opens an HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` (function `serve` in `src/server.rs`). No route checks who is calling. Any program on the computer can start agent runs (`POST /api/sessions/{id}/prompt`), answer approval prompts (`POST /api/approvals/{id}`) and read every message and tool output (`GET /api/events`, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`). The server also accepts any `Host` header, so a web page can reach it through a domain name that points to 127.0.0.1 (this is called "DNS rebinding").

The TUI and the GUI do not use HTTP. They call `AppState` directly, so this change does not affect them.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
/// Bind and serve. Returns the actual address (useful with port 0).
pub async fn serve(state: Shared, port: u16) -> Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let app = router(state).route("/api/health", get(health));
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await?;
    let addr = listener.local_addr()?;
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
    });
    Ok(addr)
}
```

#### Why it matters

A local program or a malicious web page can send a prompt, then approve its own `bash` call, and run commands with your rights. It can also read secrets that the agent printed.

#### Steps

How the fix works. Every request must carry the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. `/api/health` is the only exception. The token comes from the environment variable `OPENCODE_RUST_API_TOKEN` when it is set. Otherwise a new random token is made at every start and written to the file `<state_dir>/api-token`. `<state_dir>` is `%APPDATA%\opencode-rust` on Windows and `~/.local/share/opencode-rust` elsewhere. Every request must also be addressed to `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`. The program prints where the token file is, never the token itself.

```rust
/// New (S-01): environment variable that fixes the API token. When it is
/// not set, every start makes a new random token (see `resolve_api_token`).
pub const API_TOKEN_ENV: &str = "OPENCODE_RUST_API_TOKEN";

/// New (S-01): what every HTTP request must match (built once in `serve`).
struct ApiGuard {
    /// Expected value after `Authorization: Bearer `.
    token: String,
    /// The port we listen on; the `Host` header must name it.
    port: u16,
}

/// New (S-01): where a generated token is written: `<state_dir>/api-token`.
pub fn api_token_path(state_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
    state_dir.join("api-token")
}

/// New (S-01): one line for the startup output that says where the token
/// is. It never contains the token itself.
pub fn api_token_note(state_dir: &std::path::Path) -> String {
    match std::env::var(API_TOKEN_ENV) {
        Ok(v) if !v.trim().is_empty() => format!("API token: from ${API_TOKEN_ENV}"),
        _ => format!("API token file: {}", api_token_path(state_dir).display()),
    }
}

/// New (S-01): the token for this start: `$OPENCODE_RUST_API_TOKEN` when
/// set, else a fresh random token written to `<state_dir>/api-token`
/// (on Linux/macOS only your user can read that file).
fn resolve_api_token(state_dir: &std::path::Path) -> Result<String> {
    if let Ok(v) = std::env::var(API_TOKEN_ENV) {
        let v = v.trim().to_string();
        if !v.is_empty() {
            return Ok(v);
        }
    }
    let token = random_token();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(state_dir)
        .with_context(|| format!("creating {}", state_dir.display()))?;
    let path = api_token_path(state_dir);
    // Remove the old file first: on Unix the mode below only applies to a
    // file that is newly created.
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
    let mut opts = std::fs::OpenOptions::new();
    opts.write(true).create_new(true);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
        opts.mode(0o600);
    }
    let mut file = opts
        .open(&path)
        .with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
    std::io::Write::write_all(&mut file, token.as_bytes())
        .with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(token)
}

/// New (S-01): a 256-bit random token as 64 hex characters. `RandomState`
/// is seeded from the operating system's random source once per process;
/// hashing it with the time, the process id and a counter is good enough
/// for a local-only secret (it is not a general-purpose crypto RNG).
fn random_token() -> String {
    use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(64);
    for i in 0..4u64 {
        let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new().build_hasher();
        h.write_u64(i);
        h.write_u128(nanos);
        h.write_u32(std::process::id());
        out.push_str(&format!("{:016x}", h.finish()));
    }
    out
}

/// New (S-01): the `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1:<port>` or
/// `localhost:<port>`. A web page from another site that points its own
/// domain name at 127.0.0.1 still sends that domain name, so it is refused.
fn host_allowed(headers: &axum::http::HeaderMap, port: u16) -> bool {
    let Some(host) = headers
        .get(axum::http::header::HOST)
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
    else {
        return false;
    };
    let host = host.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    let (name, host_port) = match host.rsplit_once(':') {
        Some((name, p)) => (name.to_string(), p.parse::<u16>().ok()),
        None => (host.clone(), Some(80)),
    };
    (name == "127.0.0.1" || name == "localhost") && host_port == Some(port)
}

/// New (S-01): compare two secrets without stopping at the first
/// difference (the time taken does not reveal how much matched).
fn same_secret(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    a.len() == b.len() && a.iter().zip(b).fold(0u8, |acc, (x, y)| acc | (x ^ y)) == 0
}

/// New (S-01): middleware in front of every route (see `serve`).
async fn require_token(
    State(guard): State<Arc<ApiGuard>>,
    req: axum::extract::Request,
    next: axum::middleware::Next,
) -> axum::response::Response {
    use axum::response::IntoResponse;
    if !host_allowed(req.headers(), guard.port) {
        return (StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "forbidden: unexpected Host header").into_response();
    }
    if req.uri().path() != "/api/health" {
        let presented = req
            .headers()
            .get(axum::http::header::AUTHORIZATION)
            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
            .and_then(|v| v.strip_prefix("Bearer "))
            .unwrap_or("")
            .trim();
        if !same_secret(presented.as_bytes(), guard.token.as_bytes()) {
            return (
                StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
                [(axum::http::header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE, "Bearer")],
                "unauthorized: send the header Authorization: Bearer <token>",
            )
                .into_response();
        }
    }
    next.run(req).await
}
```

2. In the same file, replace the function `serve` (right below what you just added). The new `serve` loads the token and hands over to a new function `serve_with_token`, which tests can call with a known token.

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
/// Bind and serve. Returns the actual address (useful with port 0).
pub async fn serve(state: Shared, port: u16) -> Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let app = router(state).route("/api/health", get(health));
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await?;
    let addr = listener.local_addr()?;
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
    });
    Ok(addr)
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Bind and serve. Returns the actual address (useful with port 0).
/// New (S-01): every route except `/api/health` needs the header
/// `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and every request must be addressed to
/// `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>` (the `Host` header).
pub async fn serve(state: Shared, port: u16) -> Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let token = resolve_api_token(&state.state_dir)?;
    serve_with_token(state, port, token).await
}

/// New (S-01): `serve` with a token you choose (tests use this).
pub async fn serve_with_token(
    state: Shared,
    port: u16,
    token: String,
) -> Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await?;
    let addr = listener.local_addr()?;
    let guard = Arc::new(ApiGuard { token, port: addr.port() });
    let app = router(state)
        .route("/api/health", get(health))
        .layer(axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state(guard, require_token));
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
    });
    Ok(addr)
}
```

### S-02 · Headless mode must not approve tool calls by default

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/main.rs`: `fn headless_run` (the event loop at its end), `fn print_help` |

#### What is wrong

`opencode-rust --headless "<prompt>"` runs one prompt with nobody watching. When the agent asks for approval (for example before `bash` or `write`), the headless event loop answers "yes" by itself. It only says "no" when the environment variable `OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_DENY=1` is set. So by default a headless run may execute any shell command or overwrite any file the model asks for. `--help` does not mention this.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust
            Ok(server::ServerEvent::ApprovalNeeded { approval_id, tool, detail, .. }) => {
                // Headless: auto-approve unless OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_DENY=1.
                let auto_deny =
                    std::env::var("OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_DENY").map(|v| v == "1").unwrap_or(false);
                eprintln!(
                    "\n[approval] {tool}: {detail} → {}",
                    if auto_deny { "denied" } else { "auto-approved (headless)" }
                );
                let _ = state.decide(&approval_id, !auto_deny, false);
            }
```

#### Why it matters

A prompt-injected web page or file read during an unattended run can make the model run destructive commands, and nobody ever sees an approval prompt.

#### Steps

New behaviour: deny by default. The new flag `--yes` or the environment variable `OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_APPROVE=1` turns auto-approve on. `OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_DENY=1` keeps working and always wins.

1. Open `src/main.rs`. Find the start of the function `headless_run` (around line 220). Add two new functions right above it.

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:

```rust
async fn headless_run(
    state: std::sync::Arc<server::AppState>,
    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,
    prompt: Option<String>,
    boot_ms: u128,

```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (S-02): may headless mode say "yes" to approval prompts by itself?
/// Default: no. `--yes` (before any `--`) or OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_APPROVE=1
/// turns it on; OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_DENY=1 always wins and forces "no".
fn auto_approve_policy(args: &[String], approve_env: Option<&str>, deny_env: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    if deny_env.map(str::trim) == Some("1") {
        return false;
    }
    let yes_flag = args.iter().take_while(|a| a.as_str() != "--").any(|a| a == "--yes");
    yes_flag || approve_env.map(str::trim) == Some("1")
}

/// New (S-02): `auto_approve_policy` for this process (its real command
/// line and environment).
fn headless_auto_approve() -> bool {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let approve = std::env::var("OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_APPROVE").ok();
    let deny = std::env::var("OPENCODE_RUST_AUTO_DENY").ok();
    auto_approve_policy(&args, approve.as_deref(), deny.as_deref())
}

async fn headless_run(
    state: std::sync::Arc<server::AppState>,
    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,
    prompt: Option<String>,
    boot_ms: u128,
) -> Result<()> {
```

### S-03 · Keep file tools inside the workspace

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/tools.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tools.rs`: `fn resolve`, `fn read_file`, `fn write_file`, `fn edit_file`, `fn glob_files`, `fn grep_files`, `fn list_dir` |

#### What is wrong

The file tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `list`, `glob`, `grep`) accept any path the model sends. `fn resolve` joins relative paths onto the workspace but passes absolute paths and `..` through unchanged, so the model can read or overwrite files anywhere the user can. `read`, `list`, `glob` and `grep` are allowed without asking by default. A symlink inside the workspace that points outside it is followed too.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
fn resolve(workspace: &Path, path: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let p = Path::new(path);
    if p.is_absolute() { p.to_path_buf() } else { workspace.join(p) }
}
```

#### Why it matters

One confused or prompt-injected model turn can read private files (SSH keys, the opencode config with the API key) and send them to the provider, or overwrite files outside the project, without any prompt.

#### Steps

**Stage 1: the new helper**

1. Open `src/tools.rs` and find `fn resolve` (around line 175). Add the new shared helper `confine_path` right before it; task S-15 reuses it. It returns an absolute path inside the workspace, or an error telling the model to stay inside. Keep `resolve` for now; stage 2 removes it.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
fn resolve(workspace: &Path, path: &str) -> PathBuf {

}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// S-03: turn a path the model gave into an absolute path that is guaranteed
/// to be inside the workspace, or an error the model can act on.
/// 1. Relative paths are joined onto the workspace.
/// 2. `.` and `..` are applied as text first, so `src/../../x` cannot climb out.
/// 3. The part that exists on disk is resolved with `canonicalize` (follows
///    symlinks). A symlink leading outside, or a broken symlink, is refused.
/// 4. The result keeps the workspace prefix as `workspace` spells it (no
///    `\\?\` prefix on Windows).
pub fn confine_path(workspace: &Path, raw: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let outside = || {
        anyhow!(
            "`{raw}` is outside the workspace ({}). File tools only work inside the \
             workspace: use a path relative to it, for example `src/main.rs`.",
            workspace.display()
        )
    };
    // On Windows both `/` and `\` separate folders. Use `\` everywhere so a
    // `\\?\` path cannot hide a `/` inside one path part.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let raw_owned = raw.replace('/', "\\");
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let raw: &str = &raw_owned;
    let root = workspace
        .canonicalize()
        .with_context(|| format!("workspace {} is not accessible", workspace.display()))?;
    let base = std::path::absolute(workspace).unwrap_or_else(|_| workspace.to_path_buf());
    let given = Path::new(raw);
    let joined = if given.is_absolute() { given.to_path_buf() } else { base.join(given) };
    // Step 2: apply `.` and `..` without touching the disk.
    let mut norm = PathBuf::new();
    for part in joined.components() {
        match part {
            std::path::Component::CurDir => {}
            std::path::Component::ParentDir => {
                if !norm.pop() {
                    return Err(outside());
                }
            }
            other => norm.push(other.as_os_str()),
        }
    }
    // Step 3: find the longest part that exists (a symlink counts as
    // existing, even a broken one) and resolve it.
    let mut existing = norm.clone();
    let mut missing: Vec<std::ffi::OsString> = Vec::new();
    while std::fs::symlink_metadata(&existing).is_err() {
        match existing.file_name() {
            Some(name) => {
                missing.push(name.to_os_string());
                existing.pop();
            }
            None => break,
        }
    }
    let mut real = existing
        .canonicalize()
        .map_err(|_| anyhow!("cannot resolve `{raw}` (broken symlink or unreadable folder)"))?;
    for name in missing.iter().rev() {
        real.push(name);
    }
    // Step 4: the resolved path must still be inside the workspace.
    let inside = real.strip_prefix(&root).map_err(|_| outside())?;
    Ok(workspace.join(inside))
}

fn resolve(workspace: &Path, path: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let p = Path::new(path);
    if p.is_absolute() { p.to_path_buf() } else { workspace.join(p) }
}
```

```rust
mod s03_confine_tests {
    use super::*;

    pub fn temp_dir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_nanos();
        let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ocrs-s03-{tag}-{}-{nanos}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&p).unwrap();
        p
    }

    #[test]
    fn confine_path_keeps_inside_paths() {
        let ws = temp_dir("inside");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(ws.join("src")).unwrap();
        let p = confine_path(&ws, "src/../src/main.rs").unwrap();
        assert!(p.starts_with(&ws) && p.ends_with("src/main.rs"), "{}", p.display());
        // A file that does not exist yet (write creates it) is fine.
        assert!(confine_path(&ws, "new/dir/file.txt").unwrap().starts_with(&ws));
        // An absolute path inside the workspace is fine.
        let abs = ws.join("src").join("lib.rs");
        assert!(confine_path(&ws, abs.to_str().unwrap()).is_ok());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&ws);
    }

            let err = confine_path(&ws, bad).unwrap_err().to_string();
            assert!(err.contains("outside the workspace"), "{bad}: {err}");
        }
        assert!(confine_path(&ws, other.join("x.txt").to_str().unwrap()).is_err());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&ws);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&other);
    }

    #[cfg(unix)]
    #[test]
    fn confine_path_rejects_symlinks_that_leave() {
        let ws = temp_dir("link");
        let other = temp_dir("target");
        std::fs::write(other.join("secret.txt"), "s").unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&other, ws.join("out")).unwrap();
        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(other.join("missing.txt"), ws.join("dangling")).unwrap();
        assert!(confine_path(&ws, "out/secret.txt").is_err());
        assert!(confine_path(&ws, "out/new.txt").is_err());
        assert!(confine_path(&ws, "dangling").is_err());
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&ws);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&other);
    }
}
```

### S-04 · Canonical path details for permission rules (no `..`, Windows case)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/permissions.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `config.example.toml` |
| Read first | `src/permissions.rs`: `fn normalize_path_detail`, `fn evaluate`; `src/server.rs`: `fn tool_detail` |

#### What is wrong

Permission rules for file tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `list`, `glob`,
`grep`) are matched against a "detail" string made from the path the model
asked for. `normalize_path_detail` only strips the workspace prefix. It does
not resolve `.` or `..`, and it does not follow symlinks. So `src/../.env`
and `./.env` do not match a rule written as `.env`. A path outside the
workspace becomes a plain absolute path, which a pattern starting with `*`
can match by accident. On Windows, paths ignore letter case, but rule
matching does not, so `Secrets/key.pem` slips past a rule for `secrets/*`.
The `list` tool skips normalization completely.

```rust
    abs.strip_prefix(workspace)
        .map(|r| r.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| abs.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"))
}
```

```rust
/// The subset of path a detail represents, for rule matching:
/// commands matched verbatim, paths matched workspace-relative with `/`.
pub fn normalize_path_detail(workspace: &std::path::Path, path: &str) -> String {
    let p = std::path::Path::new(path);
    let abs = if p.is_absolute() { p.to_path_buf() } else { workspace.join(p) };
    abs.strip_prefix(workspace)
        .map(|r| r.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| abs.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"))
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Tools whose permission detail is a file path (see `tool_detail` in server.rs).
pub fn is_path_tool(tool: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(tool, "read" | "write" | "edit" | "list" | "glob" | "grep")
}

/// Rule pattern vs. detail. `fold_case` compares without letter case
/// (Windows file paths: `Secrets\a.txt` and `secrets\a.txt` are one file).
fn detail_matches(pattern: &str, detail: &str, fold_case: bool) -> bool {
    if fold_case {
        glob_match(&pattern.to_lowercase(), &detail.to_lowercase())
    } else {
        glob_match(pattern, detail)
    }
}

/// Start of a path detail that lies OUTSIDE the workspace, for example
/// `outside:/etc/hosts`. Workspace rules (`src/*`, `.env`) never match it;
/// a rule must name it on purpose (`outside:/tmp/*`).
pub const OUTSIDE_PREFIX: &str = "outside:";

/// The path detail used for rule matching and for "always allow":
/// - `.` and `..` are resolved, so `src/../.env` becomes `.env`;
/// - symlinks are followed for the part of the path that exists, so a link
///   inside the workspace that points elsewhere counts as outside;
/// - inside the workspace: relative with `/` (`src/main.rs`; `.` is the
///   workspace itself);
/// - outside the workspace: [`OUTSIDE_PREFIX`] + the absolute path;
/// - on Windows the result is lower-case (paths there ignore case).
pub fn normalize_path_detail(workspace: &std::path::Path, path: &str) -> String {
    normalize_path_detail_with(workspace, path, cfg!(windows))
}

/// [`normalize_path_detail`] with explicit case folding, so tests can check
/// the Windows behaviour on every platform.
pub fn normalize_path_detail_with(workspace: &std::path::Path, path: &str, fold_case: bool) -> String {
    let p = std::path::Path::new(path.trim());
    let joined = if p.is_absolute() { p.to_path_buf() } else { workspace.join(p) };
    let ws = resolve_for_rules(workspace);
    let abs = resolve_for_rules(&joined);
    let out = match abs.strip_prefix(&ws) {
        Ok(rel) => {
            let rel = rel.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
            if rel.is_empty() { ".".to_string() } else { rel }
        }
        Err(_) => format!("{OUTSIDE_PREFIX}{}", display_abs(&abs)),
    };
    if fold_case { out.to_lowercase() } else { out }
}

/// Resolve a path the way the file system will: canonical when it exists;
/// otherwise `.`/`..` are removed by hand, the longest existing parent is
/// canonicalized, and the missing tail is appended as written.
fn resolve_for_rules(p: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    if let Ok(c) = std::fs::canonicalize(p) {
        return c;
    }
    let clean = lexical_normalize(p);
    let mut existing = clean.as_path();
    let mut tail: Vec<&std::ffi::OsStr> = Vec::new();
    loop {
        if let Ok(mut c) = std::fs::canonicalize(existing) {
            for part in tail.iter().rev() {
                c.push(part);
            }
            return c;
        }
        match (existing.parent(), existing.file_name()) {
            (Some(parent), Some(name)) => {
                tail.push(name);
                existing = parent;
            }
            _ => return clean,
        }
    }
}

/// Remove `.` and `..` without touching the disk. `..` never climbs above
/// the root of an absolute path.
fn lexical_normalize(p: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    use std::path::Component;
    let mut out = std::path::PathBuf::new();
    for c in p.components() {
        match c {
            Component::CurDir => {}
            Component::ParentDir => {
                if matches!(out.components().next_back(), Some(Component::Normal(_))) {
                    out.pop();
                } else if !out.has_root() {
                    out.push("..");
                }
            }
            other => out.push(other.as_os_str()),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// An absolute path for display: `/` separators, no Windows `\\?\` prefix.
fn display_abs(p: &std::path::Path) -> String {
    let s = p.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix("//?/UNC/") {
        format!("//{rest}")
    } else if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix("//?/") {
        rest.to_string()
    } else {
        s
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Environment variables that hold opencode-rust's own secrets (S-05).
/// Child processes (bash, MCP servers, git) never get them.
pub const SECRET_ENV_VARS: [&str; 2] = ["OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY", "OPENCODE_RUST_API_TOKEN"];

/// Remove our secrets from a child process's environment (S-05).
pub fn scrub_secrets(cmd: &mut tokio::process::Command) -> &mut tokio::process::Command {
    for key in SECRET_ENV_VARS {

    }
    cmd
}
```

#### What is wrong

`webfetch` only checks that the URL starts with `http://` or `https://`. It fetches any host: `localhost`, the home router, other machines on the LAN, cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`). reqwest follows up to 10 redirects by itself, so a public URL can bounce to a private address. `resp.text()` loads the whole body before the 40,000-character cut, so a huge page can exhaust memory. The tool is in Plan mode and in the read-only `explore` subagent, and Turbo mode never asks.

#### Why it matters

Fetched page text goes straight back to a model that can also run `bash`. A page that tells the model to fetch `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` or the metadata URL turns the agent into a tool for reading services that were never meant to be reachable from outside.

#### Steps

**Stage 1: decide which addresses are public**

1. Open `src/tools.rs` and find `async fn webfetch` (around line 361). Add the new function `is_public_ip` right before it. It is `pub` so other code (for example the GUI's URL checks) can reuse it.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
async fn webfetch(url: &str) -> Result<String> {

```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// S-06: true only for normal public internet addresses. Loopback, private,
/// link-local (cloud metadata), shared/CGNAT, multicast, broadcast,
/// documentation, benchmarking, reserved and unspecified addresses are not.
/// IPv6 forms that wrap an IPv4 address are judged by that IPv4 address.
pub fn is_public_ip(ip: std::net::IpAddr) -> bool {
    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr};
    match ip {
        IpAddr::V4(v4) => {
            let [a, b, c, _] = v4.octets();
            !(v4.is_unspecified()
                || v4.is_loopback()
                || v4.is_private()
                || v4.is_link_local()
                || v4.is_broadcast()
                || v4.is_multicast()
                || v4.is_documentation()
                || a == 0
                || (a == 100 && (64..=127).contains(&b))
                || (a == 192 && b == 0 && c == 0)
                || (a == 198 && (b == 18 || b == 19))
                || a >= 240)
        }
        IpAddr::V6(v6) => {
            // ::ffff:a.b.c.d and ::a.b.c.d
            if let Some(v4) = v6.to_ipv4() {
                return is_public_ip(IpAddr::V4(v4));
            }
            let s = v6.segments();
            let embedded = |hi: u16, lo: u16| {
                IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new((hi >> 8) as u8, hi as u8, (lo >> 8) as u8, lo as u8))
            };
            // 64:ff9b::/96 (NAT64) and 2002::/16 (6to4) carry an IPv4 address.
            if s[0] == 0x64 && s[1] == 0xff9b && s[2..6] == [0, 0, 0, 0] {
                return is_public_ip(embedded(s[6], s[7]));
            }
            if s[0] == 0x2002 {
                return is_public_ip(embedded(s[1], s[2]));
            }
            !(v6.is_unspecified()
                || v6.is_loopback()
                || v6.is_multicast()
                || (s[0] & 0xfe00) == 0xfc00
                || (s[0] & 0xffc0) == 0xfe80
                || (s[0] & 0xffc0) == 0xfec0
                || (s[0] == 0x2001 && s[1] == 0x0db8))
        }
    }
}
```

3. Replace the whole `async fn webfetch` with the version below. It adds two new constants and the new function `fetch_checked`, which:
   - resolves the host before every request (the first one and every redirect) and refuses if ANY address is not public;
   - pins the request to exactly the checked addresses with `resolve_to_addrs`, so a second DNS lookup cannot swap in a private address ("DNS rebinding");
   - follows redirects by hand, at most 5;
   - reads the body in pieces with `chunk()` and stops at 2,000,000 bytes.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
async fn webfetch(url: &str) -> Result<String> {
    if !(url.starts_with("http://") || url.starts_with("https://")) {
        return Err(anyhow!("only http(s) urls are allowed"));
    }
    let http = reqwest::Client::builder()
        .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
        .user_agent("opencode-rust/0.1")
        .build()?;
    let resp = http.get(url).send().await.with_context(|| format!("fetching {url}"))?;
    let status = resp.status();
    if !status.is_success() {
        return Err(anyhow!("{url} returned {status}"));
    }
    let body = resp.text().await?;
    let text = html_to_text(&body);
    Ok(truncate(&text, 40_000))
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// webfetch reads at most this many bytes of a response body (S-06).
const WEBFETCH_MAX_BYTES: usize = 2_000_000;
/// webfetch follows at most this many redirects (S-06).
const WEBFETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS: usize = 5;

async fn webfetch(url: &str) -> Result<String> {
    fetch_checked(url, is_public_ip).await
}

/// S-06: GET `url` from addresses that pass `allowed` only. Checks every
/// hop, pins each request to the checked addresses, caps the body.
async fn fetch_checked(url: &str, allowed: fn(std::net::IpAddr) -> bool) -> Result<String> {
    let mut current = reqwest::Url::parse(url).with_context(|| format!("invalid url `{url}`"))?;
    for _ in 0..=WEBFETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS {
        if !matches!(current.scheme(), "http" | "https") {
            bail!("only http(s) urls are allowed");
        }
        let host = current
            .host_str()
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("url `{current}` has no host"))?
            .trim_start_matches('[')
            .trim_end_matches(']')
            .to_string();
        let port = current.port_or_known_default().unwrap_or(80);
        let addrs: Vec<std::net::SocketAddr> = match host.parse::<std::net::IpAddr>() {
            Ok(ip) => vec![std::net::SocketAddr::new(ip, port)],
            Err(_) => tokio::net::lookup_host((host.as_str(), port))
                .await
                .with_context(|| format!("cannot resolve {host}"))?
                .collect(),
        };
        if addrs.is_empty() {
            bail!("{host} did not resolve to any address");
        }
        if let Some(bad) = addrs.iter().find(|a| !allowed(a.ip())) {
            bail!(
                "refused: {host} points to {}, a local or private network address. \
                 webfetch only reads public internet pages.",
                bad.ip()
            );
        }
        let http = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))
            .user_agent("opencode-rust/0.1")
            .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
            .resolve_to_addrs(&host, &addrs)
            .build()?;
        let mut resp = http
            .get(current.clone())
            .send()
            .await
            .with_context(|| format!("fetching {current}"))?;
        let status = resp.status();
        if status.is_redirection() {
            let next = resp
                .headers()
                .get(reqwest::header::LOCATION)
                .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("{current} returned {status} without a Location header"))?;
            current = current
                .join(next)
                .with_context(|| format!("bad redirect target `{next}`"))?;
            continue;
        }
        if !status.is_success() {
            bail!("{current} returned {status}");
        }
        let mut body: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        let mut cut = false;
        while let Some(chunk) = resp.chunk().await? {
            let room = WEBFETCH_MAX_BYTES - body.len();
            if chunk.len() >= room {
                body.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..room]);
                cut = true;
                break;
            }
            body.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
        }
        let mut text = truncate(&html_to_text(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&body)), 40_000);
        if cut {
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "\n… [page is larger than {WEBFETCH_MAX_BYTES} bytes; only the start was read]"
            ));
        }
        return Ok(text);
    }
    bail!("too many redirects (more than {WEBFETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS}) starting at {url}")
}
```

4. Add tests for the fetch. They use only the local machine: `webfetch_refuses_local_hosts` never connects, because the address check fails first; the other tests call `fetch_checked` with a rule that allows only loopback, where the local test server runs.

Add this at the very end of `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod s06_fetch_tests {
    use super::*;
    use axum::http::{header, StatusCode};
    use axum::{routing::get, Router};

    fn loopback_only(ip: std::net::IpAddr) -> bool {
        ip.is_loopback()
    }

    async fn serve(app: Router) -> String {
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)).await.unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
        });
        format!("http://{addr}")
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn webfetch_refuses_local_hosts() {
        for url in ["http://127.0.0.1:9/", "http://localhost:9/", "http://[::1]:9/", "http://10.0.0.1/"] {
            let err = webfetch(url).await.unwrap_err().to_string();
            assert!(err.contains("refused"), "{url}: {err}");
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn every_redirect_is_checked_and_loops_stop() {
        let app = Router::new()
            .route("/start", get(|| async { (StatusCode::FOUND, [(header::LOCATION, "http://10.255.255.1/x")], "") }))
            .route("/loop", get(|| async { (StatusCode::FOUND, [(header::LOCATION, "/loop")], "") }));
        let base = serve(app).await;
        let err = fetch_checked(&format!("{base}/start"), loopback_only).await.unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("10.255.255.1"), "{err}");
        let err = fetch_checked(&format!("{base}/loop"), loopback_only).await.unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(err.contains("too many redirects"), "{err}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn big_bodies_are_cut() {
        let app = Router::new().route("/big", get(|| async { "a".repeat(3_000_000) }));
        let base = serve(app).await;
        let out = fetch_checked(&format!("{base}/big"), loopback_only).await.unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("only the start was read"), "size note missing");
    }
}
```

#### Do not

- Do not check the host name as text ("localhost", "127."). Names like `127.0.0.1.nip.io`, decimal IPs and IPv6 forms get around text checks; check the resolved addresses.
- Do not leave reqwest's automatic redirects on; they skip the check for the second and later hops.
- Do not call `resp.text()` or `resp.bytes()` before the size cap; they read everything into memory first.
- Do not allow a host when only SOME of its addresses are public; refuse if ANY is private.

### S-07 · Scope "Always allow" to the workspace and stop duplicate approvals

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/db.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `src/tui/draw.rs` |
| Read first | `src/db.rs`: `fn open`, `fn open_in_memory`, `fn add_approval`, `fn has_approval`; `src/server.rs`: `fn decide`, `fn check_permission` |

#### What is wrong

When you answer an approval with "always", `AppState::decide` stores
`(tool, detail)` in the `approvals` table of the main database. The table has
no column for the workspace or the session, and `has_approval` ignores the
`scope` column. So one "always" is valid in every project you ever open, for
ever, because the database file lives in the shared state directory. The TUI
even labels the key "always (session)". Also, `INSERT OR IGNORE` never
ignores anything: there is no UNIQUE constraint and every row gets a fresh
random id, so the same approval piles up again and again.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/db.rs`:
```rust

    pub fn add_approval(&self, tool: &str, pattern: &str, scope: &str) -> Result<()> {
        self.conn.lock().unwrap().execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO approvals (id, tool, pattern, scope, created_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5)",
            params![new_id("apr"), tool, pattern, scope, now_ms()],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }
```

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust

            let _ = self.db.add_approval(&entry.tool, &entry.detail, "session");

```

#### Why it matters

Saying "always" to `rm -rf build` in a throw-away project also allows it,
silently, in your real project next month. The decision must stay where the
user made it.

#### Steps

The new rule: an approval belongs to one workspace, identified by its
canonical path (`workspace_key`, new). Approvals saved by older versions have
no workspace. They are moved aside and **stop applying** — after this change
the user is asked once more for those commands. That is intended.

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Approvals table (S-07): one row per (workspace, tool, pattern).
const APPROVALS_SCHEMA: &str = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approvals (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    workspace TEXT NOT NULL,
    tool TEXT NOT NULL,
    pattern TEXT NOT NULL,
    scope TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'once' | 'session'
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (workspace, tool, pattern)
);";

/// Bring the approvals table to the S-07 layout. A table from an older
/// build has no `workspace` column: it is renamed to `approvals_unscoped`
/// and never read again, so approvals saved before this change no longer
/// apply anywhere (the user is simply asked again).
fn migrate_approvals(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {
    let has_workspace_column = {
        let mut stmt = conn.prepare("PRAGMA table_info(approvals)")?;
        let names = stmt
            .query_map([], |r| r.get::<_, String>(1))?
            .collect::<std::result::Result<Vec<String>, _>>()?;
        // No rows means the table does not exist yet.
        names.is_empty() || names.iter().any(|n| n == "workspace")
    };
    if !has_workspace_column {
        conn.execute_batch(
            "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS approvals_unscoped;
             ALTER TABLE approvals RENAME TO approvals_unscoped;",
        )?;
    }
    conn.execute_batch(APPROVALS_SCHEMA)?;
    Ok(())
}

/// The key "always allow" approvals are stored under: the workspace's
/// canonical path (symlinks and `..` resolved; lower-case on Windows), so
/// two spellings of one folder share their approvals.
pub fn workspace_key(workspace: &Path) -> String {
    let p = std::fs::canonicalize(workspace).unwrap_or_else(|_| workspace.to_path_buf());
    let s = p.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    if cfg!(windows) {
        s.to_lowercase()
    } else {
        s
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// Remember an "always allow" answer for one workspace. `workspace` is
    /// [`workspace_key`] of the workspace. Saving the same approval twice
    /// keeps one row (UNIQUE constraint + INSERT OR IGNORE).
    pub fn add_approval(&self, workspace: &str, tool: &str, pattern: &str, scope: &str) -> Result<()> {
        self.conn.lock().unwrap().execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO approvals (id, workspace, tool, pattern, scope, created_at) \
             VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5,?6)",
            params![new_id("apr"), workspace, tool, pattern, scope, now_ms()],
        )?;
        Ok(())

    /// True when this workspace has an "always allow" for (tool, pattern).

    pub fn has_approval(&self, workspace: &str, tool: &str, pattern: &str) -> Result<bool> {

        let n: i64 = conn.query_row(
```

### S-08 · Bash permission rules must check every part of a chained command

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none (if S-04 is applied too, apply S-04 first; both edit `fn evaluate` but different lines) |
| Files to change | `src/permissions.rs` |
| Read first | `src/permissions.rs`: `fn evaluate`, `fn glob_match`; `src/tools.rs`: the `bash` branch (it runs `sh -c` on Unix and `cmd /C` on Windows) |

#### What is wrong

For `bash`, the rule pattern is matched against the whole command line, and
`*` in a pattern matches every character, including `;`, `&&` and `|`. An
allow rule `git *` therefore also allows `git log && <anything>`. A deny rule
`rm *` does not see `cd build && rm -rf x`, because that line starts with
`cd`. The engine never looks at the separate commands inside one line.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/permissions.rs`:
```rust

        &self,
        tool: &str,
        detail: &str,
        remembered: impl Fn(&str, &str) -> bool,

```

```rust
/// Minimal glob: `*` matches any run of chars (incl. `/` for simplicity), `?` one char.
/// Anchored full-string match. Good enough for commands/paths; not a regex.
pub fn glob_match(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
```

#### Why it matters

People write allow rules for harmless commands (`git *`, `cargo test*`).
Today every such rule also allows whatever the model appends after `&&` or
`|`, without a prompt.

#### Steps

The new behaviour for `bash` only (other tools are unchanged):

- The command line is split into parts at the shell's control operators,
  outside quotes. Unix (`sh`): `;` `&&` `||` `|` `|&` `&` and newlines.
  Windows (`cmd`): `&` `&&` `||` `|` and newlines (`cmd` has no `;`
  separator and no single quotes; `^` escapes).
- Every part is checked with the rules and defaults. Any part denied → the
  whole command is denied. Every part allowed → allowed. Otherwise → ask.
- Syntax the splitter does not follow → ask (a `deny` rule on the whole line
  still denies): `$(...)`, backticks, `( )`, `{ }`, here-documents (`<<`),
  loops and `if`, `cmd` variables (`%VAR%`), unbalanced quotes.
- A part that sends output into a file (`> f`, `>> f`, `&> f`) asks even if a
  rule allows the command; `> /dev/null`, `> NUL` and `2>&1` do not count.
- In all "ask" cases, an earlier "always allow" for this exact full command
  still allows it. Users who want no prompts at all use Turbo mode.

```rust
/// The shell that runs `bash` tool commands: `sh -c` on Unix, `cmd /C` on
/// Windows (see `tools.rs`). They split command lines differently.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Shell {
    Posix,
    Cmd,
}

impl Shell {
    /// The shell the `bash` tool uses on this machine.
    pub fn current() -> Self {
        if cfg!(windows) {
            Shell::Cmd
        } else {
            Shell::Posix
        }
    }
}

/// One simple command cut out of a command line.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CommandPart {
    /// The command as typed (trimmed, quotes kept).
    pub text: String,
    /// It sends output into a file (`> f`, `>> f`, `&> f`).
    pub writes_file: bool,
}

/// Words that start compound commands (loops, `if`, negation): their parts
/// cannot be judged one by one, so the whole line asks.
const POSIX_KEYWORDS: &[&str] = &[
    "if", "then", "elif", "else", "fi", "case", "esac", "for", "select", "while", "until",
    "do", "done", "function", "time", "coproc", "!",
];
const CMD_KEYWORDS: &[&str] = &["if", "for"];

/// Split a command line at the shell's control operators, ignoring
/// operators inside quotes. `None` means the line uses syntax this splitter
/// does not follow (command substitution, groups, here-documents, loops,
/// `cmd` variables, unbalanced quotes): the caller must ask.
pub fn split_command(line: &str, shell: Shell) -> Option<Vec<CommandPart>> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = line.chars().collect();
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    let mut writes = false;
    let mut quote: Option<char> = None;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        let c = chars[i];
        let next = chars.get(i + 1).copied();
        if let Some(q) = quote {
            cur.push(c);
            if c == q {
                quote = None;
            } else if q == '"' && shell == Shell::Posix {
                match c {
                    '\\' => {
                        if let Some(n) = next {
                            cur.push(n);
                            i += 1;
                        }
                    }
                    '`' => return None,
                    '$' if next == Some('(') => return None,
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        match (shell, c) {
            (_, '"') | (Shell::Posix, '\'') => {
                quote = Some(c);
                cur.push(c);
            }
            (Shell::Posix, '\\') | (Shell::Cmd, '^') => {
                // Escape: the next character is literal. A trailing escape
                // continues the line, which we do not follow.
                let n = next?;
                cur.push(c);
                cur.push(n);
                i += 1;
            }
            (_, '(') | (_, ')') => return None,
            (Shell::Posix, '`') | (Shell::Posix, '{') | (Shell::Posix, '}') => return None,
            (Shell::Cmd, '%') => return None,
            (Shell::Posix, '$') if matches!(next, Some('(') | Some('\'')) => return None,
            (_, '<') if next == Some('<') => return None,
            (Shell::Posix, ';') | (_, '\n') | (_, '\r') => end_part(&mut parts, &mut cur, &mut writes),
            (_, '&') => {
                let prev = cur.chars().last();
                if next == Some('&') {
                    end_part(&mut parts, &mut cur, &mut writes);
                    i += 1;
                } else if matches!(prev, Some('>') | Some('<')) || next == Some('>') {
                    cur.push(c); // part of a redirection: `2>&1`, `<&3`, `&> file`
                } else {
                    end_part(&mut parts, &mut cur, &mut writes); // background, or cmd's `&`
                }
            }
            (_, '|') => {
                end_part(&mut parts, &mut cur, &mut writes);
                if next == Some('|') || (shell == Shell::Posix && next == Some('&')) {
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            (_, '>') => {
                if shell == Shell::Posix && next == Some('|') {
                    return None; // `>|` (force overwrite) is rare: ask
                }
                cur.push(c);
                if next == Some('>') {
                    cur.push('>');
                    i += 1;
                }
                if !redirect_is_harmless(&chars, i + 1, shell) {
                    writes = true;
                }
            }
            _ => cur.push(c),
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    if quote.is_some() {
        return None;
    }
    end_part(&mut parts, &mut cur, &mut writes);
    let keywords = match shell {
        Shell::Posix => POSIX_KEYWORDS,
        Shell::Cmd => CMD_KEYWORDS,
    };
    for p in &parts {
        let first = p.text.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_ascii_lowercase();
        if keywords.contains(&first.as_str()) {
            return None;
        }
    }
    Some(parts)
}

/// Finish the current part (empty parts are dropped).
fn end_part(parts: &mut Vec<CommandPart>, cur: &mut String, writes: &mut bool) {
    let text = cur.trim();
    if !text.is_empty() {
        parts.push(CommandPart { text: text.to_string(), writes_file: *writes });
    }
    cur.clear();
    *writes = false;
}

/// Called right after `>` or `>>`: true when nothing on disk is written,
/// i.e. the output goes to a descriptor (`>&2`) or to the null device.
fn redirect_is_harmless(chars: &[char], mut j: usize, shell: Shell) -> bool {
    if chars.get(j) == Some(&'&') {
        return matches!(chars.get(j + 1), Some(d) if d.is_ascii_digit() || *d == '-');
    }
    while chars.get(j).is_some_and(|c| *c == ' ' || *c == '\t') {
        j += 1;
    }
    let target: String = chars[j.min(chars.len())..]
        .iter()
        .take_while(|c| !c.is_whitespace() && !matches!(c, ';' | '&' | '|' | '<' | '>'))
        .collect();
    match shell {
        Shell::Posix => target == "/dev/null",
        Shell::Cmd => target.eq_ignore_ascii_case("nul"),
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// Evaluate for (tool, detail) where detail is the command for bash,
    /// the (workspace-relative) path for file tools, the url for webfetch.
    /// `remembered` = "always allow" approvals from the DB.
    ///
    /// For `bash`, a chained command (`a && b | c`) is split into its parts
    /// and every part must pass: a denied part denies the whole command, a
    /// part that is not allowed makes it ask. Syntax the splitter cannot
    /// follow, and output redirected into a file, also ask unless the user
    /// approved this exact command before.
    pub fn evaluate(
        &self,
        tool: &str,
        detail: &str,
        remembered: impl Fn(&str, &str) -> bool,
    ) -> Decision {
        if tool != "bash" {
            return self.evaluate_single(tool, detail, &remembered);
        }
        let ask_whole = Decision { action: Action::Ask, key: format!("{tool}:{detail}") };
        let allow_whole = Decision { action: Action::Allow, key: format!("{tool}:{detail}") };
        let Some(parts) = split_command(detail, Shell::current()) else {
            // We cannot see every command inside: a deny rule on the whole
            // line still wins; otherwise ask (an exact earlier approval allows).
            let whole = self.evaluate_single(tool, detail, &remembered);
            if whole.action == Action::Deny {
                return whole;
            }
            return if remembered(tool, detail) { allow_whole } else { ask_whole };
        };
        if parts.len() <= 1 {
            let d = self.evaluate_single(tool, detail, &remembered);
            let writes = parts.first().is_some_and(|p| p.writes_file);
            if d.action == Action::Allow && writes && !remembered(tool, detail) {
                return ask_whole;
            }
            return d;
        }
        let mut all_allowed = true;
        for p in &parts {
            let d = self.evaluate_single(tool, &p.text, &remembered);
            match d.action {
                Action::Deny => return d,
                Action::Allow if !p.writes_file => {}
                _ => all_allowed = false,
            }
        }
        if all_allowed || remembered(tool, detail) {
            allow_whole
        } else {
            ask_whole
        }
    }

    /// One detail against the rules, then the defaults (the old `evaluate`).
    fn evaluate_single(
        &self,
        tool: &str,
        detail: &str,
```

### S-09 · Deterministic permission defaults, merged with built-ins, invalid actions rejected

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none (S-04 and S-08 also edit `src/permissions.rs`, but other lines; any order works) |
| Files to change | `src/permissions.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `config.example.toml` |
| Read first | `src/permissions.rs`: `impl Action`, `Engine::new`; `src/config.rs`: `struct PermissionsCfg`, `impl Default for PermissionsCfg`, `Config::load` |

#### What is wrong

Three problems in how permission settings are read:

1. `Engine::new` copies the `defaults` map (a `HashMap`, whose order is
   random) into a list, and `evaluate` takes the first entry whose name
   matches. With a wildcard default such as `"*" = "allow"` next to
   `bash = "ask"`, the answer for `bash` changes from run to run.
2. If the config file has a `[permissions.defaults]` table, it **replaces**
   the built-in list. Every tool the user did not list loses its default.
3. An action word that is not exactly `allow`, `ask` or `deny` (for example
   `"Deny"` or `"denny"`) is silently skipped. A mistyped `deny` rule then
   falls through to the next rule or to the default, which for `read`,
   `list`, `glob` and `grep` is `allow`.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/permissions.rs`:
```rust
impl Engine {
    pub fn new(cfg: &PermissionsCfg) -> Self {
        let mut defaults = Vec::new();
        for (tool, action) in &cfg.defaults {
            if let Some(a) = Action::parse(action) {
                defaults.push((tool.clone(), a));
            }
        }
        Self { defaults, rules: cfg.rules.clone() }
    }
```

Find this code in `src/config.rs`:
```rust
pub struct PermissionsCfg {
    /// Per-tool default action when no rule matches: "allow" | "ask" | "deny".
    pub defaults: HashMap<String, String>,
```

#### Why it matters

A typo in one word of a `deny` rule turns that rule off without any message,
and a wildcard default can allow `bash` on one start and ask on the next.
Safety settings must behave the same every time and must fail loudly when
they are wrong.

#### Steps

New behaviour:
- Exact tool names always beat wildcard defaults; among wildcards the one
  with more literal characters wins; ties are broken by name.
- A user's `[permissions.defaults]` is merged on top of the built-in
  defaults. To change a built-in, list that tool with the new action. (A
  user `"*" = "deny"` now means "every tool not named anywhere", because the
  built-in names are exact and win.)
- Action words ignore letter case and surrounding spaces. Anything else
  stops `Config::load` with an error that names every bad entry. If such a
  word still reaches the engine (a config built in code), it becomes `ask`.

```rust
    /// "allow" | "ask" | "deny" — letter case and surrounding spaces do not
    /// matter. Anything else is `None`.
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "allow" => Some(Action::Allow),
            "ask" => Some(Action::Ask),
            "deny" => Some(Action::Deny),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The canonical config word for this action.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Action::Allow => "allow",
            Action::Ask => "ask",
```

```rust
/// Sort key for default entries: (exact name?, number of literal characters).
fn default_specificity(pattern: &str) -> (bool, usize) {
    let literal = pattern.chars().filter(|c| *c != '*' && *c != '?').count();
    (literal == pattern.chars().count(), literal)
}

impl Engine {
    pub fn new(cfg: &PermissionsCfg) -> Self {
        // An unknown action word never drops a default or a rule silently:
        // it becomes "ask". (`Config::load` already rejects such configs.)
        let mut defaults: Vec<(String, Action)> = cfg
            .defaults
            .iter()
            .map(|(tool, action)| (tool.clone(), Action::parse(action).unwrap_or(Action::Ask)))
            .collect();
        // `cfg.defaults` is a HashMap, whose order changes from run to run.
        // Sort so the most specific entry is found first: exact tool names,
        // then patterns with more literal characters, then by name.
        defaults.sort_by(|(a, _), (b, _)| {
            default_specificity(b).cmp(&default_specificity(a)).then_with(|| a.cmp(b))
        });
        let rules = cfg
            .rules
            .iter()
            .map(|r| RuleCfg {
                tool: r.tool.clone(),
                pattern: r.pattern.clone(),
                action: Action::parse(&r.action).unwrap_or(Action::Ask).as_str().to_string(),
            })
            .collect();
        Self { defaults, rules }
    }
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// The defaults every config starts from (the list in
/// `impl Default for PermissionsCfg`). A user's `[permissions.defaults]`
/// table is merged on top of this list; it does not replace it.
pub fn builtin_permission_defaults() -> HashMap<String, String> {
    PermissionsCfg::default().defaults
}

/// serde helper for `PermissionsCfg::defaults`: user entries on top of the
/// built-in ones.
fn merge_with_builtin_defaults<'de, D>(d: D) -> std::result::Result<HashMap<String, String>, D::Error>
where
    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
{
    let user = HashMap::<String, String>::deserialize(d)?;
    let mut merged = builtin_permission_defaults();
    merged.extend(user);
    Ok(merged)
}

impl PermissionsCfg {
    /// Every action word must be "allow", "ask" or "deny" (any letter case).
    /// The error lists every bad entry at once.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let ok = |s: &str| matches!(s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(), "allow" | "ask" | "deny");
        let mut bad = Vec::new();
        let mut names: Vec<&String> = self.defaults.keys().collect();
        names.sort();
        for tool in names {
            let action = &self.defaults[tool];
            if !ok(action) {
                bad.push(format!("permissions.defaults.{tool} = {action:?}"));
            }
        }
        for (i, r) in self.rules.iter().enumerate() {
            if !ok(&r.action) {
                bad.push(format!(
                    "permissions.rules[{i}].action = {:?} (tool {:?}, pattern {:?})",
                    r.action, r.tool, r.pattern
                ));
            }
        }
        if bad.is_empty() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "invalid permission action (use \"allow\", \"ask\" or \"deny\"): {}",
                bad.join("; ")
            )
        }
    }
}

    pub tool: String,
```
