### S-10 · GUI `is_local_url`: parse URLs properly (userinfo etc.)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: `fn is_local_url`, `fn normalize_url`, test `local_url_detection_covers_dev_servers` |

#### What is wrong

`is_local_url` decides if a URL stays on this machine. It is used for the
dev-server-only mode (`[browser] allow_remote = false`). It finds the host by
cutting the text at the first `/`, `:`, `?` or `#`. A URL can carry a user name
and password in front of the host (`http://name:password@host/`). For such a URL
the code reads the user name as the host. So some URLs that point to a remote
server are treated as local, and the dev-server-only mode lets them through.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
    // IPv6 literals contain colons, so they cannot go through `split(':')`.
    if rest.starts_with("[::1]") {
        return true;
    }
    let host = rest.split(['/', ':', '?', '#']).next().unwrap_or("");
    matches!(host, "localhost" | "127.0.0.1" | "0.0.0.0")
```

#### Why it matters

A user who set `allow_remote = false` expects the preview panel to load only
their own dev servers. Today a wrongly shaped URL (typed, pasted, or chosen by
the agent with `browser_navigate`) can open a remote site anyway.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/gui.rs`. Find the function `is_local_url` (around line 576).
   Replace the whole function. The new version parses the URL with the same
   rules a browser uses. The `url` crate does this, and `reqwest` already
   re-exports it as `reqwest::Url`, so no new dependency is needed.

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
/// True for URLs that stay on this machine. Used to enforce the
/// dev-server-only mode (`[browser] allow_remote = false`).
pub fn is_local_url(url: &str) -> bool {
    let u = url.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if u == "about:blank" {
        return true;
    }
    let Some(rest) = ["http://", "https://"]
        .iter()
        .find_map(|scheme| u.strip_prefix(scheme))
    else {
        return false;
    };
    // IPv6 literals contain colons, so they cannot go through `split(':')`.
    if rest.starts_with("[::1]") {
        return true;
    }
    let host = rest.split(['/', ':', '?', '#']).next().unwrap_or("");
    matches!(host, "localhost" | "127.0.0.1" | "0.0.0.0")
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// True for URLs that stay on this machine. Used to enforce the
/// dev-server-only mode (`[browser] allow_remote = false`).
///
/// The URL is parsed with the same rules a browser uses (the `url` crate,
/// re-exported by `reqwest`), so the host we check is the host the preview
/// really connects to. Cutting the text by hand got forms like
/// `http://name:password@host/` wrong.
pub fn is_local_url(url: &str) -> bool {
    let url = url.trim();
    if url.eq_ignore_ascii_case("about:blank") {
        return true;
    }
    let Ok(parsed) = reqwest::Url::parse(url) else {
        return false;
    };
    if !matches!(parsed.scheme(), "http" | "https") {
        return false;
    }
    match parsed.host_str() {
        // The parser lower-cases host names, so `LOCALHOST` arrives here too.
        Some("localhost") => true,
        // IP addresses: any loopback address (127.0.0.0/8 or ::1), or the
        // "all interfaces" address 0.0.0.0 that dev servers often print.
        // `host_str()` keeps the brackets around IPv6, so strip them first.
        Some(host) => host
            .trim_start_matches('[')
            .trim_end_matches(']')
            .parse::<std::net::IpAddr>()
            .map(|ip| ip.is_loopback() || ip.is_unspecified())
            .unwrap_or(false),
        None => false,
    }
}
```

2. Nothing else changes. Every caller (`Browse`, `browser_navigate`) keeps calling
   `is_local_url(&url)` with the same signature.

/// New (S-11): the one rule for every page the preview panel opens — typed
/// URLs, the agent's `browser_navigate`, the dev-server button, links,
/// redirects and back/forward. `Err` carries the message the panel shows.
pub fn check_navigation(url: &str, allow_remote: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
    if !is_allowed_scheme(url) {
        return Err(format!("Blocked: `{url}` — the panel only loads http(s) pages."));
    }
    if !allow_remote && !is_local_url(url) {
        return Err(format!(
            "`{url}` is blocked: this panel is dev-server-only ([browser] allow_remote = false)."
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

### S-12 · GUI preview bridge: unguessable request ids, bounded queue

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none (B-36 also edits `struct Bridge`, but other lines; either order works) |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: `struct Bridge`, `Bridge::start`, `Bridge::on_eval`, the preview `with_ipc_handler` in `fn run`; `src/browser.rs`: `fn eval_wrapper`, `fn parse_reply` |

#### What is wrong

The agent's browser tools (`browser_snapshot`, `browser_click`, …) send a request
to the preview page and wait for a reply frame `{hab: <id>, ok, result}` on the
preview's IPC channel. Three weaknesses:

- request ids count up from 1, so any page can guess the id of a waiting request;
- every page in the preview can post frames, and each frame is copied into an
  unbounded channel, even when no request is waiting;
- frames have no size limit.

So a page can answer the agent's request with made-up data, or flood the event
loop with messages.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
            .with_ipc_handler(move |req: wry::http::Request<String>| {
                let _ = eval_tx.send(UiMsg::Browser(BrowserEvt::Eval(req.body().clone())));
                let _ = eval_proxy.send_event(AppEvent::Wake);
            })
```

#### Why it matters

The agent trusts what `browser_snapshot` returns. A page that guesses the id can
put words in the agent's mouth before the real reply arrives.

#### Steps

1. Replace the counter in `struct Bridge` and add the helpers above it. Ids go
   through JavaScript as plain numbers, which are exact only up to 2^53, so the
   random id is cut to 53 bits.

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:

///

/// destroyed view) fails the tool instead of freezing the run.
struct Bridge {
    next_id: u64,
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (S-12): ids of bridge requests still waiting for a page reply. The
/// preview's IPC handler reads it to drop frames nobody asked for.
type PendingIds = Arc<std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::HashSet<u64>>>;

/// New (S-12): biggest reply frame we accept from the preview page. A
/// snapshot is capped far below this by the page runtime.
const MAX_EVAL_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 1 << 20;

/// New (S-12): a request id the page cannot guess.
///
/// Ids travel through JavaScript as plain numbers, which are exact only up
/// to 2^53, so the id is kept below that. `RandomState` is seeded randomly
/// for each process; hashing a counter and the clock with it is enough for
/// a local, short-lived token (it is not a cryptographic secret).
fn unguessable_id(counter: u64) -> u64 {
    use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};
    let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new().build_hasher();
    h.write_u64(counter);
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    h.write_u128(nanos);
    (h.finish() & ((1u64 << 53) - 1)).max(1)
}

/// Goal B: requests from agent tools that are waiting on this webview.

/// Every request has a deadline; a page that never answers (a hung script, a
/// destroyed view) fails the tool instead of freezing the run.

    counter: u64,

            .with_ipc_handler(move |req: wry::http::Request<String>| {
                // S-12: only a reply to a request we are waiting for may pass,
                // each id at most once, and never an oversized frame.
                let body = req.body();
                if body.len() > MAX_EVAL_FRAME_BYTES {
                    return;
                }
                let Some((id, _)) = crate::browser::parse_reply(body) else {
                    return;
                };
                let expected = eval_ids.lock().map(|mut set| set.remove(&id)).unwrap_or(false);
                if !expected {
                    return;

                let _ = eval_proxy.send_event(AppEvent::Wake);
            })
```

### S-13 · Browser snapshot must not return password, one-time-code or card values

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |

#### What is wrong

`browser_snapshot` runs a small JavaScript runtime in the preview page. For
every input it reports `value`, so the content of a password field goes
straight into the model's context. The helper `nm` (the element's name) is
worse: for an input without `aria-label` it falls back to `el.value`, so the
password also shows up as the element's *name*, both in the snapshot and in
the reply to `browser_click`. One-time codes and credit card numbers are
handled the same way.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
  function nm(el) {
    var v = el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.innerText || el.value || el.getAttribute('placeholder') || el.getAttribute('title') || el.tagName;
    return String(v).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 90);
  }
```

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
        var n = { ref: id, role: role(el), name: nm(el) };
        if (el.value) n.value = String(el.value).slice(0, 80);
        if (el.tagName === 'A' && el.href) n.href = String(el.href).slice(0, 140);
```

#### Why it matters

Snapshots are sent to the model provider and stored in the session database.
A password typed into a local login page would end up in both, in plain text.

#### Steps

The rule: a field is *secret* when its `type` is `password`, or its
`autocomplete` attribute says `current-password`, `new-password`,
`one-time-code` or any `cc-...` (payment card) value. A secret field never
reports its value. The snapshot shows `"value": "[hidden]"` so the model still
knows the field is filled.

1. Open `src/browser.rs` and find `RUNTIME_JS` (around line 190). Add the
   new helper `secret` and make `nm` skip secret values.

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
  function nm(el) {
    var v = el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.innerText || el.value || el.getAttribute('placeholder') || el.getAttribute('title') || el.tagName;
    return String(v).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 90);
  }
```

Replace it with:
```js
  // Password, one-time-code and payment card fields: their values never
  // leave the page (not in a snapshot, not in a click reply).
  function secret(el) {
    if (String(el.type || '').toLowerCase() === 'password') return true;
    var ac = String(el.getAttribute('autocomplete') || '').toLowerCase();
    return /(^|\s)(current-password|new-password|one-time-code|cc-[a-z-]+)(\s|$)/.test(ac);
  }
  function nm(el) {
    var val = secret(el) ? '' : el.value;
    var v = el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.innerText || val || el.getAttribute('placeholder') || el.getAttribute('title') || el.tagName;
    return String(v).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 90);
  }
```

### S-14 · gitsnap: validate stored paths, never follow symlinks, literal pathspecs

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/gitsnap.rs` |
| Read first | `src/gitsnap.rs`: `struct Manifest`, `fn take_snapshot`, `fn load_manifest`, `fn restore_manifest`, `fn read_stack` |

#### What is wrong

`/undo` restores files from a snapshot folder. Several things are unsafe:

1. `restore_manifest` trusts every path in `manifest.json` and every id in
   `undo.json`. These are plain files on disk (and can sit inside the
   workspace). A path like `../x` or an absolute path is joined to the
   workspace and written or deleted.
2. Snapshots read files with `fs::read` and restores write with `fs::copy`.
   Both follow symlinks, so a link inside the workspace makes undo read or
   overwrite a file outside it.
3. Part `// 3)` runs `git checkout -- <path>` with the path relative to the
   **repository root**, but in the **workspace** folder. When the workspace
   is a subfolder of the repo, git answers "pathspec did not match" and the
   file is silently not restored.
4. git treats `*`, `?` and `[...]` in a pathspec as wildcards: restoring
   `s[1].txt` also reverts `s1.txt`.
5. Every failure in parts `// 2)` and `// 3)` is ignored with `let _ =`, so `/undo`
   reports success when it did not restore.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gitsnap.rs`:
```rust
        } else {
            // Tracked file the run modified: scoped checkout to index/HEAD
            // content == its clean-at-snapshot content. Explicit path only,
            // repo-root-relative (that's what git expects).
            let _ = git(workspace, &["checkout", "--", &e.root_rel]);
        }
```

#### Why it matters

Undo exists to repair damage. If it can write outside the workspace, or
quietly leaves files changed, it causes new damage and hides it.

#### Steps

The new rules: every stored path must be a plain relative path (only normal
names, no `.`, `..`, root or drive). Snapshot ids must look like the ones
`next_snap_id` makes. Undo never reads, writes or deletes **through** a
symlink or a symlinked folder: a symlink itself may be removed (that never
touches its target). Dirty symlinks are recorded in a new manifest list
`links` and left alone. git runs in the repo root with
`--literal-pathspecs`. Problems are collected and returned as an error after
everything else was restored.

/// `rel` as a safe workspace-relative path: not empty, and made only of
/// normal names (no `.`, `..`, root or drive parts). Manifests and stacks
/// are files on disk, so anything else in them is refused.
fn checked_rel(rel: &str) -> Option<&Path> {
    let p = Path::new(rel);
    let ok = !rel.is_empty()
        && p.components().all(|c| matches!(c, std::path::Component::Normal(_)));
    ok.then_some(p)
}

/// True when `rel` passes through a symlinked folder inside the workspace.
/// Undo never reads or writes through one.
fn under_symlinked_dir(workspace: &Path, rel: &str) -> bool {
    let mut cur = workspace.to_path_buf();
    let parts: Vec<_> = Path::new(rel).components().collect();
    for c in parts.iter().take(parts.len().saturating_sub(1)) {
        cur.push(c.as_os_str());
        if std::fs::symlink_metadata(&cur).is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink()) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    false
}

/// Snapshot ids come from `next_snap_id` (`s<millis>_<hex>`). A stack file
/// that names anything else was not written by us.
fn valid_snap_id(id: &str) -> bool {
    id.len() <= 64 && id.starts_with('s') && id.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')
}

```rust
fn load_manifest(root: &Path, id: &str) -> Result<Manifest> {
    if !valid_snap_id(id) {
        return Err(anyhow!("refusing snapshot id {id:?}: not written by opencode-rust"));
    }
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join(id).join("manifest.json"))
        .with_context(|| format!("snapshot {id} manifest"))?;
    let m: Manifest = serde_json::from_str(&text)?;
    if m.id != id {
        return Err(anyhow!("snapshot {id}: manifest names a different id ({})", m.id));
    }
    // A manifest is a file on disk: check every path before trusting it.
    for p in m.present.iter().chain(&m.absent).chain(&m.links) {
        if checked_rel(p).is_none() {
            return Err(anyhow!("snapshot {id}: refusing unsafe path {p:?} in manifest"));
        }
    }
    Ok(m)
}

Replace it with:
```rust
    // 3) Dirty now but clean at snapshot time → the run changed it.
    let snapshot_set: std::collections::HashSet<String> =
        m.present.iter().chain(&m.absent).chain(&m.links).cloned().collect();
    let repo = repo_root(workspace);
    for e in dirty_entries(workspace, state_dir)? {
        if snapshot_set.contains(&e.rel) || under_symlinked_dir(workspace, &e.rel) {
            continue;
        }
        if e.kind == "??" {
            // File (or symlink) the run created: remove it. Removing a
            // symlink removes the link only.
            let file_or_link = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&e.abs)
                .is_ok_and(|md| md.is_file() || md.file_type().is_symlink());
            if file_or_link {
                if let Err(err) = std::fs::remove_file(&e.abs) {
                    problems.push(format!("{}: cannot remove: {err}", e.rel));
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Tracked file the run modified: check out its index/HEAD
            // content (= its clean-at-snapshot content). `root_rel` is
            // relative to the repo root, so git must run there; literal
            // pathspecs keep `[`, `*` and `?` in names from matching others.
            if let Err(err) = git(&repo, &["--literal-pathspecs", "checkout", "--", &e.root_rel]) {
                problems.push(format!("{}: {err}", e.rel));
            }
        }
    }
    if problems.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(anyhow!(
            "undo restored what it could, but {} path(s) need a look:\n  {}",
            problems.len(),
            problems.join("\n  ")
        ))
    }
}

### S-15 · Inline `/edit`: obey permission rules, refuse symlink escapes, no headless auto-apply

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |

| Depends on | S-02, S-03 |

#### What is wrong

`/edit` reads a file, sends it to the model and rewrites it, but it never asks the permission engine (`src/permissions.rs`). A `deny` rule such as "never edit `.env`" stops the agent's own `edit` tool, but not `/edit`. `resolve_in_workspace` only checks the typed text: a symlink inside the workspace that points outside it is followed. In headless mode (`--headless "/edit …"`), the edit is written at once, with no preview step anyone can answer.

#### Where it is

```rust

A user who denied edits to `.env` or `.git/*` can still have them rewritten (and their content sent to the model) through `/edit`. A symlink can lead `/edit` to a file outside the project. A script that runs `--headless "/edit …"` changes files without anyone seeing the diff.

/// S-15: `/edit` obeys the permission rules like the agent's own tools. A
/// `deny` rule for `read` (the file goes to the model) or `edit` (the file
/// is rewritten) on this path stops it before anything is read. `ask`
/// needs no extra prompt: the diff preview is the question.
pub fn check_edit_allowed(st: &Shared, path: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let detail = crate::permissions::normalize_path_detail(&st.workspace, path);
    for tool in ["read", "edit"] {
        let decision = st.engine.evaluate(tool, &detail, |_, _| false);
        if decision.action == crate::permissions::Action::Deny {

### S-16 · `/export`: stay inside the workspace, no silent overwrite

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn transcript_markdown`; `src/main.rs`: `Cmd::Export` in `fn headless_run`, `tui::InputAction::Export` in `fn tui_run` |

#### What is wrong

`/export [path]` writes the session transcript as markdown, in two places: the headless branch `Cmd::Export` and the TUI branch `tui::InputAction::Export`. Both accept any path. An absolute path is used as it is, and `..` can leave the workspace. Both use `std::fs::write`, which replaces an existing file without asking. So `/export ../../.bashrc` or `/export src/main.rs` silently destroys that file.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust
                        let path = match &arg {
                            Some(p) => {
                                let p = std::path::PathBuf::from(p);
                                if p.is_absolute() { p } else { st.workspace.join(p) }
```

#### Why it matters

One typo in a path wipes a source file or a config file. The transcript can also contain secrets (tool outputs), so it should not land in arbitrary folders.

#### Steps

New rules. The path must be inside the workspace (no `..`; an absolute path must start with the workspace). An existing file is replaced only if it is an earlier export (its first line is a marker) or the user typed `/export --force <path>`. Folders in the path are created. The check is done on the text of the path; a symbolic link inside the workspace is not followed. That is fine here, because you type the export path yourself.

    /// New (S-16): first line of every exported transcript. `/export` only
    /// replaces an existing file that starts with it (or with `--force`).
    pub const EXPORT_MARKER: &'static str = "<!-- opencode-rust transcript export -->";

    /// New (S-16): `/export [--force] [path]`: write the transcript as
    /// markdown INSIDE the workspace and return the file written. Refuses
    /// paths that leave the workspace, and refuses to replace a file that is
    /// not an earlier export unless `--force` is given.
    pub fn export_transcript(&self, session_id: &str, arg: Option<&str>) -> Result<PathBuf> {
        let mut raw = arg.unwrap_or("").trim();
        let mut force = false;
        if let Some(rest) = raw.strip_prefix("--force") {
            if rest.is_empty() || rest.starts_with(char::is_whitespace) {
                force = true;
                raw = rest.trim();
            }
        }
        let name = if raw.is_empty() {
            format!("opencode-rust-transcript-{session_id}.md")
        } else {
            raw.to_string()
        };
        let path = Self::export_path(&self.workspace, &name)?;
        if path.exists() && !force {
            let existing = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
            if !existing.starts_with(Self::EXPORT_MARKER) {
                anyhow::bail!(
                    "{} already exists and is not an earlier export; pick another name or use /export --force {name}",
                    path.display()
                );
            }
        }
        if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).with_context(|| format!("creating {}", dir.display()))?;
        }
        let md = format!("{}\n{}", Self::EXPORT_MARKER, self.transcript_markdown(session_id));
        std::fs::write(&path, md).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", path.display()))?;
        Ok(path)
    }

    /// New (S-16): `raw` as a path inside `workspace`, checked on the text
    /// only: no `..`, and an absolute path must start with the workspace.
    fn export_path(workspace: &std::path::Path, raw: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
        use std::path::Component;
        let p = std::path::Path::new(raw);
        let rel = if p.is_absolute() {
            p.strip_prefix(workspace)
                .map_err(|_| {
                    anyhow::anyhow!(
                        "export path must be inside the workspace ({}); use a relative path",
                        workspace.display()
                    )
                })?
                .to_path_buf()
        } else {
            p.to_path_buf()
        };
        let mut clean = PathBuf::new();
        for part in rel.components() {
            match part {
                Component::Normal(x) => clean.push(x),
                Component::CurDir => {}
                _ => anyhow::bail!("export path must stay inside the workspace (no `..`): {raw}"),
            }
        }
        if clean.as_os_str().is_empty() {
            anyhow::bail!("export path is empty");
        }
        Ok(workspace.join(clean))
    }

#### What is wrong

`/skill install <file-or-url>` reads a Markdown skill, asks the model for a
verdict, and then "bakes" the skill into every future system prompt.

1. The downloaded text is pasted into the vetting prompt with no marking, so

2. The verdict check is `starts_with("WORTHY")`: an answer like

3. A local source is `workspace.join(source)`, so `../` or an absolute path
   reads any file on the machine and sends it to the model provider.
4. A URL is fetched with the `webfetch` tool directly, skipping the
   permission engine, so a `deny` rule for `webfetch` does not apply.
5. `name` and `description` are written into the skill file's frontmatter

const SKILL_FENCE_START: &str = "<untrusted_skill>";
const SKILL_FENCE_END: &str = "</untrusted_skill>";

/// The user message for the vetting call: the skill text fenced as data.
/// Fence markers inside the text are neutralised, so it cannot end the
/// fence early.
fn skill_vetting_input(doc: &crate::skills::Doc) -> String {
    let text = format!(
        "Skill name: {}\nDescription: {}\n\nBody:\n{}",
        doc.name, doc.description, doc.body
    )
    .replace(SKILL_FENCE_START, "[fence removed]")
    .replace(SKILL_FENCE_END, "[fence removed]");
    format!("{SKILL_FENCE_START}\n{text}\n{SKILL_FENCE_END}")
}

/// The vetting verdict: `Some(true)` = WORTHY, `Some(false)` = SKIP, `None`
/// when the first word is neither. Markdown around the word (`**WORTHY**`)
/// is ignored; `WORTHYISH` is not WORTHY.
fn parse_verdict(reply: &str) -> Option<bool> {
    let first_line = reply.lines().map(str::trim).find(|l| !l.is_empty())?;
    let word: String = first_line
        .trim_start_matches(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric())
        .chars()
        .take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric())
        .collect();
    match word.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str() {
        "WORTHY" => Some(true),
        "SKIP" => Some(false),
        _ => None,
    }
}

### S-18 · GUI hardening: devtools only in debug, CSP, no external fonts, lock main webview navigation, preview clipboard

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs`, `src/gui.html`, `tests/gui/run.sh`, `tests/gui/panel.js` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: the two `wry::WebViewBuilder::new()` calls in `fn run`; `src/gui.html`: `<head>`, `renderMarkdown`, `window.copyCode`, the "Starter Prompt Chips" part of `initApp` |

#### What is wrong

- DevTools are enabled in every build (`.with_devtools(true)`), including release.
- The app page has no Content Security Policy (CSP: a browser rule list that
  says which scripts and resources a page may load). The Copy button uses an
  inline `onclick="…"`, which a strict CSP forbids.
- The page loads fonts from Google on every start (needs network, tells Google
  each time the app starts).
- The main window has no navigation handler. It carries the privileged IPC verbs
  (approve, turbo, send, close); nothing stops it from being navigated away to
  another page.
- The preview webview uses `.with_clipboard(true)`. In wry 0.57 on Windows this
  answers every clipboard-READ permission request with "allow", for every page the
  panel opens (verified in `wry-0.57.0/src/webview2/mod.rs`, the `// Enable clipboard`
  block around line 511).

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
    let webview = wry::WebViewBuilder::new()
        .with_background_color((7, 10, 18, 255))
        .with_devtools(true)
```

#### Why it matters

Any web page opened in the preview can read whatever the user copied (API keys,
passwords) without a prompt. Without a CSP and a navigation lock, one HTML
injection bug in the app page would be enough to answer approvals or switch to
Turbo.

2. Add the two new functions used above, right before the doc comment of

/// Apply the panel's rect and visibility to the native child view.
///
/// Bounds go first: a view shown at a stale rect flashes a grey/white
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (S-18): may the main window go to `uri`? Only our own page: WebView2
/// reports the page loaded from a string as `about:blank` or as a
/// `data:text/html…` URI (the exact form depends on the runtime version).
/// Chromium itself refuses `data:` navigations started by page scripts.
fn main_window_may_navigate(uri: &str) -> bool {
    let u = uri.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    u == "about:blank" || u.starts_with("data:text/html")
}

/// New (S-18): navigation handler for the main window. The very first
/// navigation is always our own page (`with_html`), whatever URI the
/// runtime reports for it; after that only `main_window_may_navigate` URIs.
fn main_window_navigation_guard() -> impl Fn(String) -> bool + 'static {
    let first = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(true);
    move |uri: String| {
        if first.swap(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) || main_window_may_navigate(&uri) {
            return true;
        }
        eprintln!("[gui] blocked a navigation of the main window to {uri}");
        false
    }
}

/// Apply the panel's rect and visibility to the native child view.
///
/// Bounds go first: a view shown at a stale rect flashes a grey/white
```

<!-- TASK:S-19 -->
### S-19 · kaggle_setup_cell.py: no shell strings from remote data, token check in front of the tunnel

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none (B-08 makes the TUI's heartbeat send the token; until then its "api" indicator may show DOWN while chat works) |
| Files to change | `kaggle_setup_cell.py` |
| Read first | `kaggle_setup_cell.py` (whole file, 210 lines) |

#### What is wrong

The notebook cell starts Ollama on Kaggle and opens a public Cloudflare
"quick tunnel" to it. Problems:

1. The tunnel points straight at Ollama, which has no login. Anyone who
   learns the `*.trycloudflare.com` address can use the GPU and call every
   Ollama endpoint, including the ones that pull, create and delete models.
   The script even prints `OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY="none"`.
2. Commands are built as shell strings (`shell=True`). The download command
   contains a file name that comes from the Hugging Face listing, so an
   unexpected name (with `"` or `$(`) would be run by the shell. The same
   name is written into the Modelfile without checks.
3. `cloudflared` is downloaded from `releases/latest`, so every run may get a
   different, unverified binary. The model file's checksum is not checked.
4. The Hugging Face listing is not recursive and reads only the first page,
   so a GGUF in a subfolder is never found.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `kaggle_setup_cell.py`:
```python
            rc, log = sh(f'curl -fL {flag} --retry 5 --retry-all-errors '
                         f'--speed-limit 50000 --speed-time 60 '
                         f'-o "{part}" "{url}"', timeout=7200)
```

Find this code in `kaggle_setup_cell.py`:
```python
def tunnel_proc():
    return subprocess.Popen(
        f"{WORKDIR}/cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:{PORT} "
        f"--no-autoupdate >> {LOG} 2>&1", shell=True, env=env)
```

#### Why it matters

A public, unauthenticated model server is free GPU time for strangers and
lets them change what model you are talking to. A shell string built from
downloaded data is one bad file name away from running a command.

#### Steps

The new design: every program runs with a **list** of arguments (no shell).
A small token proxy (Python standard library only) listens on
`127.0.0.1:11435`. It forwards a request to Ollama only when the request
carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The tunnel points at the proxy, never
at Ollama. The token is random per run and is printed as
`OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY`; opencode-rust already sends `Authorization: Bearer
<key>` when the key is not empty (`src/provider.rs`). `cloudflared` is pinned
to version 2025.8.1 and checked by SHA-256. The GGUF is checked against the
SHA-256 that Hugging Face publishes.

**Stage 1 — no shell strings, checked downloads**

1. Imports.

Find this code in `kaggle_setup_cell.py`:
```python
import os, re, json, glob, time, shutil, subprocess, threading, urllib.request

# ---------- CONFIG ----------
```

Replace it with:
```python
import os, re, json, glob, time, shutil, subprocess, threading, urllib.request
import hashlib, hmac, secrets, urllib.parse, http.client, http.server

# ---------- CONFIG ----------

    """Run a program with a LIST of arguments (no shell); return (rc, output)."""
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
                           env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout + p.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return 124, "TIMEOUT after %ss" % timeout
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        return 127, str(e)

```python
# ---------- 5) Token proxy + tunnel + watchdog ----------
# The tunnel is public. Ollama has no login, so the tunnel points at this
# small proxy, which forwards only requests that carry the token.
API_TOKEN = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
SKIP_HEADERS = {"connection", "keep-alive", "proxy-authenticate", "proxy-authorization",
                "te", "trailers", "transfer-encoding", "upgrade", "host",
                "authorization", "content-length"}

class TokenProxy(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"   # the body ends when the connection closes (streams fine)

    def _forward(self):
        sent = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        if not hmac.compare_digest(sent.encode(), f"Bearer {API_TOKEN}".encode()):
            self.send_error(401, "missing or wrong token")
            return
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else None
        headers = {k: v for k, v in self.headers.items() if k.lower() not in SKIP_HEADERS}
        upstream = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", PORT, timeout=1800)
        try:
            upstream.request(self.command, self.path, body=body, headers=headers)
            resp = upstream.getresponse()
            self.send_response(resp.status, resp.reason)
            for k, v in resp.getheaders():
                if k.lower() not in SKIP_HEADERS:
                    self.send_header(k, v)
            self.end_headers()
            while True:
                chunk = resp.read1(65536)   # returns as soon as data arrives (streaming)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                self.wfile.write(chunk)
                self.wfile.flush()
        except Exception as e:
            try:
                self.send_error(502, f"upstream error: {e}")
            except Exception:
                pass
        finally:
            upstream.close()

    do_GET = do_POST = do_PUT = do_DELETE = do_HEAD = _forward

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):   # keep the notebook output readable
        pass

proxy = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PROXY_PORT), TokenProxy)
threading.Thread(target=proxy.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
print(f"token proxy: 127.0.0.1:{PROXY_PORT} -> 127.0.0.1:{PORT} ✔", flush=True)

print("=== Tunnel ===", flush=True)
CF = f"{WORKDIR}/cloudflared"

def sha256_of(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()

if not (os.path.exists(CF) and sha256_of(CF) == CLOUDFLARED_SHA256):
    rc, log = run(["curl", "-fL", "--retry", "3", "-o", CF,
                   "https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/download/"
                   f"{CLOUDFLARED_VER}/cloudflared-linux-amd64"])
    if rc != 0 or not os.path.exists(CF) or sha256_of(CF) != CLOUDFLARED_SHA256:
        raise RuntimeError(f"cloudflared {CLOUDFLARED_VER}: download failed or checksum mismatch (rc={rc})")
    os.chmod(CF, 0o755)
run(["pkill", "-f", "cloudflared tunnel"], timeout=10)
time.sleep(1)
LOG = f"{WORKDIR}/tunnel.log"
open(LOG, "w").close()
tunnel_log = open(LOG, "a")
```

### B-01 · `edit` tool: reject an empty `old_str`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/tools.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tools.rs`: `fn edit_file`, the `"edit"` entry in `fn tool_specs` |

#### What is wrong

`edit_file` counts matches with `text.matches(old_str)`. When `old_str` is empty, Rust finds an empty match between every pair of characters, so `"abc"` has 4 matches. With `replace_all: true`, `text.replace("", new_str)` puts `new_str` between every character and writes that back to disk. With `replace_all: false`, the model gets a confusing "matches 4 times" error instead of being told what is wrong.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
    let matches = text.matches(old_str).count();
    if matches == 0 {
        return Err(anyhow!("old_str not found in {path}"));
    }
```

#### Why it matters

One bad tool call from a small model turns a source file into garbage, for example `XaXbXcX` instead of `abc`, in a single step.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/tools.rs`. Find the signature of `fn edit_file` (around line 223). Add the empty check as the first thing in the body, before the file is read.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust

    new_str: &str,
    replace_all: bool,
) -> Result<String> {
```

Replace it with:

### B-02 · `/edit` must not cut Markdown files or drop the last newline

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P0 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/inline_edit.rs` |
| Read first | `src/inline_edit.rs`: `fn propose`, `fn strip_fences`, `mod tests` |

#### What is wrong

`/edit <file> <what>` asks the model for the complete new file. `strip_fences` then removes a Markdown code fence (a line of three backticks) that the model may have wrapped around its answer. It looks for the first backtick fence anywhere in the reply and the last line that starts a fence, and keeps only the text between them. A README that starts with a short heading and contains a code block is cut down to the inside of that block. Example: `# Title`, a bash block with `npm i`, then more text, becomes just `npm i`. When the fence is removed, the file's final newline is also lost, and the line-based diff preview cannot show that.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/inline_edit.rs`:
```rust
    let raw = one_shot(st, SYSTEM, &user, abort, false).await?;
    let new = strip_fences(&raw);
    if new == old {
        bail!("model returned the file unchanged");
    }
```

#### Why it matters

You press `y` on a preview and a Markdown file loses almost all its text, or every edited file ends without a newline (noisy git diffs). A cut-off reply (`finish_reason: "length"`) is a separate problem, fixed by B-03.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/inline_edit.rs`. Replace the whole function `strip_fences` (around line 96).

Find this code in `src/inline_edit.rs`:
```rust
/// Strip a markdown code fence the model wrapped its answer in, while
/// leaving a raw file that merely *contains* fences alone.
pub fn strip_fences(s: &str) -> String {
    let t = s.trim();
    let Some(first) = t.find("```") else { return s.to_string() };
    // Only treat leading text as preamble if it is short (a file that
    // starts with or contains ``` deep inside keeps its content intact).
    if t[..first].trim().len() > 100 {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let Some(nl) = t[first..].find('\n') else { return s.to_string() };
    let body_start = first + nl + 1;
    match t[body_start..].rfind("\n```") {
        Some(end) => t[body_start..][..end].to_string(),
        None => s.to_string(),
    }
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Strip ONE markdown fence that wraps the model's whole reply, while
/// leaving a file that merely *contains* fences alone (B-02).
///
/// The reply is unwrapped only when all of these hold:
/// - an opening fence line (3+ backticks, optional language) starts the
///   reply, or follows a short preamble (at most 100 chars) that is not
///   the first line of the old file;
/// - the last non-empty line is a closing fence with the same backticks;
/// - the old file does not itself start with a fence line.
/// Fences between the first and the last line are kept as they are.
pub fn strip_fences(reply: &str, old: &str) -> String {
    let lines: Vec<&str> = reply.lines().collect();
    let Some(open) = lines.iter().position(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with("```")) else {
        return reply.to_string();
    };
    let Some(close) = lines.iter().rposition(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()) else {
        return reply.to_string();
    };
    if close <= open {
        return reply.to_string();
    }
    let ticks = lines[open].trim_start().chars().take_while(|c| *c == '`').count();
    if lines[close].trim() != "`".repeat(ticks) {
        return reply.to_string();
    }
    let old_start = old.trim_start();
    if old_start.starts_with("```") {
        return reply.to_string(); // the file itself starts with a fence
    }
    let preamble = lines[..open].join("\n");
    let preamble = preamble.trim();
    if preamble.len() > 100 {
        return reply.to_string();
    }
    if let Some(first) = preamble.lines().next() {
        if old_start.starts_with(first.trim()) {
            return reply.to_string(); // the "preamble" is the file's own first line
        }
    }
    lines[open + 1..close].join("\n")
}

/// Give `new` the same line ending at the end of the file as `old` (B-02).
/// Models often drop the final newline; keeping the old ending avoids a
/// "no newline at end of file" change the diff preview cannot show.
pub fn match_trailing_newline(new: &str, old: &str) -> String {
    let old_body = old.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
    let old_tail = &old[old_body.len()..];
    format!("{}{old_tail}", new.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']))
}
```

### B-03 · Cut-off replies (`finish_reason: "length"`) are treated as complete

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/compact.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `pub async fn one_shot`, `pub async fn run_loop`; `src/compact.rs`: `async fn summarize`; `src/provider.rs`: `enum StreamEvent` |

#### What is wrong

Every reply ends with a `finish_reason`. `"length"` means the model hit its output token limit and the reply is incomplete. `StreamEvent::Done` carries this value, but every reader ignores it (`Done { .. } => break`):
- `run_loop` treats a cut-off text reply as the final answer, and runs a cut-off tool call. Broken JSON arguments become `{"raw": "..."}`, and the model gets a confusing "missing string arg" error.
- `one_shot` (inline `/edit`, the `/team` planner and reviewer, skill vetting) returns half an answer as if it were whole.
- The `/compact` summarizer returns half a summary, which then replaces the real history.

Small local models with a small output limit hit this often.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
                StreamEvent::Done { .. } => break,
                _ => acc.push(&ev),
            }
```

#### Why it matters

Inline `/edit` writes the reply back as the WHOLE file, so a cut-off reply deletes the end of the file. A cut-off `/compact` summary loses conversation history for good.

#### Steps

After this task: `one_shot` and the summarizer return an error instead of half a result. In `run_loop`, a cut-off text reply is kept but marked `[reply cut off: ...]`, and a `Note` event tells the user. A reply cut off in the middle of a tool call runs none of its calls; each call gets an error result, and the loop continues, so the model can retry within the same run.

<!-- TASK:B-04 -->
### B-04 · Repair chat history before sending it to the provider

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn build_chat_messages`, the start of `fn run_loop`; `src/provider.rs`: `struct ChatMsg`, `struct ToolCallReq` |

#### What is wrong

`build_chat_messages` turns the saved messages of a session into the list that is sent to the model. It sends whatever is in the database, and some saved shapes are invalid for OpenAI-compatible servers:

1. The run loop saves the assistant message with its tool calls *before* the tools run. If the program stops in between (you quit the TUI during a long `bash`, a crash, a database error), the history keeps tool calls that never got a `tool` result. The server then rejects every later request for that session.
2. A reply with only reasoning (no text, no tool calls) is saved and later sent as an empty assistant message, which some servers reject.
3. A slash-command expansion is saved as a `system` message in the middle of the history (in `agent_inner`). Many local chat templates allow `system` only as the first message.
4. `tool` messages that answer nothing are only removed when they are at the very end.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
    // Keep tool results that follow their assistant tool_call (the normal
    // mid-loop state the model must see). Drop trailing tool messages only
    // when they have no assistant tool_calls predecessor — true orphans
    // left behind by an interrupted/restarted run.
    let last_non_tool = out.iter().rposition(|m| m.role != "tool");
    let orphaned = last_non_tool
        .map(|i| !(out[i].role == "assistant" && out[i].tool_calls.is_some()))
        .unwrap_or(true);
```

#### Why it matters

One interrupted tool call makes the session unusable: every new prompt fails with an HTTP 400 from the provider until the user starts a new session. Compaction (B-05) and auto-compaction (F-07) can leave the same shapes, and this repair is their safety net.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/server.rs`. Go to the end of `fn build_chat_messages` (around line 1729). Replace the old orphan handling with one call to a new function `repair_history`, and add that function and two small helpers right after `build_chat_messages`.

Replace it with:

    // New (B-04): repair what a crash, an abort or a compaction can leave
    // behind before the provider sees it (see `repair_history`).
    Ok(repair_history(out))
}

/// New (B-04): the result sent for a tool call that never finished.
const INTERRUPTED_TOOL_RESULT: &str =
    "[interrupted] this tool call did not finish (the run was stopped); its result is unknown";

/// New (B-04): make a replayed history safe to send. Providers reject (or
/// get confused by) shapes that a crash, an abort or a compaction can leave
/// in the database:
/// - every `tool_calls` id of an assistant message must be answered by a
///   `tool` message right after it: a missing answer gets
///   `INTERRUPTED_TOOL_RESULT`, an answer to an unknown id is dropped;
/// - an assistant message with neither text nor tool calls is dropped;
/// - only the first message may be `system`: system notes at the start (a
///   compaction summary) are joined to it, later ones are sent as user text;
/// - back-to-back user messages become one.
fn repair_history(msgs: Vec<ChatMsg>) -> Vec<ChatMsg> {
    let mut out: Vec<ChatMsg> = Vec::with_capacity(msgs.len());
    // Tool call ids of the last assistant message that still need a result.
    let mut open: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for m in msgs {
        if m.role != "tool" {
            close_open_calls(&mut out, &mut open);
        }
        match m.role.as_str() {
            "tool" => {
                let id = m.tool_call_id.clone().unwrap_or_default();
                if let Some(i) = open.iter().position(|c| *c == id) {
                    open.remove(i);
                    out.push(m);
                }
                // Otherwise it answers nothing we sent: drop it.
            }
            "assistant" => {
                let has_text = m.content.as_deref().is_some_and(|t| !t.trim().is_empty());
                let ids: Vec<String> = m
                    .tool_calls
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|calls| calls.iter().map(|c| c.id.clone()).collect())
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                if !has_text && ids.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                open = ids;
                out.push(m);
            }
            "system" => {
                let text = m.content.unwrap_or_default();
                if out.iter().all(|x| x.role == "system") {
                    match out.first_mut() {
                        Some(first) => {
                            let joined =
                                format!("{}\n\n{text}", first.content.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
                            first.content = Some(joined);
                        }
                        None => out.push(ChatMsg {
                            role: "system".into(),
                            content: Some(text),
                            tool_calls: None,
                            tool_call_id: None,
                        }),
                    }
                } else {
                    push_user_text(&mut out, format!("[system note]\n{text}"));
                }
            }
            "user" => push_user_text(&mut out, m.content.unwrap_or_default()),
            _ => out.push(m),
        }
    }
    close_open_calls(&mut out, &mut open);
    out
}

/// New (B-04): answer every still-open tool call with
/// `INTERRUPTED_TOOL_RESULT`.
fn close_open_calls(out: &mut Vec<ChatMsg>, open: &mut Vec<String>) {
    for id in open.drain(..) {
        out.push(ChatMsg {
            role: "tool".into(),
            content: Some(INTERRUPTED_TOOL_RESULT.to_string()),
            tool_calls: None,
            tool_call_id: Some(id),
        });
    }
}

/// New (B-04): add user text; merge it into the previous message when that
/// one is also from the user.
fn push_user_text(out: &mut Vec<ChatMsg>, text: String) {
    if let Some(last) = out.last_mut() {
        if last.role == "user" {
            let joined = format!("{}\n\n{text}", last.content.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
            last.content = Some(joined);
            return;
        }
    }
    out.push(ChatMsg { role: "user".into(), content: Some(text), tool_calls: None, tool_call_id: None });
}
```

Nothing else changes: `build_chat_messages` still builds the raw list exactly as before, and only the last step is new.

### B-05 · Compaction: safe split point, never delete new messages, one transaction, role labels

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/compact.rs`, `src/db.rs`, `src/sessions.rs` |
| Read first | `src/compact.rs`: `fn split_at`, `fn compact`; `src/db.rs`: `fn apply_compaction`; `src/sessions.rs`: `fn flatten_msg` |

#### What is wrong

`/compact` replaces old messages with one summary message. Four bugs:

1. **Split point.** It always keeps the last 6 messages. If message number
   `len-6` is a `tool` result, the kept part starts with a tool result whose
   assistant tool call was summarized away. Strict OpenAI-style providers
   reject that history with an error.
2. **Lost messages.** `apply_compaction` deletes "every message not in the
   kept list", read again *after* the summary was written. A message that
   arrived during the (slow) summary call is in neither list and is deleted.
3. **No transaction.** Messages are deleted one by one and the summary is
   inserted afterwards. A crash in between loses history.
4. **Poor input.** The transcript uses `flatten_msg`, which has no `role:`
   prefix, so the summarizer cannot tell the user from the assistant. Every
   part is cut to 200–400 characters, and an earlier summary is cut to 400
   characters on the next `/compact`, so knowledge gets lost each time.

#### Where it is

```rust

```

            kept_ids.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();

#### Why it matters

A compaction should make a long session cheaper, not break it: today it can
make the next model call fail, and it can silently delete the newest user
message.

/// The diffable display text for a single message (no role prefix).
pub fn flatten_msg(m: &Message) -> String {
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    for p in &m.parts {
        match p {
            Part::Text { text } => parts.push(collapse(text, 400)),
            Part::Reasoning { text } => parts.push(format!("✻ {}", collapse(text, 300))),
            Part::ToolCall { name, input, .. } => {
                let args = collapse(&input.to_string(), 200);
                parts.push(format!("[call {name} {args}]"));
            }
            Part::ToolResult { output, is_error, .. } => {
                let tag = if *is_error { "err" } else { "ok" };
                parts.push(format!("[result {tag} {}]", collapse(output, 300)));
            }
        }
    }
    parts.join(" ")
}

/// Per-part character limits for [`flatten_msg_with`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FlattenLimits {
    pub text: usize,
    /// 0 = leave reasoning out.
    pub reasoning: usize,
    pub tool_args: usize,
    pub tool_result: usize,
}

/// The short limits `/diff` uses, so diffs stay readable.
pub const DIFF_LIMITS: FlattenLimits =
    FlattenLimits { text: 400, reasoning: 300, tool_args: 200, tool_result: 300 };

/// The diffable display text for a single message (no role prefix).
pub fn flatten_msg(m: &Message) -> String {
    flatten_msg_with(m, DIFF_LIMITS)
}

/// [`flatten_msg`] with explicit limits.
pub fn flatten_msg_with(m: &Message, lim: FlattenLimits) -> String {
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    for p in &m.parts {
        match p {
            Part::Text { text } => parts.push(collapse(text, lim.text)),
            Part::Reasoning { text } => {
                if lim.reasoning > 0 {
                    parts.push(format!("✻ {}", collapse(text, lim.reasoning)));
                }
            }
            Part::ToolCall { name, input, .. } => {
                let args = collapse(&input.to_string(), lim.tool_args);
                parts.push(format!("[call {name} {args}]"));
            }
            Part::ToolResult { output, is_error, .. } => {
                let tag = if *is_error { "err" } else { "ok" };
                parts.push(format!("[result {tag} {}]", collapse(output, lim.tool_result)));
            }
        }
    }
    parts.join(" ")
}

pub const SUMMARY_MARKER: &str = "[context compacted]";

/// Like [`split_at`], but the kept tail never starts with a `tool` message:
/// the assistant message that asked for those tool calls must stay in front
/// of its results (providers reject a tool result without its call). The
/// split moves earlier (keeping more) when it can, otherwise later.
pub fn safe_split(msgs: &[crate::db::Message]) -> Option<usize> {
    let start = split_at(msgs.len())?;
    let is_tool = |i: usize| msgs.get(i).is_some_and(|m| m.role == "tool");
    let mut s = start;
    while s > 0 && is_tool(s) {
        s -= 1;
    }
    if s >= MIN_COMPRESS && !is_tool(s) {
        return Some(s);
    }
    let mut s = start;
    while s < msgs.len() && is_tool(s) {
        s += 1;
    }
    (s < msgs.len()).then_some(s)
}

/// Limits for the summarizer's transcript: long enough to keep real detail.
pub const COMPACT_LIMITS: crate::sessions::FlattenLimits =
    crate::sessions::FlattenLimits { text: 4000, reasoning: 0, tool_args: 1000, tool_result: 1500 };

/// One transcript line per message for the summarizer: `role: text`. An
/// earlier summary is kept whole, so a second `/compact` does not cut the
/// first summary down.
pub fn transcript_lines(msgs: &[crate::db::Message]) -> Vec<String> {
    msgs.iter()
        .map(|m| {
            let texts: Vec<&str> = m
                .parts
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|p| match p {
                    crate::db::Part::Text { text } => Some(text.as_str()),
                    _ => None,
                })
                .collect();
            let earlier_summary =
                m.role == "system" && texts.iter().any(|t| t.starts_with(SUMMARY_MARKER));
            if earlier_summary {
                format!("system: {}", texts.join("\n"))
            } else {
                format!("{}: {}", m.role, crate::sessions::flatten_msg_with(m, COMPACT_LIMITS))
            }
        })
        .collect()
}
```

    /// `summary` as a system message positioned where the removed history

    pub fn apply_compaction(&self, session_id: &str, kept_ids: &[String], summary: &str) -> Result<()> {

```

Replace it with:
```rust
    /// Compaction: delete exactly the messages in `summarized_ids` and insert
    /// `summary` as one system message just before the oldest of them
    /// (timestamp minus 1 ms, so it sorts first). Everything happens in one
    /// transaction. Messages that arrived while the summary was being
    /// written are not in `summarized_ids`, so they are kept.
    pub fn replace_with_summary(&self, session_id: &str, summarized_ids: &[String], summary: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let mut conn = self.conn.lock().unwrap();
        let tx = conn.transaction()?;
        let mut first_at: Option<i64> = None;
        {
            let mut find = tx.prepare("SELECT created_at FROM messages WHERE id=?1 AND session_id=?2")?;
            let mut del = tx.prepare("DELETE FROM messages WHERE id=?1 AND session_id=?2")?;
            for id in summarized_ids {
                let at: Option<i64> = find.query_row(params![id, session_id], |r| r.get(0)).optional()?;
                if let Some(at) = at {
                    first_at = Some(first_at.map_or(at, |f| f.min(at)));
                    del.execute(params![id, session_id])?;
                }
            }
        }
        let Some(first_at) = first_at else {
            // Nothing left to replace (another compaction ran): change nothing.
            anyhow::bail!("the messages to compact no longer exist — nothing changed");
        };
        let parts = serde_json::to_string(&[Part::Text { text: summary.to_string() }])?;
        tx.execute(
            "INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, role, parts, created_at) VALUES (?1,?2,'system',?3,?4)",
            params![new_id("msg"), session_id, parts, first_at.saturating_sub(1)],
        )?;
        tx.execute("UPDATE sessions SET updated_at=?1 WHERE id=?2", params![now_ms(), session_id])?;
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(())
    }
```

### B-06 · Abort really stops: between tool calls, inside bash, for every run kind

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | L (a day or more) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/tools.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: the tool loop in `fn run_loop`, `fn execute_routed`, `fn install_skill_flow`, `fn kick_run`; `src/tools.rs`: `fn execute`, `fn bash`; `src/main.rs`: `fn headless_run`, `fn tui_run` |

#### What is wrong

A run stops when its "abort flag" (an `AtomicBool` shared with the run) is set. A new prompt sets it for the old run, and so does `POST /api/sessions/{id}/abort`. Today this only partly works:

1. The run loop checks the flag only before each model call. When the model asked for several tools in one turn, the remaining tools still run after an abort.
2. `tools::execute` has no abort flag. A running `bash` keeps going until it ends or times out (120 s by default). On timeout only the shell is killed, so its child processes (a dev server, `npm`) keep running.
3. Team runs, compaction, skill installs and several headless runs create a private flag that is never registered in `AppState::busy`. Nothing can stop them, and a new prompt runs in parallel with them.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
    match tools::execute(name, input, &st.workspace).await {
        Ok(out) => (out, true),
        Err(e) => (format!("error: {e}"), false),
```

#### Why it matters

You press stop (or send a new prompt) while the agent runs `rm`, `git` or `npm install`, and it keeps going: the next tool call in the turn still runs, the command keeps running, and orphan processes keep ports busy. GOALS.md lists "Cancel button → aborts the in-flight tool" as not done.

7. Replace the end of `fn bash` (from `child.spawn()` to its closing brace) and add three small helper functions after it. A "process group" is a set of processes that can be signalled together. On Linux/macOS the shell becomes the leader of its own group, so killing the group stops everything it started. On Windows, `taskkill /T` kills the process and all its children. It must run while the shell still exists, because Windows finds the children through it.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:

Replace it with:
```rust
    // New (B-06): on Linux/macOS the shell leads its own process group, so
    // abort and timeout can stop everything it started, not just the shell.
    #[cfg(unix)]
    child.process_group(0);
    let mut child = child.spawn().context("spawning shell")?;
    let pid = child.id();
    let mut stdout = child.stdout.take();
    let mut stderr = child.stderr.take();
    // Read both pipes to the end, then reap the shell (like wait_with_output).
    let work = async move {
        let (out, err) = tokio::join!(read_pipe(&mut stdout), read_pipe(&mut stderr));
        (child.wait().await, out, err)
    };
    tokio::pin!(work);
    let stopped = tokio::select! {
        (status, out, err) = &mut work => {
            let status = status.map_err(|e| anyhow!("command failed to run: {e}"))?;
            let mut s = format!("exit code: {}\n", status.code().unwrap_or(-1));
            if !out.is_empty() {
                s.push_str("--- stdout ---\n");
                s.push_str(&truncate(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&out), 60_000));
            }
            if !err.is_empty() {
                s.push_str("\n--- stderr ---\n");
                s.push_str(&truncate(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&err), 20_000));
            }
            return Ok(s);
        }
        _ = tokio::time::sleep(timeout) => format!("command timed out after {}s", timeout.as_secs()),
        _ = wait_for_abort(abort) => "command aborted".to_string(),
    };
    // Abort or timeout: kill the whole process tree while the shell still
    // exists (`work` keeps it alive until this function returns).
    kill_tree(pid).await;
    Err(anyhow!("{stopped} (process tree killed)"))
}

/// New (B-06): read a child's pipe to the end (empty when there is none).
async fn read_pipe<R: tokio::io::AsyncRead + Unpin>(pipe: &mut Option<R>) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    if let Some(p) = pipe.as_mut() {
        let _ = tokio::io::AsyncReadExt::read_to_end(p, &mut buf).await;
    }
    buf
}

/// New (B-06): kill a shell and everything it started. Linux/macOS: signal
/// the shell's process group (see `bash`). Windows: taskkill walks the tree.
async fn kill_tree(pid: Option<u32>) {
    let Some(pid) = pid else { return };
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let mut cmd = {
        let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new("taskkill");
        c.args(["/T", "/F", "/PID", &pid.to_string()]);
        c
    };
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let mut cmd = {
        let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new("kill");
        c.args(["-s", "KILL", "--", &format!("-{pid}")]);
        c
    };
    cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()).stdout(Stdio::null()).stderr(Stdio::null());
    let _ = cmd.status().await;
}

/// New (B-06): resolves once `abort` is set (checked every 100 ms).
async fn wait_for_abort(abort: &std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool) {
    while !abort.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
    }
}
```

/// (so `/undo` can roll the run back), stores the message, expands slash

pub async fn run_agent(st: &Shared, session_id: &str, user_content: &str, abort: Arc<AtomicBool>) {
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (B-06): the "busy slot" API. Every kind of run registers its abort
/// flag in `busy`, so `/abort`, a new prompt, the TUI and the GUI can stop it.
impl AppState {
    /// Register a new run for `session_id` and return its abort flag. A run
    /// already active on the session is told to stop (it is replaced).
    pub async fn claim_run(&self, session_id: &str) -> Arc<AtomicBool> {
        let mut busy = self.busy.write().await;
        if let Some(old) = busy.remove(session_id) {
            old.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        }
        let flag = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        busy.insert(session_id.to_string(), flag.clone());
        flag
    }

    /// Free the session's slot, but only while `flag` still owns it.
    pub async fn release_run(&self, session_id: &str, flag: &Arc<AtomicBool>) {
        let mut busy = self.busy.write().await;
        if busy.get(session_id).map(|f| Arc::ptr_eq(f, flag)).unwrap_or(false) {
            busy.remove(session_id);
        }
    }

    /// True when a newer run took the session's slot from `flag`.
    pub async fn is_superseded(&self, session_id: &str, flag: &Arc<AtomicBool>) -> bool {
        let busy = self.busy.read().await;
        busy.get(session_id).map(|f| !Arc::ptr_eq(f, flag)).unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Ask the session's active run to stop. False when nothing runs.
    pub async fn abort_run(&self, session_id: &str) -> bool {
        let busy = self.busy.read().await;
        match busy.get(session_id) {
            Some(flag) => {
                flag.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
                true
            }
            None => false,
        }
    }

    /// True while a run is registered for the session.
    pub async fn run_active(&self, session_id: &str) -> bool {
        self.busy.read().await.contains_key(session_id)
    }

    /// Run `work` as the session's current run: registered in `busy`,
    /// replacing any active run, released when it ends. `work` gets the
    /// state, the session id and the run's abort flag.
    pub async fn kick_task<F, Fut>(self: &Shared, session_id: String, work: F)
    where
        F: FnOnce(Shared, String, Arc<AtomicBool>) -> Fut + Send + 'static,
        Fut: std::future::Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'static,
    {
        let flag = self.claim_run(&session_id).await;
        let st = self.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            work(st.clone(), session_id.clone(), flag.clone()).await;

### B-07 · CLI: the prompt must not pick up option values

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/main.rs`: `fn run` (argument handling at its start), `fn print_help` |

#### What is wrong

`fn run` finds the prompt by taking the first command-line word that does not start with `-`. That word is often the value of an option:

- `opencode-rust --model gpt-4 --headless "fix the bug"` runs the prompt `gpt-4`.
- `opencode-rust --port 4000` opens the TUI and immediately sends `4000` to the model.
- `opencode-rust --headless fix the bug` (no quotes) only sends `fix`.
- A typo such as `--headles "hi"` is silently ignored, and the TUI starts and sends `hi`.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust
    // Positional prompt for headless mode.
    let prompt: Option<String> = args
        .iter()
        .find(|a| !a.starts_with('-'))
        .cloned();
```

#### Why it matters

The model gets a wrong prompt (for example `4000`) and starts working on nonsense. A headless script can run the wrong task, and a mistyped option gives no error.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/main.rs`. In `fn run` (around line 106), replace the prompt search with a call to a new function `positional_prompt`.

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust
    // Positional prompt for headless mode.
    let prompt: Option<String> = args
        .iter()
        .find(|a| !a.starts_with('-'))
        .cloned();
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    // Positional prompt: every word that is not an option or an option's
    // value, joined with spaces. New (B-07): see `positional_prompt`.
    let prompt: Option<String> = match positional_prompt(&args) {
        Ok(p) => p,
        Err(msg) => {
            eprintln!("{msg}\nRun `opencode-rust --help` for the list of options.");
            std::process::exit(2);
        }
    };
```

2. Add the new function and its two lists of options right above `async fn snapshot_command` (around line 135).

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust
/// `/undo` / `/redo`: git snapshot restore off the async runtime (subprocess).
async fn snapshot_command(st: std::sync::Arc<server::AppState>, sid: String, redo: bool) {
    let ws = st.workspace.clone();
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (B-07): options that take a value. Their value is never part of the
/// prompt. (`--timeout` is used by task B-09.)
const VALUE_FLAGS: &[&str] = &["--port", "--model", "--base-url", "--timeout"];
/// New (B-07): options without a value. (`--yes` is used by task S-02.)
const SWITCH_FLAGS: &[&str] = &["--headless", "--gui", "--yes", "--version", "-V", "--help", "-h"];

/// New (B-07): the prompt from the command line. Options and their values
/// are skipped, the remaining words are joined with spaces, and everything
/// after `--` is prompt text (so a prompt may start with `-`).
/// Err = an option this program does not know.
fn positional_prompt(args: &[String]) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
    let mut words: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < args.len() {
        let a = args[i].as_str();
        if a == "--" {
            words.extend(args[i + 1..].iter().map(String::as_str));
            break;
        }
        if VALUE_FLAGS.contains(&a) {
            i += 2; // skip the option and its value
            continue;
        }
        if SWITCH_FLAGS.contains(&a) {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if a.starts_with('-') && a.len() > 1 {
            return Err(format!("unknown option: {a}"));
        }
        words.push(a);
        i += 1;
    }
    let prompt = words.join(" ");
    Ok(if prompt.trim().is_empty() { None } else { Some(prompt) })
}

/// `/undo` / `/redo`: git snapshot restore off the async runtime (subprocess).
async fn snapshot_command(st: std::sync::Arc<server::AppState>, sid: String, redo: bool) {
    let ws = st.workspace.clone();
```

### B-08 · Heartbeat: send the API key, match the comment, skip it in headless mode

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn start_heartbeat`; `src/config.rs`: `fn effective_base_url`; `src/provider.rs`: `fn new` and how requests add `bearer_auth` |

#### What is wrong

Every 15 seconds `start_heartbeat` calls `GET {base_url}/models` and reports "api ok" or "api DOWN" in the TUI header.

1. It sends no `Authorization` header. Providers that need a key (OpenAI, OpenRouter and many others) answer 401, so the header shows "api DOWN" all the time, even while the agent works fine.
2. The doc comment says "Any HTTP response (even 404) counts as reachable", but the code requires a 2xx answer. The comment is wrong; the code is right.
3. It reads `cfg.provider.base_url` directly instead of `cfg.effective_base_url()`, the function the real client uses.
4. `main.rs` starts it in every mode, including `--headless`, where nobody sees it.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
                let ok = http
                    .get(format!("{base}/models"))
                    .send()
                    .await
                    .map(|r| r.status().is_success())
                    .unwrap_or(false);
```

#### Why it matters

A permanent "api DOWN" teaches users to ignore the indicator, so they miss a real outage (for example an expired tunnel). Headless runs also make needless network calls to the provider.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/server.rs`. Replace the doc comment and the start of `fn start_heartbeat` (around line 354).

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust

    /// counts as reachable — only transport errors mean DOWN. Also keeps
    /// Cloudflare quick tunnels warm between prompts.
    pub fn start_heartbeat(self: &Shared) {
        let st = self.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let base = st.cfg.provider.base_url.trim().trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
            if base.is_empty() {
                return;
            }
```

Replace it with:

    /// New (B-08): sends the API key like the real client, and uses the same

    /// tunnels warm between prompts.
    pub fn start_heartbeat(self: &Shared) {
        let st = self.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let Ok(base) = st.cfg.effective_base_url() else {
                return;
            };
            let key = st.cfg.provider.api_key.clone();

#### What is wrong

All events (streamed text, tool starts, approval requests, run ends) travel over one `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel with room for only 256 events. Every streamed text piece is one event. A client that reads too slowly gets the error `Lagged` and the oldest events are gone. Every client then simply continues:

- `events_sse` (HTTP), the TUI forwarder and the headless loop all ignore `Lagged`.
- If the lost event was `ApprovalNeeded`, the run waits for an answer that nobody can give and is denied after `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s).
- If the lost event was `RunFinished`, the headless loop waits forever. It also has no overall time limit.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
                Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => continue,
                Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => return None,
            }
```

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => break,
            Err(_) => continue,
        }
```

#### Why it matters

A slow terminal or a busy machine can make a prompt disappear. The tool is then denied after five minutes without the user ever seeing the question. A headless job in CI can hang until the CI system kills it.

#### Steps

How the fix works. A bigger buffer makes lag rare. Every pending approval keeps a copy of its `ApprovalNeeded` event, so a client that lagged can get the prompts again. The headless loop answers missed approvals, checks every 2 s of silence that its run is still alive, and stops after a time limit.

The work has three stages. Build and test after each one.

**Stage 1: the core (bigger buffer, pending approvals, HTTP event stream).**

    let rx = st.events.subscribe();
    // New (B-09): events waiting to be sent before the next live one.
    let queue: std::collections::VecDeque<Event> = std::collections::VecDeque::new();
    let stream = futures::stream::unfold((rx, queue, st), |(mut rx, mut queue, st)| async move {
        loop {
            if let Some(ev) = queue.pop_front() {
                return Some((Ok(ev), (rx, queue, st)));
            }
            match rx.recv().await {
                Ok(ev) => {
                    if let Ok(data) = serde_json::to_string(&ev) {
                        return Some((Ok(Event::default().data(data)), (rx, queue, st)));
                    }

                // New (B-09): this client fell behind and lost events. Say so
                // (SSE event "lagged", data = how many) and send every
                // approval that still waits, so no prompt is lost.
                Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(n)) => {
                    queue.push_back(Event::default().event("lagged").data(n.to_string()));
                    for ev in st.pending_approvals() {
                        if let Ok(data) = serde_json::to_string(&ev) {
                            queue.push_back(Event::default().data(data));
                        }
                    }
                }
                Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => return None,
            }
        }
    });

/// New (B-09): how long a whole headless run may take. `--timeout N`
/// (seconds) or OPENCODE_RUST_HEADLESS_TIMEOUT; default 2 hours; 0 = no
/// limit. A value that is not a number falls back to the default.
fn headless_timeout(args: &[String], env: Option<&str>) -> Option<std::time::Duration> {
    let from_args = args
        .iter()
        .position(|a| a == "--timeout")
        .and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1))
        .map(String::as_str);
    let secs = from_args
        .or(env)
        .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<u64>().ok())
        .unwrap_or(7200);
    (secs > 0).then(|| std::time::Duration::from_secs(secs))
}

#### Do not

- Do not "fix" lag by making the channel unbounded; a stuck client would then use unlimited memory.
- Do not re-send old text deltas after a lag; only approvals are re-sent, because they need an answer.
- Do not exit with code 0 when the run's result was lost; a script must see that something went wrong.

### B-10 · New event `ApprovalResolved` (answered, timed out, aborted, released by turbo)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/tui/state.rs` |

#### What is wrong

When an approval request ends, the core sends no event. This happens when it is answered from another place (HTTP, the GUI, the headless loop), when it times out, when the run is aborted, or when turbo mode releases it. A UI that shows an approval modal cannot know that the question is gone, so the modal stays on screen and a late key press answers nothing. `set_perm_mode` returns the released ids, but the TUI ignores them.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
    let result = tokio::select! {
        r = rx => r.unwrap_or(false),
        _ = tokio::time::sleep(timeout) => false,
        _ = async {
            while !abort.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
            }
        } => false,
    };
```

#### Why it matters

A modal for a request that already timed out invites the user to "approve" something that will never run, while the run went on without the tool. Tasks B-13 (GUI) and B-15 (TUI) need this event to close their modals.

#### Steps

Design: the event is sent in exactly one place, the waiting function `check_permission`, after the wait ends. Whoever ends the wait (`decide`, the turbo drain, the timeout, an abort) gives the reason, which travels through the approval's channel. So each request gets exactly one `ApprovalResolved`, even when an answer and the timeout happen at the same moment.

            ("always".into(), true),

### B-11 · GUI: `covered` flag never hides the native preview view

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs` |

#### What is wrong

The preview panel is a native child webview. It always paints on top of the
HTML page, so it must be hidden while the approval modal is open. The code sets
`gs.browser.covered = true` when an approval arrives, and back to `false` when
it is answered. But `covered` is only read inside `show_browser`, and nothing
calls `show_browser` after these changes. So the preview stays on screen over
the modal until some unrelated event (a resize, a page load) happens to call
`show_browser`. Switching to Turbo also clears the modal without resetting
`covered`.

```

The modal asks "may the agent run `rm -rf build`?". If the preview page covers
the modal, the user cannot read or answer it, and the request is denied after
the timeout.
