<!-- TASK:B-12 -->
### B-12 · GUI: events from other sessions leak into the open chat

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: `struct GuiState`, `struct PendingApproval`, `GuiState::on_event`, `GuiState::submit`, `GuiState::payload`, `fn settle_approval`, `fn load_session`, the `NewSession` and `Mode` arms in `fn run` |

#### What is wrong

All chats share one event bus (`state.events`). Every event carries a
`session_id`, but `GuiState::on_event` ignores it. So:

- text streamed by a run in chat A appears in chat B when you switch to B;
- a run finishing in any chat clears `busy` and the approval modal of the chat
  on screen, even when that modal belongs to another chat (that run then waits
  for its timeout and is denied);
- `SessionCreated` / `SessionLoaded` from another client (HTTP API, TUI) switch
  the GUI to that chat;
- a second approval (from another chat) silently replaces the one on screen.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
            ServerEvent::RunFinished { ok, message, .. } => {
                eprintln!("[gui] run finished ok={ok}");
                self.busy = false;
                // A finished run cannot still be waiting on an approval.
                self.approval = None;
```

#### Why it matters

The user reads a wrong transcript, a run in another chat gets its approval
dropped (a silent denial), and another client can change what the window shows.

#### Steps

Stage 1 makes approvals belong to a chat (shown for every chat, queued, removed
by id). Stage 2 sends transcript text only to its own chat: text for a running
chat that is not on screen goes to a live copy in the map `background`.

```rust
///
/// B-12: a chat whose run is still going is shown from its live copy, and
/// the chat we leave keeps its live copy if its run is still going.
fn load_session(gs: &mut GuiState, st: &server::AppState, id: &str) {
    let entries = match gs.background.remove(id) {
        Some(live) => live,
        None => match st.db.messages(id) {
            Ok(msgs) => entries_from_messages(&msgs),
            Err(e) => {
                gs.push(EntryKind::Error, format!("load session failed: {e}"));
                return;
            }
        },
    };
    gs.leave_current_chat();
    gs.session = Some(id.to_string());
    gs.entries = entries;
    gs.busy = gs.running.contains(id);
}
```

### B-13 · GUI: approval modal lingers, hotkeys need focus, one-key always-allow

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-10 (adds `ServerEvent::ApprovalResolved`), B-12 (adds `PendingApproval::session_id`, `GuiState::finish_approval`, `approval_queue` and the payload keys `other_chat`, `chat`, `queued`) |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs`, `src/gui.html`, `tests/gui/panel.js` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: `GuiState::apply_event` (named `on_event` before B-12), `GuiState::finish_approval`; `src/gui.html`: the `#approval` markup, the `D1: approval modal` part of `window.render`, `answerApproval` in `initApp` |

#### What is wrong

- When the core times out or aborts an approval, the GUI hears nothing. The
  modal stays on screen at "0s" and blocks the window until the run ends.
- The hotkeys `y` / `a` / `n` are ignored while focus is in a text field, and
  the composer has focus when the modal appears. So the shown hotkeys do nothing
  until the user clicks somewhere else.
- A single key press on `a` grants a permanent "always allow". That is easy to
  hit by accident.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gui.html`:
```js
      var k = String(ev.key || "").toLowerCase();
      if (k === "y") { ev.preventDefault(); answerApproval(true, false); }
      else if (k === "a") { ev.preventDefault(); answerApproval(true, true); }
      else if (k === "n") { ev.preventDefault(); answerApproval(false, false); }
```

#### Why it matters

A stuck modal makes the whole window unusable. A permanent grant typed by
accident lets that exact tool call (for example a `bash` command) run without
asking from then on.

#### Steps

Stage 1 — Rust (`src/gui.rs`).

2. Rust: a safety net for a lost event (the event bus can drop events when it
   lags). Add a new method right after `GuiState::new`.

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
impl GuiState {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
```

Replace it with:
```rust
impl GuiState {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// New (B-13): drop approvals the core must have timed out already —
    /// their `ApprovalResolved` event may have been lost. `now` is a
    /// parameter so tests can use a fixed clock. Returns true when one went.
    pub fn expire_stale_approval(&mut self, now: Instant) -> bool {
        let grace = Duration::from_secs(self.approval_timeout_secs + 5);
        let stale: Vec<String> = self
            .approval
            .iter()
            .chain(self.approval_queue.iter())
            .filter(|a| now.saturating_duration_since(a.started) > grace)
            .map(|a| a.id.clone())
            .collect();
        for id in &stale {
            self.finish_approval(id);
        }
        if !stale.is_empty() {
            self.push(
                EntryKind::System,
                "An approval got no answer in time and was denied.".to_string(),
            );
        }
        !stale.is_empty()
    }
```

### B-14 · TUI transcript: show the newest lines even when lines wrap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `Cargo.toml`, `src/tui/draw.rs`, `src/tui/state.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tui/draw.rs`: the `// Transcript` part of `fn draw`; `src/tui/state.rs`: `struct App`, `KeyCode::Up` / `KeyCode::Down` in `fn on_key` |

#### What is wrong

The transcript scrolls by logical lines (one line of text), but the `Paragraph` wraps each long line onto several screen rows. `draw` takes the last N logical lines, where N is the box height, and the wrapping then needs more rows than the box has. The bottom rows, which are the newest output, are cut off. Pressing ↓ cannot reach them, because scroll 0 is already "the bottom". Also, `scroll` grows without limit when you press ↑ at the top, so ↓ seems dead afterwards.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tui/draw.rs`:
```rust
    let total = lines.len() as u16;
    let view_h = transcript_area.height.saturating_sub(2) as u16;
    let max_scroll = total.saturating_sub(view_h);
    let start = max_scroll.saturating_sub(app.scroll);
```

#### Why it matters

LLM answers are long paragraphs, which are single long lines. In a normal session the end of the answer is invisible, so the user cannot read what the agent just said.

#### Steps

1. Open `Cargo.toml`. Turn on ratatui's `unstable-rendered-line-info` feature. It unlocks one function, `Paragraph::line_count`, which tells how many rows a wrapped paragraph needs. Cargo.lock does not record features, so it does not change.

Find this code in `Cargo.toml`:
```toml
# TUI
ratatui = "0.29"
crossterm = { version = "0.28", features = ["event-stream"] }
```

Replace it with:
```toml
# TUI
ratatui = { version = "0.29", features = ["unstable-rendered-line-info"] }
crossterm = { version = "0.28", features = ["event-stream"] }
```

2. Open `src/tui/state.rs`. Add a field to `struct App` (around line 274) where `draw` stores how far the transcript can scroll. `draw` only gets `&App`, so the field is a `Cell` (a value you may set through a shared reference).

Find this code in `src/tui/state.rs`:
```rust
    pub session_id: Option<String>,
    pub scroll: u16,
```

Add this right after it:
```rust

    /// sets it every frame (it knows the wrapped height); `on_key` caps
    /// `scroll` with it.
    pub scroll_max: std::cell::Cell<u16>,
```

Find this code in `src/tui/state.rs`:
```rust

            scroll: 0,
```

Add this right after it:


Find this code in `src/tui/state.rs`:
```rust

                self.scroll = self.scroll.saturating_add(1);

```


5. Open `src/tui/draw.rs`. In `fn draw`, replace the transcript scroll code (around line 172) with row-based scrolling. `line_count` is measured BEFORE the border block is added, so it counts text rows only, at the inner width.

Find this code in `src/tui/draw.rs`:
```rust
    let total = lines.len() as u16;
    let view_h = transcript_area.height.saturating_sub(2) as u16;
    let max_scroll = total.saturating_sub(view_h);
    let start = max_scroll.saturating_sub(app.scroll);
    let visible: Vec<Line> = lines
        .into_iter()
        .skip(start as usize)
        .take(view_h as usize)
        .collect();
    // The title counts the scrollback so nobody wonders where the rest went.
    let title = if start > 0 {
        format!(" transcript · ↑{start} earlier ")
    } else {
        " transcript ".to_string()
    };
    let transcript = Paragraph::new(visible)
        .block(
            Block::default()
                .borders(Borders::ALL)
                .border_type(BorderType::Rounded)
                .border_style(Style::default().fg(FB_BORDER))
                .title(title),
        )
        .wrap(Wrap { trim: false });
    f.render_widget(transcript, transcript_area);
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    // B-14: scroll by screen rows AFTER wrapping. Counting logical lines
    // hid the newest output whenever long lines wrapped onto several rows.
    let inner_w = transcript_area.width.saturating_sub(2);
    let view_h = transcript_area.height.saturating_sub(2) as usize;
    let paragraph = Paragraph::new(lines).wrap(Wrap { trim: false });
    let total = paragraph.line_count(inner_w); // rows; no block set yet
    let max_scroll = total.saturating_sub(view_h);
    app.scroll_max.set(max_scroll.min(u16::MAX as usize) as u16);
    let up = (app.scroll as usize).min(max_scroll);
    let top = max_scroll - up; // first row shown
    // The title counts the scrollback so nobody wonders where the rest went.
    let title = if top > 0 {
        format!(" transcript · ↑{top} earlier ")
    } else {
        " transcript ".to_string()
    };
    let transcript = paragraph
        .block(
            Block::default()
                .borders(Borders::ALL)
                .border_type(BorderType::Rounded)
                .border_style(Style::default().fg(FB_BORDER))
                .title(title),
        )
        .scroll((top.min(u16::MAX as usize) as u16, 0));
    f.render_widget(transcript, transcript_area);
```

| Field | Value |

| Priority | P1 |

| Depends on | B-10, S-07, B-22 |
| Files to change | `src/tui/state.rs`, `src/tui/draw.rs`, `src/tui/tests.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tui/state.rs`: `struct App`, `fn on_key`, `fn on_approval_key`, `fn on_event`; `src/tui/draw.rs`: the overlay blocks in `fn draw` |

#### What is wrong

1. The approval overlay shows only the first 200 characters of the tool input, and drops line breaks, so two commands look like one.
2. A second `ApprovalNeeded` replaces the one on screen. The first is never answered and waits for the server timeout.
3. `y`/`a`/`n` also work with Ctrl or Alt held (Ctrl+A = "always allow"), and a key typed for the input box just as the overlay appears answers it.
4. Help, sessions, the mission picker and the edit preview are drawn over the approval box while the keys still go to the approval.
5. Ctrl+C does nothing while an approval is open.

B-10 adds `ServerEvent::ApprovalResolved` (answered elsewhere, timed out, aborted, or released by turbo). The overlay must close when it arrives.


#### Why it matters

The approval prompt is the user's last check before a command runs. If it hides part of the command, answers itself, or sits under another window, that check fails.

#### Steps

**Stage 1: queue, keys and `ApprovalResolved` (`src/tui/state.rs`).**

```rust
            KeyCode::Char('y') | KeyCode::Char('Y') => {

            }

                Some(InputAction::Approve { id: ap.id, always: true })
            }
            KeyCode::Char('n') | KeyCode::Char('N') | KeyCode::Esc => {
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    /// B-15: decision keys are ignored this long after an approval appears.
    const APPROVAL_GRACE: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_millis(400);

    /// Approval overlay keys: y = once, a = always, n/Esc = deny,
    /// ↑/↓/PgUp/PgDn scroll the detail, Ctrl+C quits (B-15).
    fn on_approval_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> Option<InputAction> {
        let ctrl = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL);
        let alt = key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::ALT);
        if ctrl && key.code == KeyCode::Char('c') {
            self.should_quit = true;
            return None;
        }
        match key.code {
            KeyCode::Up => self.approval_scroll = self.approval_scroll.saturating_sub(1),
            KeyCode::Down => self.approval_scroll = self.approval_scroll.saturating_add(1),
            KeyCode::PageUp => self.approval_scroll = self.approval_scroll.saturating_sub(10),
            KeyCode::PageDown => self.approval_scroll = self.approval_scroll.saturating_add(10),
            _ => {}
        }
        // Never answer on Ctrl/Alt combinations (Ctrl+A must not mean
        // "always"), nor on keys typed just before the overlay appeared.
        if ctrl || alt || self.approval_since.is_some_and(|t| t.elapsed() < Self::APPROVAL_GRACE) {
            return None;
        }
        let ap = match key.code {
            KeyCode::Char('y' | 'Y' | 'a' | 'A' | 'n' | 'N') | KeyCode::Esc => self.approval.take()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let action = match key.code {
            KeyCode::Char('y' | 'Y') => InputAction::Approve { id: ap.id, always: false },
            KeyCode::Char('a' | 'A') => InputAction::Approve { id: ap.id, always: true },
            _ => InputAction::Deny(ap.id),
        };
        self.next_approval();
        Some(action)
    }

    /// B-15: put `ap` on screen with a fresh scroll and grace timer.
    fn show_approval(&mut self, ap: PendingApproval) {
        self.approval = Some(ap);
        self.approval_scroll = 0;
        self.approval_since = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
    }

    /// B-15: show the next queued approval, if any.
    fn next_approval(&mut self) {
        self.approval_scroll = 0;
        self.approval_since = None;
        if let Some(ap) = self.approval_queue.pop_front() {
            self.show_approval(ap);
        }
    }
```

```rust
/// B-15: the approval overlay — the WHOLE tool input, scrollable, with the
/// keys in the bottom border so they stay visible.
fn draw_approval(f: &mut Frame, app: &App) {
    let Some(ap) = &app.approval else { return };
    let area = centered_rect(80, 70, f.area());
    f.render_widget(Clear, area);
    let mut text = vec![
        Line::from("Tool approval required")
            .style(Style::default().fg(FB_ERROR).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
        Line::from(format!("Tool:  {}", ap.tool)).style(Style::default().fg(FB_FG)),
        Line::from("Input:").style(Style::default().fg(FB_FG)),
    ];
    for l in approval_detail_lines(&ap.detail) {
        text.push(Line::from(l).style(Style::default().fg(FB_MUTED)));
    }
    let title = match app.approval_queue.len() {
        0 => " approval ".to_string(),
        n => format!(" approval · {n} more waiting "),
    };
    let keys = " [y] allow once  [a] always (this workspace)  [n/Esc] deny  [↑↓] scroll ";
    let scroll = app.approval_scroll.min(text.len().min(u16::MAX as usize) as u16);
    let block = Block::default()
        .borders(Borders::ALL)
        .border_type(BorderType::Rounded)
        .border_style(Style::default().fg(FB_BORDER))
        .title(title)
        .title_bottom(Line::from(keys).style(Style::default().fg(FB_GREEN)));
    let widget = Paragraph::new(text).block(block).wrap(Wrap { trim: false }).scroll((scroll, 0));
    f.render_widget(widget, area);
}

/// B-15: one row per line of the detail; a tab becomes four spaces and any
/// other control character `\u{..}`, so nothing is hidden or merged.
pub fn approval_detail_lines(detail: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    detail
        .split('\n')
        .map(|line| {
            line.chars()
                .map(|c| match c {
                    '\t' => "    ".to_string(),
                    c if c.is_control() => format!("\\u{{{:x}}}", c as u32),
                    c => c.to_string(),
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .collect()
}
```

### B-16 · TUI: give the terminal back on errors and panics

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/tui/mod.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tui/mod.rs`: `fn run`; `src/main.rs`: `fn install_crash_log`; `Cargo.toml`: `[profile.release]` |

#### What is wrong

`tui::run` switches the terminal into raw mode (keys are not echoed, Enter does not move to a new line) and into the alternate screen. It only switches back at the very end of `run`. Any `?` that returns an error earlier (`Terminal::new`, `draw`, `event::poll`, `event::read`) skips that cleanup. A panic skips it too. The release build has `panic = "abort"`, so no destructor runs on a panic; only the panic hook (the function Rust calls when a panic starts) runs.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tui/mod.rs`:
```rust
    disable_raw_mode()?;
    terminal2.backend_mut().execute(LeaveAlternateScreen)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

#### Why it matters

After an error or panic, the user's shell is unusable: typed text is invisible, the screen stays blank, and the panic message is printed into the alternate screen and lost. The user must type `reset` blindly or close the window.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/tui/mod.rs`. Replace the `use` lines at the top (around line 11) with the same lines plus a restore function, a guard type and a panic-hook installer. A guard is a value whose `Drop` code runs when it goes out of scope, which includes every early `return` or `?`.

Find this code in `src/tui/mod.rs`:
```rust
use crate::server::ServerEvent;
use anyhow::Result;
use crossterm::{
    event::{self, Event, KeyEventKind},
    terminal::{disable_raw_mode, enable_raw_mode, EnterAlternateScreen, LeaveAlternateScreen},
    ExecutableCommand,
};
use ratatui::prelude::*;
use std::time::Duration;
```

Replace it with:
```rust
use crate::server::ServerEvent;
use anyhow::Result;
use crossterm::{
    event::{self, Event, KeyEventKind},
    terminal::{disable_raw_mode, enable_raw_mode, EnterAlternateScreen, LeaveAlternateScreen},
    ExecutableCommand,
};
use ratatui::prelude::*;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::time::Duration;

/// B-16: true while the TUI owns the terminal (raw mode + alternate screen).
static TERMINAL_TAKEN: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// B-16: claim the "restore" job. Returns true exactly once per take.
fn release_terminal() -> bool {
    TERMINAL_TAKEN.swap(false, Ordering::SeqCst)
}

/// B-16: give the terminal back — end raw mode, leave the alternate screen,
/// show the cursor. Does nothing if the TUI does not own the terminal.
/// Every step is tried even when an earlier one fails.
fn restore_terminal() {
    if release_terminal() {
        let _ = disable_raw_mode();
        let mut out = std::io::stdout();
        let _ = out.execute(LeaveAlternateScreen);
        let _ = out.execute(crossterm::cursor::Show);
    }
}

/// B-16: restores the terminal when dropped — on the normal exit and on
/// every early `?` return out of [`run`].
struct TerminalGuard;

impl Drop for TerminalGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        restore_terminal();
    }
}

/// B-16: restore the terminal BEFORE the panic message is printed. With
/// `panic = "abort"` no destructor runs on a panic, but the hook does. It
/// chains to the previous hook (main.rs `install_crash_log`), so the
/// message and crash.log are still written.
fn install_panic_restore() {
    static ONCE: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
    ONCE.call_once(|| {
        let previous = std::panic::take_hook();
        std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |info| {
            restore_terminal();
            previous(info);
        }));
    });
}
```

2. In `fn run`, install the hook and create the guard right after raw mode is on, before anything else can fail (around line 27).

Find this code in `src/tui/mod.rs`:
```rust
    let mut stdout = std::io::stdout();
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    stdout.execute(EnterAlternateScreen)?;
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    install_panic_restore();
    let mut stdout = std::io::stdout();
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    TERMINAL_TAKEN.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    // From here on, any early return (`?`) restores the terminal.
    let _guard = TerminalGuard;
    stdout.execute(EnterAlternateScreen)?;
```

3. At the end of `fn run`, let the guard do the cleanup. `terminal2` is declared after `_guard`, so it is dropped first, while the alternate screen is still active.

Find this code in `src/tui/mod.rs`:
```rust
    disable_raw_mode()?;
    terminal2.backend_mut().execute(LeaveAlternateScreen)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    // `_guard` restores the terminal when this function returns.
    Ok(())
}
```

No automatic test can drive a real terminal. This test checks the "restore once" rule without writing escape codes. Add this test at the very end of `src/tui/tests.rs`, after the closing `}` of the last test:

```rust
    fn terminal_restore_runs_once_per_take() {
        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
        super::TERMINAL_TAKEN.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        assert!(super::release_terminal(), "first restore does the work");
        assert!(!super::release_terminal(), "second restore is a no-op");
        assert!(!super::TERMINAL_TAKEN.load(Ordering::SeqCst));
    }
```

### B-17 · Make the `..\evil.rs` test assertion correct on every OS

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |

#### What is wrong

The test `resolve_rejects_absolute_and_parent_escapes` expects `resolve_in_workspace(ws, "..\\evil.rs")` to fail. That is only true on Windows, where `\` separates path parts, so the path really contains `..`. On Linux and macOS, `\` is an ordinary character. There `..\evil.rs` is one file name inside the workspace, `resolve_in_workspace` returns `Ok`, and the test fails. It is the only failing test in `cargo test` on Linux today.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/inline_edit.rs`:

```rust
        assert!(resolve_in_workspace(ws, "").is_err());

```

#### Why it matters

A test that always fails on Linux hides new failures. A CI job on Linux (H-03) would be red from the start. The code itself is safe on both systems; only the test is wrong.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/inline_edit.rs`. In `mod tests`, find the test `resolve_rejects_absolute_and_parent_escapes` (around line 209) and its `..\\evil.rs` line.

Replace it with:

```rust
        assert!(resolve_in_workspace(ws, "").is_err());
        // `\` separates path parts only on Windows. On Linux/macOS
        // `..\evil.rs` is one ordinary file name: it may be refused, or
        // resolved to that one name inside the workspace — never outside.
        if cfg!(windows) {
            assert!(resolve_in_workspace(ws, "..\\evil.rs").is_err());
        } else if let Ok(p) = resolve_in_workspace(ws, "..\\evil.rs") {
            assert_eq!(p.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()), Some("..\\evil.rs"));
        }
        assert!(resolve_in_workspace(ws, "a/../b.rs").is_err(), "even contained .. is rejected");
```

### B-18 · /team: plan-mode gate, subtask cap, honest fallback, abort status

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/team.rs` |
| Read first | `src/team.rs` (whole file); `src/tui/state.rs`: `TeamState::feed_line`, `fn parse_worker_line` |

#### What is wrong

1. `/team` runs in plan mode too, and its workers get every tool (`allow: None`). So a session in read-only plan mode can still edit files through `/team`.
2. The planner is asked for 1–4 subtasks, but nothing enforces it. 30 subtasks start 30 parallel agents.
3. When the planner's reply has no usable JSON, the fallback subtask's instructions are the planner's own text, not the user's goal.
4. The JSON is cut from the first `[` to the last `]`, so any bracket in the surrounding prose ("see [1]") breaks parsing.
5. An aborted worker is reported as `done`. A crashed worker loses its title. Errors print with `{e}` and lose their cause chain. Summaries have no size cap.
6. Workers are never told that nobody can answer their questions, and they do not get the project's AGENTS.md.

Find this code in `src/team.rs`:
```rust
    // Fallback: single subtask = the whole goal.
    vec![Subtask { title: "task".into(), instructions: text.chars().take(2000).collect() }]
}
```

#### Why it matters

Plan mode is the user's "do not touch my files" switch, and `/team` silently ignores it. An unbounded planner reply starts dozens of file-editing agents at once.

<!-- TASK:B-19 -->
### B-19 · MCP: startup can hang; provider-safe tool names; output cap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/mcp.rs` |
| Read first | `src/mcp.rs`: `Client::list_tools`, `Client::call_tool`, `sanitize_server`, `tool_fn_name`, `parse_fn_name`, `McpConn::spawn`, `Registry::start_all`, `Registry::call` |

#### What is wrong

1. Tool names reach the model as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. The tool part is used as is, but OpenAI-style APIs accept only `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`. One tool named `read.file`, or one long name, makes the provider reject the WHOLE request, so no tool works.
2. Tool results have no size limit, so one MCP call can flood the model's context.
3. Two tools with the same model-facing name silently shadow each other.
4. `tools/list` has no time limit (only `initialize` and `tools/call` do). A server that never answers hangs startup forever.
5. `Registry::start_all` starts servers one after another, so slow servers add up.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/mcp.rs`:
```rust
/// The model-facing function name for an MCP tool.
pub fn tool_fn_name(server: &str, tool: &str) -> String {
    format!("mcp__{}__{}", sanitize_server(server), tool)
}
```

#### Why it matters

One badly behaved or oddly named MCP server can freeze opencode-rust at startup, or break every request to the model.

#### Steps

**Stage 1: safe names and capped results**

3. Replace `pub fn sanitize_server` and `pub fn tool_fn_name` (around line 159). This adds the new helpers `cap_result` and `short_hash`. The new `tool_fn_name` turns every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` into `_`. When the tool name had to change, or the result would be longer than 64 characters, it appends `_` plus an 8-digit hash of the real name, so two tools never share a name. Names that are already fine stay exactly as before (`mcp__srv__do_thing`).

Find this code in `src/mcp.rs`:
```rust
/// Server names become part of a function name: keep [A-Za-z0-9-], fold the
/// rest to `-`, so `mcp__<server>__<tool>` parsing stays unambiguous.
pub fn sanitize_server(name: &str) -> String {
    name.chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' { c } else { '-' })
        .collect()
}

/// The model-facing function name for an MCP tool.
pub fn tool_fn_name(server: &str, tool: &str) -> String {
    format!("mcp__{}__{}", sanitize_server(server), tool)
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Cut an over-long tool result to MAX_RESULT_BYTES (B-19).
fn cap_result(text: String) -> String {
    if text.len() <= MAX_RESULT_BYTES {
        return text;
    }
    let mut cut = MAX_RESULT_BYTES;
    while !text.is_char_boundary(cut) {
        cut -= 1;
    }
    format!("{}\n… [mcp result truncated: {} bytes in total]", &text[..cut], text.len())
}

/// Server names become part of a function name: keep [A-Za-z0-9-], fold the
/// rest to `-`, so `mcp__<server>__<tool>` parsing stays unambiguous.
/// B-19: at most MAX_SERVER_PART characters, so the tool part has room.
pub fn sanitize_server(name: &str) -> String {
    name.chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' { c } else { '-' })
        .take(MAX_SERVER_PART)
        .collect()
}

/// Short, stable hash (FNV-1a, 32 bit): same input, same output, every run.
fn short_hash(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut h: u32 = 0x811c_9dc5;
    for b in s.bytes() {
        h ^= b as u32;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
    }
    format!("{h:08x}")
}

/// The model-facing function name for an MCP tool, always matching
/// `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (B-19). [`resolve_tool_name`] maps it back.
pub fn tool_fn_name(server: &str, tool: &str) -> String {
    let prefix = format!("mcp__{}__", sanitize_server(server));
    let clean: String = tool
        .chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '-' { c } else { '_' })
        .collect();
    let full = format!("{prefix}{clean}");
    if clean == tool && !clean.is_empty() && full.len() <= MAX_FN_NAME {
        return full;
    }
    // Room for the readable part: 64 minus the prefix, minus "_" + 8 hex digits.
    let room = MAX_FN_NAME - prefix.len() - 9;
    let head: String = clean.chars().take(room).collect();
    format!("{prefix}{head}_{}", short_hash(tool))
}
```

```rust
pub fn parse_fn_name(fn_name: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    let rest = fn_name.strip_prefix("mcp__")?;
    let (server, tool) = rest.split_once("__")?;
    if server.is_empty() || tool.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some((server.to_string(), tool.to_string()))
}

/// The real MCP tool name behind the tool part of `mcp__<server>__<part>`
/// (B-19). Falls back to `part` itself when no tool matches.
pub fn resolve_tool_name(server: &str, tools: &[McpTool], part: &str) -> String {
    let wanted = format!("mcp__{server}__{part}");
    tools
        .iter()
        .find(|t| tool_fn_name(server, &t.name) == wanted)
        .map(|t| t.name.clone())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| part.to_string())
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    pub async fn start_all(&mut self, servers: &[McpServerCfg]) {
        // B-19: all servers start at the same time; each start is bounded by
        // the initialize and tools/list time limits.
        let mut starts = Vec::new();
        let mut planned = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for cfg in servers {
            if cfg.name.is_empty() || cfg.command.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let key = sanitize_server(&cfg.name);
            if self.conns.contains_key(&key) {
                continue; // already running
            }
            if !planned.insert(key.clone()) {
                eprintln!("[mcp] skipping `{}`: another server already uses the name `{key}`", cfg.name);
                continue;
            }
            starts.push(async move { (key, cfg, McpConn::spawn(&cfg.name, cfg).await) });
        }
        for (key, cfg, result) in futures::future::join_all(starts).await {
            match result {
                Ok(conn) => {
                    eprintln!(
                        "[mcp] {} connected ({} tool(s))",
                        conn.server,
                        conn.tools.len()
                    );
                    self.conns.insert(key, conn);
                }
                Err(e) => eprintln!("[mcp] failed to start `{}`: {e:#}", cfg.name),
            }
        }
    }
```

### B-20 · MCP: one global lock serializes every call

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-19 (uses its `resolve_tool_name`) |
| Files to change | `src/mcp.rs`, `src/server.rs` |
| Read first | `src/mcp.rs`: `pub struct McpConn`, `McpConn::spawn`, `McpConn::call`, `impl Registry`; `src/server.rs`: `async fn execute_routed` |

#### What is wrong

All MCP servers live in one `Registry` behind one async mutex (`pub mcp: AsyncMutex<crate::mcp::Registry>` in `AppState`). `execute_routed` holds that lock for the WHOLE tool call, which can last up to 300 seconds. While one call runs, every other MCP call in every session, subagent and team worker waits. Every new agent turn also waits, because `run_loop` locks the registry to list the MCP tools. MCP calls also ignore the abort flag.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
    if crate::mcp::parse_fn_name(name).is_some() {
        return match st.mcp.lock().await.call(name, input).await {
            Ok(out) => (out, true),
            Err(e) => (format!("error: {e:#}"), false),
        };
    }
```

#### Why it matters

One slow MCP tool (a long search, a stuck server) freezes all parallel work: spawned subagents, `/team` workers and other sessions stop dead until it finishes or times out. Pressing stop does not help.

#### Steps

How the fix works: each server gets its own lock around its process pipe (new struct `Live`). The registry lock is held only for the moment it takes to look up a server; the new method `Registry::route` returns a handle (new struct `McpRoute`) that makes the call with the registry unlocked. Calls to the SAME server still take turns, because they share one pipe; calls to different servers run at the same time.

Apply B-19 first.

### B-21 · Provider stream: error frames, early end, missing delta, ids, `content: null`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/provider.rs` |
| Read first | `src/provider.rs`: `struct ChatMsg`, `struct SseChunk`, `struct SseChoice`, `fn sse_event_stream`, `fn parse_sse_line`, `struct ToolCallAccumulator` |

#### What is wrong

1. **Error frames are dropped.** Providers report a failure mid-stream as `data: {"error": {...}}`. `parse_sse_line` does `serde_json::from_str(data).ok()?`, so the reply just stops.
2. **An early end looks like success.** If the connection closes before `[DONE]` (dead tunnel, crashed backend), the stream ends quietly, and half a reply is taken as complete.
3. **Required fields that are optional in practice.** `SseChoice.delta` is required, so a last chunk like `{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop"}]}` is dropped together with its finish reason.
4. **Tool call ids.** A server that sends no `id` produces `tool_call_id: ""`. A server that sends every parallel call as `index: 0` gets the calls glued together into broken JSON.
5. **`content` is left out.** `ChatMsg` skips `content` when it is `None`. Assistant messages that only carry tool calls then have no `content` key, which some OpenAI-compatible servers reject.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/provider.rs`:
```rust
    let chunk: SseChunk = serde_json::from_str(data).ok()?;
    let mut events = Vec::new();
    for choice in &chunk.choices {
```

```rust
/// The message of a mid-stream error frame such as
/// `data: {"error": {"message": "..."}}` (B-21), or `None` for other lines.
fn sse_error_message(line: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let data = line.strip_prefix("data:")?.trim();
    if !data.starts_with('{') || !data.contains("\"error\"") {
        return None;
    }
    let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(data).ok()?;
    let err = v.get("error").filter(|e| !e.is_null())?;
    let msg = err
        .get("message")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .map(str::to_string)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| err.to_string());
    Some(msg.chars().take(400).collect())
}
```

```rust
            let entry = self.calls.entry(*index).or_default();
            if let Some(id) = id {

                    entry.0 = id.clone();
                }
            }
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    pub fn push(&mut self, ev: &StreamEvent) {
        if let StreamEvent::ToolCallDelta { index, id, name, args_delta } = ev {
            let new_id = id.as_deref().filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
            // B-21: some servers send every call as `index: 0`. A different id
            // on a known index means a new call, not more of the old one.
            let slot = match self.slot_of.get(index).copied() {
                Some(s) => {
                    let known = self.calls.get(&s).map(|c| c.0.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
                    let other_call = matches!(new_id, Some(n) if !known.is_empty() && known != n);
                    if other_call { self.new_slot(*index) } else { s }
                }
                None => self.new_slot(*index),
            };
            let entry = self.calls.entry(slot).or_default();
            if let Some(n) = new_id {
                entry.0 = n.to_string();
            }
            if let Some(name) = name {
                if !name.is_empty() {
                    entry.1 = name.clone();
                }
            }
            entry.2.push_str(args_delta);
        }
    }

    /// B-21: start a new call slot for provider `index`.
    fn new_slot(&mut self, index: usize) -> usize {
        let slot = self.next_slot;
        self.next_slot += 1;
        self.slot_of.insert(index, slot);
        slot
    }
```

```rust
    /// Returns final calls; args parsed as JSON (falls back to {"raw": args}).
    /// B-21: empty args become `{}`; a missing id gets a generated one.
    pub fn finish(self) -> Vec<(String, String, Value)> {
        self.calls
            .into_values()
            .map(|(id, name, args)| {
                let v = if args.trim().is_empty() {
                    json!({})
                } else {
                    serde_json::from_str(&args).unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({ "raw": args }))
                };
                let id = if id.is_empty() { crate::db::new_id("call") } else { id };
                (id, name, v)
            })
            .collect()
    }
```

### B-22 · Write/edit approvals must show what will change

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-09 (only the order: apply B-09 first if you do both; both edit `check_permission`) |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/gui.rs` (two test constructors) |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `enum ServerEvent` (`ApprovalNeeded`), `fn tool_detail`, `fn check_permission`, the tool loop in `fn run_loop`; `src/tools.rs`: the `write` and `edit` tool specs (keys `content`, `old_str`, `new_str`) |

#### What is wrong

For `write` and `edit`, the approval prompt shows only the file path. `tool_detail` turns the call into the text that permission rules match on, and for file tools that text is the path. So the user approves (or picks "always") without seeing what will be written. "Always" then allows any future content for that path.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
        "read" | "write" | "edit" | "glob" | "grep" => {
            let p = input.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
            normalize_path_detail(&st.workspace, p)
        }
```

#### Why it matters

A model that was misled by a file or a web page can overwrite `src/main.rs` or a config file with harmful content. The user cannot notice it at the prompt, because all they see is "write src/main.rs".

#### Steps

How the fix works. `detail` stays exactly as it is: it is the key that permission rules and "always allow" match on. A new `preview` string shows what will change: the first lines of the new content for `write`, and old and new lines for `edit`. It travels in a new field of `ApprovalNeeded`. It is also sent as a `Note` right before the prompt, so the TUI, the GUI and the headless output all show it today. Tasks B-13 (GUI) and B-15 (TUI) can later show `preview` inside the modal.

```rust
/// New (B-22): what a `write`/`edit` call will change, for the approval
/// prompt. Empty for other tools (their `detail` already says it all).
pub fn approval_preview(tool: &str, input: &Value) -> String {
    const MAX_LINES: usize = 40;
    const MAX_CHARS: usize = 4_000;
    let field = |k: &str| input.get(k).and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let mut out = String::new();
    match tool {
        "write" => {
            let content = field("content");
            out.push_str(&format!(
                "write {} — {} line(s), {} byte(s)\n",
                field("path"),
                content.lines().count(),
                content.len()
            ));
            push_prefixed(&mut out, "+ ", content, MAX_LINES);
        }
        "edit" => {
            let all = input.get("replace_all").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false);
            out.push_str(&format!("edit {}{}\n", field("path"), if all { " (every match)" } else { "" }));
            push_prefixed(&mut out, "- ", field("old_str"), MAX_LINES / 2);
            push_prefixed(&mut out, "+ ", field("new_str"), MAX_LINES / 2);
        }
        _ => return String::new(),
    }
    if out.len() > MAX_CHARS {
        let mut cut = MAX_CHARS;
        while !out.is_char_boundary(cut) {
            cut -= 1;
        }
        out.truncate(cut);
        out.push_str("\n… (preview cut)");
    }
    out
}

/// New (B-22): append up to `max_lines` lines of `text`, each with `prefix`.
fn push_prefixed(out: &mut String, prefix: &str, text: &str, max_lines: usize) {
    let total = text.lines().count();
    for line in text.lines().take(max_lines) {
        out.push_str(prefix);
        out.push_str(line);
        out.push('\n');
    }
    if total > max_lines {
        out.push_str(&format!("  … {} more line(s)\n", total - max_lines));
    }
}

/// Returns true if the tool call may proceed; blocks on an approval prompt when needed.
/// (No preview. The run loop calls `check_permission_preview`.)

    st: &Shared,
    session_id: &str,
    tool: &str,
    detail: &str,
    abort: &AtomicBool,
```

### B-23 · TUI subscribes to events too late (startup race)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/main.rs`: the start of `fn tui_run` up to the "SSE forwarder task" |

#### What is wrong

`opencode-rust "some prompt"` starts the TUI and sends the prompt right away. `fn tui_run` starts that run with `state.kick_run(...)` first and only a few lines later subscribes to the event bus (`state.events.subscribe()` in the "SSE forwarder task"). A broadcast channel only delivers events to receivers that already exist. So events sent in between are lost, for example the first text pieces, or a fast `RunFinished` when the provider refuses the connection. The headless mode does it right: it subscribes before it starts the run.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/main.rs`:
```rust

        app.push(tui::EntryKind::User, format!("> {p}"));
        app.busy = true;
        state.kick_run(session.id.clone(), p).await;
    }
```

#### Why it matters

When the very first event is lost (typically a quick error), the TUI shows "busy" forever and no error message, and the user does not know what happened.

#### Steps

### B-24 · Turbo: one run until the last continuation, and a cap that really holds

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-06 |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn turbo_streak`, `fn spawn_kick_run`, the end of `fn run_agent`, `fn run_review` |

#### What is wrong

In turbo mode, a run that ends with open todos starts a "continuation" run by itself, at most `TURBO_MAX_CONTINUATIONS` (8) times in a row.

1. `run_agent` sends `RunFinished` first and starts the continuation afterwards. The headless loop exits on the first `RunFinished`, so in `--headless` the continuation is dropped, although it prints "runs continue on their own". The TUI and GUI see a `RunFinished` between every continuation.
2. The cap does not hold. `turbo_streak` counts the trailing `TURBO-CONTINUE:` user messages and stops counting at any other user message. But the automatic review (`run_review`, on by default) adds its own user message ("Review the current uncommitted changes …") after every run that changed files. The streak is therefore reset after every continuation, so a turbo run with open todos can loop forever.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
        let is_continue = m.parts.iter().any(|p| {
            matches!(p, Part::Text { text } if text.starts_with(TURBO_CONTINUE_PREFIX))
        });
        if is_continue {
            streak += 1;
        } else {
            break;
        }
```

#### Why it matters

An endless turbo loop keeps running model calls (and tools with full access) until someone notices, which is real cost and risk. In headless mode the advertised "keep working on its own" simply does not happen.

#### Steps

How the fix works. A continuation is part of the same run. `run_agent` decides on it before it announces anything, registers it in `busy` (with `claim_run` from B-06), starts it, and sends no `RunFinished` in between. Clients see one run that ends when the last continuation ends, so the headless loop works without any change. The review prompt no longer breaks the streak.

```rust
/// Fire-and-forget wrapper around [`AppState::kick_run`]. Deliberately NOT
/// async: `run_agent` → `kick_run` → `run_agent` would otherwise make their
/// future types recursive (E0391). A sync call keeps the cycle broken.
fn spawn_kick_run(st: Shared, session_id: String, user_content: String) {

        st.kick_run(session_id, user_content).await;

}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Fire-and-forget start of a run whose `busy` slot is already claimed
/// (`flag`). Deliberately NOT async: `run_agent` → spawn → `run_agent` would
/// otherwise make their future types recursive (E0391). A sync call keeps
/// the cycle broken. New (B-24): replaces `spawn_kick_run`.
fn spawn_claimed_run(st: Shared, session_id: String, user_content: String, flag: Arc<AtomicBool>) {
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        run_agent(&st, &session_id, &user_content, flag.clone()).await;
        st.release_run(&session_id, &flag).await;
    });
}

/// New (B-24): the prompt for a turbo continuation when this run should go
/// on by itself (turbo on, run ok and not aborted, open todos, streak below
/// the cap), else None. A trailing "?" in the answer does NOT count as more
/// work: asking is the one thing turbo must respect. The model is blocked
/// on the user, and pushing it to "decide for yourself" produces guesses.
fn turbo_continuation(st: &Shared, session_id: &str, result: &Result<String>) -> Option<String> {
    let aborted = matches!(result.as_deref(), Ok("aborted"));
    if !st.turbo() || result.is_err() || aborted {
        return None;
    }
    if !todos_open(st, session_id) || turbo_streak(st, session_id) >= TURBO_MAX_CONTINUATIONS {
        return None;
    }
    Some(format!(
        "{TURBO_CONTINUE_PREFIX} you have full access and must not ask the \
         user anything. Make the most reasonable decision yourself, keep \
         working on the remaining todos until none are open, and finish the job."
    ))
}
```

### B-25 · `/parallel`: real parallelism, current model, no hidden approval waits

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn run_parallel`, `fn build_state_ephemeral`, `fn check_permission`, `fn current_model` |

#### What is wrong

`/parallel <task>` runs one task in two git worktrees (separate checkouts of the repository) and reports both results. Every worker gets a fresh `AppState` from `build_state_ephemeral`:

1. The two workers run one after the other, not in parallel (`for n in 1..=2` awaits each worker).
2. Each worker has its own event bus that nobody listens to. When a tool needs approval (`write`, `bash` by default), the prompt is never shown, and the worker waits the full `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s) per call before it is denied.
3. Workers always start in the default permission mode, even when the session runs in turbo.
4. Workers use `cfg.provider.model`, not the model chosen with `/model`.
5. The report does not say how to remove the worktrees and branches it leaves behind.
6. Unit tests build their state with `build_state_ephemeral`, which uses the real user state folder. So the `/parallel` tests leave worktree folders there (`parallel/`, plus empty `workers/` folders), and test runs write git snapshots there.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
        let mut cfg = st.cfg.clone();
        cfg.agent.auto_review = false; // no nested reviews in workers
        let worker = build_state_ephemeral(cfg, wt.clone()).await;
```

#### Why it matters

With the default config, a `/parallel` run that needs to edit files spends 5 minutes per refused tool call and still produces nothing, and it takes twice as long as needed. Users then conclude the feature is broken.

### B-27 · Subagents: abort shown as done, children told to ask questions, no spawn limit

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/subagent.rs` |
| Read first | `src/subagent.rs`: `fn spawn_spec`, `fn spawn_subagent`; `src/agents.rs`: `fn compose_system` (the "When to act" section) |

#### What is wrong

1. **No limit.** In one turn the model can emit any number of `spawn` calls, and `run_loop` runs them all at once with `join_all`. Each child is a full agent run of up to `max_steps` provider calls.
2. **Abort shows as done.** When the user aborts, `run_loop` returns `Ok("aborted")`. `spawn_subagent` treats that as success: the agents panel shows "done", and the parent gets "aborted" as if it were the child's summary.
3. **Children are told to ask questions.** `compose_system` always adds "If a request is ambiguous, ask one short clarifying question instead of guessing." A subagent has nobody to ask, so it may end with a question instead of doing the task.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/subagent.rs`:
```rust

    let mut summary = summary;
    if summary.chars().count() > 4000 {
```

#### Why it matters

A model that answers "split this into tasks" with 20 spawns starts 20 agents at once (cost, rate limits, files edited in parallel). After an abort, the panel claims the work is done.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/subagent.rs`. Find the end of `pub fn spawn_spec` (around line 35). Add the new limit and the new slot counter right after the function.

```rust
/// Most subagents one parent session may run at the same time (B-27).
pub const MAX_RUNNING_SUBAGENTS: usize = 4;

/// Running children per parent session (B-27).
fn running() -> &'static std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::HashMap<String, usize>> {
    static RUNNING: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::HashMap<String, usize>>> =
        std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    RUNNING.get_or_init(Default::default)
}

/// One running child (B-27). The slot is given back when this value is
/// dropped, also on error, abort or panic.
struct SpawnSlot(String);

impl SpawnSlot {
    fn take(parent: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut map = running().lock().map_err(|_| anyhow!("subagent counter is poisoned"))?;
        let count = map.entry(parent.to_string()).or_insert(0);
        if *count >= MAX_RUNNING_SUBAGENTS {
            return Err(anyhow!(
                "too many subagents at once: at most {MAX_RUNNING_SUBAGENTS} can run for this \
                 session. Wait for their results, then spawn the rest."
            ));
        }
        *count += 1;
        Ok(SpawnSlot(parent.to_string()))
    }
}

impl Drop for SpawnSlot {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Ok(mut map) = running().lock() {
            if let Some(count) = map.get_mut(&self.0) {
                *count = count.saturating_sub(1);
                if *count == 0 {
                    map.remove(&self.0);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### B-28 · MCP protocol gaps: server requests, null fields, pagination, cancel-safe reads

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-19 (uses its `list_tools_within` and its `limit` parameter) |
| Files to change | `src/mcp.rs` |
| Read first | `src/mcp.rs`: `struct McpTool`, `struct Client`, `Client::request`, `Client::list_tools` |

#### What is wrong

1. **Wrong reply matching.** `Client::request` takes the first message whose `id` equals its own as the answer. A request FROM the server (for example `ping`) that uses the same id number is taken as the reply and returns `null`. Server requests are never answered, so a server that waits for its `ping` reply stalls.
2. **Fragile tool list.** `"description": null` fails to parse (`#[serde(default)]` only covers a missing field), and one bad entry fails the whole list, so the server is dropped. `tools/list` pages (`nextCursor`) are ignored, so tools after the first page are lost.
3. **Lost data on timeout.** `read_line` is not cancel-safe. When a timeout cancels a read halfway through a line, the part already read is thrown away.
4. **Unclear errors for a stopped server.** When a server process exits, calls fail with "closed its stdout" and nothing says how to recover. There is no automatic restart. Name collisions between servers are reported by task B-19.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/mcp.rs`:
```rust
            if msg.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64) != Some(id) {
                continue; // notification or another id
            }
```

#### Why it matters

Real MCP servers send pings and paginate long tool lists, and sometimes they leave optional fields `null`. Today each of these silently loses a server or its tools.

#### Steps

Apply B-19 first.

**Stage 1: replies, server requests and cancel-safe reads**

Open `src/mcp.rs`.

4. Replace the read loop of `request` (right below). The new loop:
   - reads with `read_until` into `self.line`;
   - answers requests coming FROM the server: `ping` gets an empty result, anything else gets "method not found";
   - ignores server notifications;
   - accepts a message as the reply only when it has our id and no `method`.

Find this code in `src/mcp.rs`:
```rust
        loop {
            let mut line = String::new();
            let n = self.reader.read_line(&mut line).await?;
            if n == 0 {
                return Err(anyhow!("mcp server closed its stdout during `{method}`"));
            }
            let Ok(msg) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line.trim()) else {
                continue; // non-JSON noise on stdout: ignore
            };
            if msg.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64) != Some(id) {
                continue; // notification or another id
            }
            if let Some(err) = msg.get("error") {

            }
            return Ok(msg.get("result").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null));
        }
```

Replace it with:
```rust
        loop {
            let n = self.reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut self.line).await?;
            if n == 0 {
                return Err(anyhow!(
                    "mcp server closed its stdout during `{method}` (the server process has \
                     probably exited; restart opencode-rust to reconnect it)"
                ));
            }
            if self.line.last() != Some(&b'\n') {
                continue; // end of stream inside a line; the next read returns 0
            }
            let raw = std::mem::take(&mut self.line);
            let Ok(msg) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&raw) else {
                continue; // non-JSON noise on stdout: ignore
            };
            // B-28: a message with a `method` comes FROM the server.
            if let Some(server_method) = msg.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                if let Some(req_id) = msg.get("id").cloned() {
                    let reply = if server_method == "ping" {
                        json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": req_id, "result": {} })
                    } else {
                        json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": req_id, "error": {
                            "code": -32601,
                            "message": format!("`{server_method}` is not supported by this client")
                        }})
                    };
                    self.write_msg(&reply).await?;
                }
                continue; // requests are answered, notifications ignored
            }
            if msg.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64) != Some(id) {
                continue; // a reply to an older, timed-out request
            }
            if let Some(err) = msg.get("error") {
                return Err(anyhow!("mcp `{method}` failed: {err}"));
            }
            return Ok(msg.get("result").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null));
        }
```

```rust
                    json!({"tools": [{"name": "c", "description": null}]})
                } else {
                    json!({"tools": [{"name": "a", "description": null}, {"description": "no name"}, {"name": "b"}],
                           "nextCursor": "p2"})
                };
                send(&mut ws, json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": req["id"], "result": result})).await;
            }
        });
        let tools = client.list_tools().await.unwrap();
        let names: Vec<&str> = tools.iter().map(|t| t.name.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, vec!["a", "b", "c"]);
        assert_eq!(tools[0].description, "");
        drop(client);
        let _ = server.await;
    }
}
```

### B-29 · The client lock is held while waiting for the provider

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/provider.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `src/compact.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `pub client: AsyncMutex<Client>` in `AppState`, `pub async fn one_shot`, `pub async fn run_loop`, `available_models`; `src/compact.rs`: `async fn summarize` |

#### What is wrong

`AppState.client` is one `provider::Client` behind an async mutex. Every caller does `let client = st.client.lock().await;`, then `client.stream(...).await`, and only then `drop(client)`. `stream()` waits until the provider sends its response headers, and many servers only do that after reading the whole prompt (the prefill). `available_models` holds the lock for a whole `GET /models`. So parallel subagents, `/team` workers and other sessions queue up behind each other's slowest request.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
        let client = st.client.lock().await;
        let mut stream = client.stream(&client.model, &msgs, &specs).await?;
        drop(client);
```

#### Why it matters

With a slow local model, the "parallel" workers of `/team` and `spawn` effectively start one at a time, and `/model` freezes while a run is starting.

#### Steps

How the fix works: `provider::Client` holds a `reqwest::Client` (cheap to copy: the copy shares the same connection pool) plus a few strings. Copy it out of the lock, release the lock at once, then make the request with the copy. `/model <id>` still changes the shared client, so the next request uses the new model.

1. Open `src/provider.rs`. Find `pub struct Client` (around line 8) and let it be copied.

Find this code in `src/provider.rs`:
```rust

```

```rust
/// Cheap to clone (B-29): the inner reqwest client shares its pool.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Client {
```

```rust
                ([(axum::http::header::CONTENT_TYPE, "text/event-stream")], payload)
```

<!-- TASK:B-30 -->
### B-30 · read tool: binary detection, memory use, offset meaning, very long lines

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none (if S-03 is applied, the first line of `fn read_file` reads `confine_path` instead of `resolve`; this task does not touch that line) |
| Files to change | `src/tools.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tools.rs`: `fn read_file`, the `"read"` entry in `fn tool_specs` |

#### What is wrong

1. `read_file` uses `std::fs::read_to_string`, which fails on any file that is not valid UTF-8. A real binary file therefore gives a raw "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" error, not the friendly `(binary file)` message the next lines try to produce. A Latin-1 text file cannot be read at all.
2. The whole file is loaded before `limit` applies, with no size check. A 2 GB log is loaded completely to show 2,000 lines.
3. `offset` means "lines to skip" (0-based), but the numbers the tool prints start at 1. A model that passes the number it saw as `offset` starts one line too late.
4. Lines are never cut. One minified 5 MB line is returned whole and fills the model's context.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&abs).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", abs.display()))?;
    if text.bytes().any(|b| b == 0) {
        return Ok(format!("(binary file: {path})"));
    }
```

#### Why it matters

Small local models have small contexts. One huge line or one huge file can push everything else out, and the off-by-one makes the model miss the exact line it wanted to see.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/tools.rs`. Find the `"read"` entry in `fn tool_specs` (around line 22) and describe the arguments.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
        spec(
            "read",
            "Read a text file. Returns numbered lines. For directories, use list instead.",
```

Replace it with:
```rust
        spec(
            "read",
            "Read a text file. Returns numbered lines. offset = first line number to show (1-based, as printed); limit = how many lines (default 2000). For directories, use list instead.",
```

2. Find the rest of `fn read_file`, from the `read_to_string` line to the end of the function (around line 185). Replace it with the version below. It adds two new constants and the new helper `cap_line` after the function.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&abs).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", abs.display()))?;
    if text.bytes().any(|b| b == 0) {
        return Ok(format!("(binary file: {path})"));
    }
    let limit = limit.clamp(1, 10_000) as usize;
    let offset = offset.max(0) as usize;
    let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
    let slice: Vec<String> = lines
        .iter()
        .skip(offset)
        .take(limit)
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, l)| format!("{:>6}\t{}", offset + i + 1, l))
        .collect();
    let mut out = slice.join("\n");
    if offset + limit < lines.len() {
        out.push_str(&format!("\n… [{} more lines]", lines.len() - offset - limit));
    }
    Ok(out)
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    // B-30: refuse huge files before loading them.
    let size = std::fs::metadata(&abs).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", abs.display()))?.len();
    if size > READ_MAX_BYTES {
        bail!(
            "{path} is {size} bytes, too big for the read tool (limit {READ_MAX_BYTES}). \
             Use grep to find the part you need, or bash with head/tail."
        );
    }
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&abs).with_context(|| format!("reading {}", abs.display()))?;
    // B-30: a NUL byte near the start means binary. Other text is shown even
    // when it is not valid UTF-8 (bad bytes become the � character).
    if bytes.iter().take(8192).any(|&b| b == 0) {
        return Ok(format!("(binary file: {path}, {size} bytes)"));
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes);
    let note = if matches!(text, std::borrow::Cow::Owned(_)) {
        "\n… [note: this file is not valid UTF-8; bad bytes are shown as �. The edit tool cannot change it.]"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    let limit = limit.clamp(1, 10_000) as usize;
    // B-30: `offset` is the first line shown, 1-based like the printed
    // numbers; 0 and 1 both mean "from the top".
    let skip = (offset.max(1) - 1) as usize;
    let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
    let slice: Vec<String> = lines
        .iter()
        .skip(skip)
        .take(limit)
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, l)| format!("{:>6}\t{}", skip + i + 1, cap_line(l)))
        .collect();
    let mut out = slice.join("\n");
    if skip + limit < lines.len() {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "\n… [{} more lines; continue with offset {}]",
            lines.len() - skip - limit,
            skip + limit + 1
        ));
    }
    out.push_str(note);
    Ok(out)
}

/// Largest file the read tool loads, in bytes (B-30).
const READ_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 20_000_000;
/// Longest line the read tool shows, in characters (B-30).
const READ_MAX_LINE_CHARS: usize = 2000;

/// Cut one very long line, for example in a minified file (B-30).
fn cap_line(line: &str) -> std::borrow::Cow<'_, str> {
    if line.chars().count() <= READ_MAX_LINE_CHARS {
        std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(line)
    } else {
        let head: String = line.chars().take(READ_MAX_LINE_CHARS).collect();
        std::borrow::Cow::Owned(format!("{head}… [line cut at {READ_MAX_LINE_CHARS} characters]"))
    }
}
```

<!-- TASK:B-31 -->
### B-31 · write/edit: atomic writes and a correct "created/wrote" message

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/tools.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tools.rs`: `fn write_file`, `fn edit_file` |

#### What is wrong

1. `write_file` and `edit_file` write with `std::fs::write`, which first empties the file and then writes the new bytes. If the process is killed, the disk fills up, or the power goes out in between, the file is left empty or half written.
2. `write_file` decides between "created" and "wrote" with `std::fs::read_to_string(&abs).ok()`. For an existing file that is not valid UTF-8 (or not readable), that gives `None`, so the tool says "created" although it just overwrote a file. It also reads the whole old file only to get its size.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
    let existing = std::fs::read_to_string(&abs).ok();
    std::fs::write(&abs, content).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", abs.display()))?;
```

#### Why it matters

A half-written source file breaks the build in confusing ways. A wrong "created" message hides the fact that an existing file was replaced, so neither the model nor the user notices.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/tools.rs`. Find the end of `fn write_file` (around line 211). Replace it with the version below, which adds the new helper `write_atomic`. The helper writes a temporary file next to the target and then renames it over the target in one step. It keeps the old file's permissions (for example the executable bit), refuses read-only files, and falls back to a normal write if the rename is refused. On Windows that happens when another program holds the file open.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
    let existing = std::fs::read_to_string(&abs).ok();
    std::fs::write(&abs, content).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", abs.display()))?;
    let bytes = content.len();
    Ok(match existing {
        Some(old) => {
            let delta = content.len() as i64 - old.len() as i64;
            format!("wrote {path} ({bytes} bytes, {delta:+} bytes vs previous)")
        }
        None => format!("created {path} ({bytes} bytes)"),
    })
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    // B-31: the old size from metadata (works for any file, reads nothing).
    let old_len = std::fs::metadata(&abs).ok().filter(|m| m.is_file()).map(|m| m.len());
    write_atomic(&abs, content.as_bytes()).with_context(|| format!("writing {}", abs.display()))?;
    let bytes = content.len();
    Ok(match old_len {
        Some(old) => {
            let delta = bytes as i64 - old as i64;
            format!("wrote {path} ({bytes} bytes, {delta:+} bytes vs previous)")
        }
        None => format!("created {path} ({bytes} bytes)"),
    })
}

/// Write a file so it is never left half written (B-31): write a
/// temporary file in the same folder, then rename it over the target.
/// Keeps the old permissions, refuses read-only files, and falls back to
/// a plain write when the rename is refused (Windows, file held open).
fn write_atomic(path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    static COUNTER: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
    let old_perms = std::fs::metadata(path).ok().map(|m| m.permissions());
    if old_perms.as_ref().map(|p| p.readonly()).unwrap_or(false) {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied, "the file is read-only"));
    }
    let n = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    let dir = path.parent().unwrap_or_else(|| Path::new("."));
    let name = path.file_name().map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
    let tmp = dir.join(format!(".{name}.ocrs-{}-{n}.tmp", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::write(&tmp, data)?;
    if let Some(perms) = old_perms {
        let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&tmp, perms);
    }
    match std::fs::rename(&tmp, path) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(_) => {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
            std::fs::write(path, data)
        }
    }
}
```

2. In `fn edit_file`, find the write (around line 246) and use the same helper.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:

```rust
    let lines_before = text.matches('\n').count();
    let lines_after = new_text.matches('\n').count();
```

Replace it with:

```rust
    let lines_before = text.matches('\n').count();
    let lines_after = new_text.matches('\n').count();
```

#### Do not

- Do not write the temporary file to the system temp folder. A rename only works within one drive/file system, so it must sit next to the target.
- Do not delete the target before the rename. `std::fs::rename` replaces an existing target in one call on Windows and on Unix, so there is no moment without the file.

### B-32 · glob/grep: same path style, `{a,b}`, correct `**/`, skip `.git`, report skipped files

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/tools.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tools.rs`: `fn glob_files`, `fn match_glob`, `fn grep_files` |

#### What is wrong

1. `glob` prints paths relative to the folder it searched (`path` argument), while `grep` prints them relative to the workspace. After `glob("*.rs", path="src")` the model gets `main.rs`, and `read("main.rs")` then fails.
2. Brace patterns like `**/*.{rs,toml}` are not supported and quietly match nothing.
3. In `match_glob`, `**/x` retries at every character instead of only after a `/`, so `**/x.rs` also matches `foox.rs`.
4. Both tools walk with `hidden(false)` and so walk into `.git` too, which can hold credentials in remote URLs (`.git/config`).
5. `grep` silently skips files over 2 MB and files that are not UTF-8 (Latin-1, UTF-16), so "no matches" can be false.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
                    if rest.first() == Some(&b'/') {
                        // `**/x` matches `x` or `any/x`
                        return m(&rest[1..], t) || (0..t.len()).any(|i| m(p, &t[i + 1..]));
                    }
```

#### Why it matters

The model trusts these tools to find code. Wrong paths, false matches and silent gaps make it edit the wrong file or conclude that code does not exist.

#### Steps

**Stage 1: glob**

1. Open `src/tools.rs`. In `fn glob_files` (around line 258), replace everything from `let mut matches` to the end of the function. This adds the new helper `expand_braces` after it.

Find this code in `src/tools.rs`:
```rust
    let mut matches = Vec::new();
    // require_git(false): honor .gitignore even in non-git workspaces.
    for entry in WalkBuilder::new(&root).hidden(false).require_git(false).build().flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        if !path.is_file() {
            continue;
        }
        let rel = path.strip_prefix(&root).unwrap_or(path);
        let rel_str = rel.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
        if match_glob(pattern, &rel_str) {
            matches.push(rel_str);
            if matches.len() >= 500 {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if matches.is_empty() {
        return Ok(format!("no files matched `{pattern}`"));
    }
    Ok(matches.join("\n"))
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    let mut matches = Vec::new();
    // B-32: `{a,b}` alternatives become separate patterns.
    let patterns = expand_braces(pattern);
    // require_git(false): honor .gitignore even in non-git workspaces.
    // B-32: never walk into `.git`.
    for entry in WalkBuilder::new(&root)
        .hidden(false)
        .require_git(false)
        .filter_entry(|e| e.file_name() != ".git")
        .build()
        .flatten()
    {
        let path = entry.path();
        if !path.is_file() {
            continue;
        }
        // Match relative to the folder that was searched ...
        let rel = path.strip_prefix(&root).unwrap_or(path);
        let rel_str = rel.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
        if patterns.iter().any(|p| match_glob(p, &rel_str)) {
            // ... but print relative to the workspace, like grep (B-32), so
            // the path works directly with read and edit.
            let shown = path.strip_prefix(workspace).unwrap_or(path);
            matches.push(shown.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"));
            if matches.len() >= 500 {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if matches.is_empty() {
        return Ok(format!("no files matched `{pattern}`"));
    }
    Ok(matches.join("\n"))
}

/// Expand `{a,b}` groups into separate glob patterns (B-32). Groups do not
/// nest; a `{` without a closing `}` is kept as plain text.
fn expand_braces(pattern: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(open) = pattern.find('{') else { return vec![pattern.to_string()] };
    let Some(len) = pattern[open..].find('}') else { return vec![pattern.to_string()] };
    let close = open + len;
    let (head, body, tail) = (&pattern[..open], &pattern[open + 1..close], &pattern[close + 1..]);
    body.split(',').flat_map(|alt| expand_braces(&format!("{head}{alt}{tail}"))).collect()
}
```

### B-33 · TUI: keep the busy flag true while a run is going

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/tui/state.rs`, `src/tui/tests.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tui/state.rs`: the `KeyCode::Enter` arm of `fn on_key`, `fn on_mission_key`, `fn on_event` |

#### What is wrong

`App.busy` drives the header spinner, the input placeholder and the cursor. It goes wrong in four ways:

1. After every Enter, `self.busy = busy;` sets it to the command's own value. Typing `/debt`, `/help` or `/plan` during a run therefore shows "ready" while the agent is still working.
2. A mission started from the mission picker never sets `busy`.
3. The replies to `/sessions` and `/model` set `busy = false`, although those commands never started a run.
4. `/team`, `/compact`, `/review`, `/parallel`, `/edit` and `/skill install` typed during a run start a second job next to it. A plain message, by contrast, replaces the run on the server (`kick_run`). The first of the two to finish then clears `busy` while the other still runs.

Find this code in `src/tui/state.rs`:
```rust
                self.busy = busy;
                action
            }
```

The user sees "ready" and types the next request while the agent is still editing files, or starts a compaction in the middle of a run.

```rust
    let idx = idx.trim().parse::<usize>().ok()?;
    // B-34: the error text after `failed:` may contain ") " itself.
    let status = if tail.contains(") failed: ") || tail.ends_with(") failed") {
        TeamStatus::Failed
    } else if tail.ends_with(") done") {
        TeamStatus::Done
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    Some((idx, status))
}
```

### B-35 · TUI input: Ctrl/Alt keys, pasting, long lines, wide characters

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-16 |
| Files to change | `src/tui/mod.rs`, `src/tui/state.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `src/tui/draw.rs`, `src/tui/tests.rs` |
| Read first | `src/tui/mod.rs`: `fn run`; `src/tui/state.rs`: `KeyCode::Char(c)` in `fn on_key`; `src/tui/draw.rs`: the `// Input` part of `fn draw` |

#### What is wrong

- `KeyCode::Char(c)` inserts `c` whatever modifier is held, so Ctrl+U, Ctrl+D or Alt+X type a plain letter.
- Bracketed paste (the terminal marking a paste as one block) is off. Pasted text with line breaks presses Enter at every break, which sends the lines as separate messages.
- The input box shows one row and never scrolls sideways, so text past the right edge, and the cursor, disappear.
- The cursor column is the character count. Wide characters such as 日本 take two columns each, so the cursor lands in the wrong place.
- The same character counting cuts and wraps text wrongly elsewhere: the header's right part (`right_w`), `truncate_str` (card titles, session list) and `wrap_n` (card bodies). A session title with a line break runs into the next text.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/tui/draw.rs`:
```rust
    if !app.busy {
        let x = chunks[2].x + 1 + app.cursor as u16;
        let y = chunks[2].y + 1;
```

#### Why it matters

Pasting a stack trace or a code block (common with a coding agent) fires off a burst of half-messages, and each one replaces the previous run. Long prompts cannot be read before sending.

```rust
    /// B-35: insert pasted text at the cursor. Line breaks are kept (the

    pub fn on_paste(&mut self, text: &str) {
```

Add this right before it:

```rust
/// B-35: the part of `input` that fits in `width` terminal columns with
/// the cursor visible, and the cursor's column inside that part. Columns
/// are display widths (日 = 2). A line break shows as ⏎, a tab as →.
pub fn input_view(input: &str, cursor: usize, width: usize) -> (String, usize) {
    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
    let shown: Vec<(char, usize)> = input
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            let c = match c {
                '\n' => '⏎',
                '\t' => '→',
                c if c.is_control() => '·',
                c => c,
            };
            (c, c.width().unwrap_or(0))
        })
        .collect();
    let width = width.max(1);
    let before: usize = shown.iter().take(cursor).map(|(_, w)| w).sum();
    // Skip whole characters from the left until the cursor fits.
    let need = before.saturating_sub(width - 1);
    let (mut start, mut skipped) = (0, 0);
    while start < shown.len() && skipped < need {
        skipped += shown[start].1;
        start += 1;
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut used = 0;
    for (c, w) in &shown[start..] {
        if used + w > width {
            break;
        }
        out.push(*c);
        used += w;
    }
    (out, before - skipped)
}

```

```rust
fn truncate_str(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() <= max {
        s.to_string()
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Cut `s` to at most `max` terminal columns and add `…` when something was
/// cut (B-35: display width, so wide characters count double).
fn truncate_str(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {
    use unicode_width::{UnicodeWidthChar, UnicodeWidthStr};
    if s.width() <= max {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    let mut cut = String::new();
    let mut used = 0;
    for c in s.chars() {
        let w = c.width().unwrap_or(0);
        if used + w > max {
            break;
        }
        cut.push(c);
        used += w;
    }
    format!("{cut}…")
}
```
