### B-36 · GUI preview bridge timing bugs

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none (S-12 also edits `struct Bridge`, but other lines; either order works) |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: `struct Bridge`, `Bridge::start` (`"navigate"` and `"wait"`), `Bridge::on_loaded`, `Bridge::expire`, the `UiMsg::Browser(ev)` arm in `fn run`; `src/browser.rs`: `fn wait_script` |

#### What is wrong

The agent's `browser_navigate` and `browser_wait` are answered by the GUI's
`Bridge`. Four timing bugs:

1. `browser_wait` with only `ms` allows up to 30 000 ms, but every bridge
   request expires after 25 s. A wait of 26–30 s always fails with "the page
   did not answer in time".
2. `browser_wait` with a selector or text always waits at most 8 s; the `ms`
   the model passes is ignored.
3. A second `browser_navigate` replaces the first one's reply channel. The
   first caller gets a vague "panel closed" error instead of a reason.
4. A navigation resolves on the next "load finished" event, even one from the
   page we are leaving; and a navigation the panel refuses never resolves, so
   the caller waits 25 s for "navigation timed out".

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
                        .unwrap_or(500)
                        .clamp(1, 30_000);
```

#### Why it matters

The agent gets wrong page data (the old page's URL and title) or long, useless
timeouts. It then retries, or reasons about the wrong page.

#### Steps

1. Give a waiting navigation a struct with a `started` flag, and name the wait
   limit. In `struct Bridge`, replace the `nav` field.

```rust
/// New (B-36): one `browser_navigate` waiting for its page to load.
struct NavWait {
    reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<String, String>>,
    deadline: Instant,
    /// Set once the new page starts loading. A "finished" event that comes
    /// before that belongs to the page we are leaving and must not answer.
    started: bool,
}

/// New (B-36): longest `browser_wait` we run. It must stay below the 25 s
/// request deadline in `Bridge::start`, or the deadline fires first.
const MAX_WAIT_MS: u64 = 20_000;
```

<!-- TASK:B-37 -->
### B-37 · GUI transcript re-render cost per streamed token

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/gui.rs`, `src/gui.html`, `tests/gui/panel.js` |
| Read first | `src/gui.rs`: `GuiState::payload`, `fn paint`, `enum IpcMsg`, `fn parse_ipc`, the `IpcMsg::Ready` arm in `fn run`; `src/gui.html`: the "Render Transcript Entries" part of `window.render` |

#### What is wrong

Every streamed token makes Rust serialize the WHOLE transcript and send it to the
page (`paint` → `payload`). The page then turns the whole list into a string to
compare it, and if anything changed it deletes every row and rebuilds them all,
running the Markdown renderer again for every assistant message. On a long chat
this costs more per token the longer the chat gets. Rebuilding also closes every
reasoning box the user opened and drops their text selection.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gui.html`:
```js
    var sig = JSON.stringify(d.entries || []) + "\u0000" + (d.session || "");
    if (log && log._sig !== sig) {
      var stick = true;
      if (entries && log._sig !== undefined && log._session === (d.session || "")) {
        stick = entries.scrollHeight - entries.scrollTop - entries.clientHeight < 60;
      }
      var saved = entries ? entries.scrollTop : 0;
      log._sig = sig;
      log._session = d.session || "";
      log.textContent = "";
```

#### Why it matters

Long sessions get sluggish while the agent streams, and the user cannot keep a
reasoning box open or select text while a reply is arriving.

#### Steps

Stage 1 — the page keeps its rows and updates only what changed.

```js
  function updateRow(log, row, e) {
    var text = e.t || "";
    if (row._k === e.k && row._t === text) return row;

    var total = typeof d.entries_len === "number" ? d.entries_len : from + list.length;
    var sameChat = log._rows !== undefined && log._session === session;
    var rows = sameChat ? log._rows : [];
    if (!sameChat) log.textContent = "";
    log._rows = rows;
    log._session = session;
    if (from > rows.length) {
      // We missed a paint (for example the page reloaded): ask for all.
      postToRust({ type: "resync" });
      return;
    }
    // Keep the reader's place: follow new text only if they were at the bottom.
    var stick = true;
    if (entries && sameChat) {
      stick = entries.scrollHeight - entries.scrollTop - entries.clientHeight < 60;
    }
    var saved = entries ? entries.scrollTop : 0;
    var changed = !sameChat;
    for (var j = 0; j < list.length; j++) {
      var e = list[j];
      var idx = from + j;
      if (idx < rows.length) {
        var old = rows[idx];
        if (old._k !== e.k || old._t !== (e.t || "")) {
          rows[idx] = updateRow(log, old, e);
          changed = true;
        }
      } else {
        var row = buildRow(e);
        log.appendChild(row);
        rows.push(row);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
    while (rows.length > total) {
      log.removeChild(rows.pop());
      changed = true;
    }
    if (!changed || !entries) return;
    if (stick) {
      entries.scrollTop = entries.scrollHeight;
    } else {
      // Restore the reading position instantly (no smooth animation).
      entries.style.scrollBehavior = "auto";
      entries.scrollTop = saved;
      entries.style.scrollBehavior = "";
```

```rust
    pub fn payload(&self) -> String {
        let entries: Vec<serde_json::Value> = self

```

Replace it with:
```rust
    /// JSON payload for `window.render(...)` — keys are read by gui.html.
    pub fn payload(&self) -> String {
        self.payload_from(0)
    }

    /// New (B-37): the payload for a paint. It sends only the entries that
    /// changed since the last paint; the page keeps the rows it already has.
    pub fn paint_payload(&self) -> String {
        let mut sent = self.sent.borrow_mut();
        // Another chat on screen: the page rebuilds, so send everything.
        if *self.sent_session.borrow() != self.session {
            sent.clear();
            *self.sent_session.borrow_mut() = self.session.clone();
        }
        let from = self
            .entries
            .iter()
            .zip(sent.iter())
            .take_while(|(now, before)| now == before)
            .count();
        sent.truncate(from);
        sent.extend(self.entries[from..].iter().cloned());
        drop(sent);
        self.payload_from(from)
    }

    /// New (B-37): forget what the page has; the next paint sends everything.
    pub fn resync(&self) {
        self.sent.borrow_mut().clear();
        *self.sent_session.borrow_mut() = None;
    }

    /// New (B-37): the payload with `entries[from..]`, plus `entries_from`
    /// and `entries_len` so the page knows where that slice starts.
    fn payload_from(&self, from: usize) -> String {
        let entries: Vec<serde_json::Value> = self
            .entries
            .iter()
            .skip(from)
            .map(|(k, t)| serde_json::json!({ "k": kind_class(k).to_string(), "t": t }))
            .collect();
```

### B-38 · db: transactions, foreign keys, schema parity, readable parse errors, better ids

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | S-07 (moves the approvals table), B-05 (replaces `apply_compaction`). The Find blocks below are not touched by either task, so the order does not matter for applying; do them first for a clean history. |
| Files to change | `src/db.rs` |
| Read first | `src/db.rs`: `new_id`, `Db::open`, `Db::open_in_memory`, `insert_message`, `fork_session`, `messages` |

#### What is wrong

1. `insert_message` runs two statements (insert message, bump session time)
   without a transaction; `fork_session` copies messages one call at a time.
   A crash in the middle leaves half-done work.
2. SQLite ignores `REFERENCES ... ON DELETE CASCADE` unless
   `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set for the connection. It never is, so a
   message can point at a session that does not exist.
3. `open_in_memory` (used by tests and ephemeral runs) creates `messages`
   without the `REFERENCES` clause, so tests run against a different schema.
4. `messages()` turns unreadable `parts` JSON into an empty list
   (`unwrap_or_default`). The message silently loses its content.
5. `new_id` hashes time, thread id and a counter with a fixed-key hasher;
   it also hashes eight zero bytes that do nothing. Two processes started in
   the same instant can produce the same id.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/db.rs`:
```rust
            let (id, role, parts_json, created_at) = row?;
            let parts: Vec<Part> = serde_json::from_str(&parts_json).unwrap_or_default();
            out.push(Message { id, session_id: session_id.to_string(), role, parts, created_at });
```

#### Why it matters

The database is the only record of a session. Silent loss (half a fork, an
emptied message) is worse than a visible error.

#### Steps


**Stage 1 — readable rows and better ids**

1. Open `src/db.rs`. Replace `new_id` (around line 48). It now uses a hasher
   that is seeded randomly once per process.

Find this code in `src/db.rs`:
```rust
pub fn new_id(prefix: &str) -> String {
    use std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher;
    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
    let mut h = DefaultHasher::new();
    now_ms().hash(&mut h);
    std::thread::current().id().hash(&mut h);
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.subsec_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    nanos.hash(&mut h);
    let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
    // Cheap per-process randomness for ids: hash + atomic counter.
    static CTR: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
    let n = CTR.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    n.hash(&mut h);
    h.write(&mut buf);
    format!("{prefix}_{:016x}", h.finish())
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
pub fn new_id(prefix: &str) -> String {
    use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hash, Hasher};
    // `RandomState` is seeded randomly per process, so two processes that
    // start in the same instant still get different ids; time plus a counter
    // keeps ids unique inside one process. Ids are unique, not secret.
    static SEED: std::sync::OnceLock<std::collections::hash_map::RandomState> =
        std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    static CTR: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
    let mut h = SEED.get_or_init(std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new).build_hasher();
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    nanos.hash(&mut h);
    CTR.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed).hash(&mut h);
    format!("{prefix}_{:016x}", h.finish())
}
```

```rust
    pub fn fork_session(&self, id: &str, title: &str) -> Result<Session> {
        let parent = self
            .get_session(id)?
            .with_context(|| format!("no session `{id}`"))?;
        let new = self.create_session(title, Some(&parent.id))?;
```

Replace it with:
```rust
    pub fn fork_session(&self, id: &str, title: &str) -> Result<Session> {
        let parent = self
            .get_session(id)?
            .with_context(|| format!("no session `{id}`"))?;
        let msgs = self.messages(&parent.id)?;
        let now = now_ms();
        let new = Session {
            id: new_id("ses"),
            title: title.to_string(),
            parent_id: Some(parent.id.clone()),
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now,
        };
        // One transaction: a failed fork leaves no half-copied session.
        let mut conn = self.conn.lock().unwrap();
        let tx = conn.transaction()?;
        tx.execute(
            "INSERT INTO sessions (id, title, parent_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5)",
            params![new.id, new.title, new.parent_id, new.created_at, new.updated_at],
        )?;
        {
            let mut ins = tx.prepare(
                "INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, role, parts, created_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4,?5)",
            )?;
            for m in &msgs {
                let json = serde_json::to_string(&m.parts)?;
                ins.execute(params![new_id("msg"), new.id, m.role, json, m.created_at])?;
            }
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(new)
    }
```

### B-39 · gitsnap: clear redo on a new run, pop only after success, stable folder hash

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | S-14 (it validates stack ids, which this task relies on when it deletes snapshot folders; it also makes `restore_manifest` report problems instead of hiding them) |
| Files to change | `src/gitsnap.rs` |
| Read first | `src/gitsnap.rs`: `fn snap_root`, `fn record_before_run`, `fn undo`, `fn redo` |

#### What is wrong

1. `record_before_run` pushes onto the undo stack but never clears the redo
   stack. After a new run, `/redo` can still "restore" a state from before
   that run, on top of newer work.
2. `undo` and `redo` pop the stack **first** and only then take the
   counter-snapshot and restore. If either step fails, the entry is gone.
3. The snapshot folder that was just restored is never deleted, so every
   `/undo` leaves a folder behind (only the oldest beyond 20 are pruned).
4. `snap_root` names the folder with `DefaultHasher`, whose output Rust may
   change between versions, over the raw workspace string. A Rust upgrade or
   another spelling of the same folder (`C:\repo` vs `C:\repo\.`) loses the
   undo history.

(The "errors are swallowed during restore" part of this item is fixed by
S-14, which changes the same lines.)

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/gitsnap.rs`:
```rust
    let Some(id) = pop_stack(&undo_path) else { return Ok(None) };
    // Capture the state we're about to replace so redo can bring it back.
    if let Some(cur) = take_snapshot(workspace, state_dir, "pre-undo")? {
        push_stack(&redo_path, &cur.id, &root)?;
    }
```

#### Why it matters

Undo and redo must be predictable. A redo that brings back an old state, or
an undo that silently loses its entry, destroys work instead of saving it.

#### Steps


**Stage 1 — a stable folder name**

1. Open `src/gitsnap.rs`. Replace `snap_root` (around line 172). The new
   folder name is a stable FNV-1a hash (a simple, fixed hash function) of
   the canonical workspace path. Undo history stored under the old name is
   not migrated: after this change `/undo` starts with an empty history once.
   The old `snaps_<hash>` folders in the state directory can be deleted by
   hand.

Find this code in `src/gitsnap.rs`:
```rust
/// workspace-specific snapshot root under the state dir.
fn snap_root(state_dir: &Path, workspace: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    use std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher;
    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
    let mut h = DefaultHasher::new();
    workspace.to_string_lossy().hash(&mut h);
    state_dir.join(format!("snaps_{:016x}", h.finish()))
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Workspace-specific snapshot root under the state dir. The folder name is
/// a fixed FNV-1a hash of the canonical workspace path (lower-case on
/// Windows), so it survives restarts, Rust upgrades and other spellings of
/// the same folder.
fn snap_root(state_dir: &Path, workspace: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let canon = std::fs::canonicalize(workspace).unwrap_or_else(|_| workspace.to_path_buf());
    let mut key = canon.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    if cfg!(windows) {
        key = key.to_lowercase();
    }
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for b in key.as_bytes() {
        h ^= u64::from(*b);
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
    }
    state_dir.join(format!("snaps_{h:016x}"))
}
```

```rust
/// Restore the most recent snapshot (undo). `Ok(None)` = nothing to undo.
pub fn undo(workspace: &Path, state_dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Manifest>> {
    let root = snap_root(state_dir, workspace);
    let (undo_path, redo_path) = stack_paths(&root);
    let Some(id) = pop_stack(&undo_path) else { return Ok(None) };
    // Capture the state we're about to replace so redo can bring it back.
    if let Some(cur) = take_snapshot(workspace, state_dir, "pre-undo")? {
        push_stack(&redo_path, &cur.id, &root)?;
    }
    let m = load_manifest(&root, &id)?;
    restore_manifest(workspace, state_dir, &root, &m)?;
    Ok(Some(m))
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Shared body of undo and redo: restore the newest entry of the `from`
/// stack after saving the current state on the `to` stack.
/// - A damaged entry (bad manifest) is dropped from `from` and reported;
///   nothing else changes.
/// - If the counter-snapshot fails, both stacks stay as they were.
/// - Once files may have changed, the step is recorded even when restore
///   reports problems: the counter-snapshot goes on `to`, the used entry
///   leaves `from`, and its folder is deleted.
fn step(
    workspace: &Path,
    state_dir: &Path,
    from: &Path,
    to: &Path,
    label: &str,
) -> Result<Option<Manifest>> {
    let root = snap_root(state_dir, workspace);
    let Some(id) = read_stack(from).last().cloned() else { return Ok(None) };
    let m = match load_manifest(&root, &id) {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            pop_stack(from);
            return Err(anyhow!("{e:#} (snapshot {id} was dropped from the stack)"));
        }
    };
    let cur = take_snapshot(workspace, state_dir, label)?;
    let restored = restore_manifest(workspace, state_dir, &root, &m);
    if let Some(cur) = cur {
        push_stack(to, &cur.id, &root)?;
    }
    pop_stack(from);
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(root.join(&id));
    restored.map(|_| Some(m))
}

/// Restore the most recent snapshot (undo). `Ok(None)` = nothing to undo.
pub fn undo(workspace: &Path, state_dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Manifest>> {
    let root = snap_root(state_dir, workspace);
    let (undo_path, redo_path) = stack_paths(&root);
    step(workspace, state_dir, &undo_path, &redo_path, "pre-undo")
}
```

4. Replace `redo` (around line 352).

Find this code in `src/gitsnap.rs`:
```rust
/// Re-apply the state an `/undo` replaced. `Ok(None)` = nothing to redo.
pub fn redo(workspace: &Path, state_dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Manifest>> {
    let root = snap_root(state_dir, workspace);
    let (undo_path, redo_path) = stack_paths(&root);
    let Some(id) = pop_stack(&redo_path) else { return Ok(None) };
    if let Some(cur) = take_snapshot(workspace, state_dir, "pre-redo")? {
        push_stack(&undo_path, &cur.id, &root)?;
    }
    let m = load_manifest(&root, &id)?;
    restore_manifest(workspace, state_dir, &root, &m)?;
    Ok(Some(m))
}
```

```rust
/// Re-apply the state an `/undo` replaced. `Ok(None)` = nothing to redo.
pub fn redo(workspace: &Path, state_dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<Manifest>> {
    let root = snap_root(state_dir, workspace);
    let (undo_path, redo_path) = stack_paths(&root);
    step(workspace, state_dir, &redo_path, &undo_path, "pre-redo")
}
```

### B-40 · browser.rs: element refs from an older snapshot can hit the wrong element

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | S-13 (its test helpers `FAKE_DOM` and `run_runtime_in_node` are reused here) |
| Files to change | `src/browser.rs` |
| Read first | `src/browser.rs`: `RUNTIME_JS` (`snapshot`, `click`, `type`) |

#### What is wrong

Each `browser_snapshot` numbers the visible interactive elements `e1`, `e2`,
… and writes the number into the attribute `data-habi-ref`. Old attributes
are never removed. If element A was `e1` in an earlier snapshot and is now
hidden, the next snapshot skips A (it keeps its old `e1`) and gives `e1` to
element B. `click('e1')` then uses `querySelector`, which returns the first
match in the page — often the hidden A, not the B the model just saw. The
comment says stale refs "fail loudly", which is only true after a full page
load.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
    snapshot: function () {
      var nodes = document.querySelectorAll(SEL);
      var out = [];
```

#### Why it matters

The model clicks what it believes is the "Submit" button and the page
receives a click on a different, hidden element. That is an action the
user approved for one thing and got for another.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/browser.rs` and find `RUNTIME_JS` (around line 190). At the
   start of `snapshot`, remove all old refs first.

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
    snapshot: function () {
      var nodes = document.querySelectorAll(SEL);
      var out = [];
```

Replace it with:
```js
    snapshot: function () {
      // Refs from an older snapshot must not survive: clear them first, so
      // every ref names exactly one element of THIS snapshot.
      var old = document.querySelectorAll('[data-habi-ref]');
      for (var k = 0; k < old.length; k++) old[k].removeAttribute('data-habi-ref');
      var nodes = document.querySelectorAll(SEL);
      var out = [];
```

2. In `click`, refuse an element that is no longer visible.

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
    click: function (ref) {
      var el = document.querySelector('[data-habi-ref="' + ref + '"]');
      if (!el) throw new Error('no element with ref ' + ref + ' — take a fresh snapshot');
```

Replace it with:
```js
    click: function (ref) {
      var el = document.querySelector('[data-habi-ref="' + ref + '"]');
      if (!el) throw new Error('no element with ref ' + ref + ' — take a fresh snapshot');
      if (!vis(el)) throw new Error('element ' + ref + ' is no longer visible — take a fresh snapshot');
```

3. Same in `type`.

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```js
    type: function (ref, text, submit) {
      var el = document.querySelector('[data-habi-ref="' + ref + '"]');
      if (!el) throw new Error('no element with ref ' + ref + ' — take a fresh snapshot');
```

Replace it with:
```js
    type: function (ref, text, submit) {
      var el = document.querySelector('[data-habi-ref="' + ref + '"]');
      if (!el) throw new Error('no element with ref ' + ref + ' — take a fresh snapshot');
      if (!vis(el)) throw new Error('element ' + ref + ' is no longer visible — take a fresh snapshot');
```

4. Fix the doc comment above `RUNTIME_JS` so it says what really happens.

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```rust
/// Refs (`data-habi-ref`) are only valid for the snapshot that produced them;
/// a navigation wipes the document, so a stale ref fails loudly instead of
/// clicking something the model did not mean.
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Refs (`data-habi-ref`) are only valid for the snapshot that produced them:
/// every snapshot first removes all old refs, and click/type refuse an
/// element that is gone or hidden, so a stale ref fails loudly instead of
/// clicking something the model did not mean.
```

`RUNTIME_JS` must still end with the line `})();"#;` at column 0
(`tests/gui/run.sh` depends on it).

#### Tests to add

Add this test at the end of `mod tests` in `src/browser.rs` (right before its last closing brace):
```rust

        let prelude = format!(
            "{FAKE_DOM}\nvar FIELDS = [\n\

        );
        let Some(out) = run_runtime_in_node(

        assert!(lines[0].contains("\"name\":\"New\"") && !lines[0].contains("Old"), "{out}");
```

```rust
    let mut name = fallback_name.clone();
    let mut description = String::new();
    // Editors on Windows often start UTF-8 files with a byte-order mark.
    let text = text.strip_prefix('\u{feff}').unwrap_or(text);
    let mut body = text;

    if let Some((fm, body_text)) = split_frontmatter(text) {
        let lines: Vec<&str> = fm.lines().collect();

                let mut v = v.trim().to_string();
                // `key: >` or `key: |` (YAML block): the value is on the
                // following indented lines.
                if matches!(v.as_str(), ">" | "|" | ">-" | "|-") {
                    let mut parts = Vec::new();
                    while i + 1 < lines.len() && lines[i + 1].starts_with([' ', '\t']) {
                        i += 1;
                        parts.push(lines[i].trim());
                    }
                    v = parts.join(" ");
                }
                let v = unquote(&v);
                match k.trim() {
                    "name" if !v.is_empty() => name = v.to_string(),
                    "description" if !v.is_empty() => description = v.to_string(),
```

```rust
    }

/// `---` as the whole first line, then everything up to the next line that
/// is exactly `---` (trailing spaces allowed). Returns (frontmatter, body).
fn split_frontmatter(text: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let rest = text.strip_prefix("---")?;
    let rest = rest.strip_prefix("\r\n").or_else(|| rest.strip_prefix('\n'))?;
    let mut offset = 0;
    for line in rest.split_inclusive('\n') {
        if line.trim_end() == "---" {
            return Some((&rest[..offset], &rest[offset + line.len()..]));
        }
        offset += line.len();
    }
    None
}

/// Strip one pair of matching quotes: `"Deploy the app"` → `Deploy the app`.
fn unquote(v: &str) -> &str {
    let b = v.as_bytes();
    if b.len() >= 2 && (b[0] == b'"' || b[0] == b'\'') && b[b.len() - 1] == b[0] {
        &v[1..v.len() - 1]
    } else {
        v
    }
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Keys in the config text that this version does not know (typos, old
/// names), as dotted paths like `provider.modle` or `mcp.servers[0].argz`.
pub fn unknown_config_keys(text: &str, cfg: &Config) -> Vec<String> {
    fn walk(user: &toml::Value, known: &toml::Value, path: &str, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
        match (user, known) {
            (toml::Value::Table(u), toml::Value::Table(k)) => {
                for (key, v) in u {
                    let here = if path.is_empty() { key.clone() } else { format!("{path}.{key}") };
                    match k.get(key) {
                        Some(kv) => walk(v, kv, &here, out),
                        None => out.push(here),
                    }
                }
            }
            (toml::Value::Array(u), toml::Value::Array(k)) => {
                for (i, (uv, kv)) in u.iter().zip(k).enumerate() {
                    walk(uv, kv, &format!("{path}[{i}]"), out);
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let (Ok(user), Ok(known)) = (text.parse::<toml::Table>(), toml::Value::try_from(cfg)) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    walk(&toml::Value::Table(user), &known, "", &mut out);
    out
}

pub fn default_config_path() -> PathBuf {
    let base = std::env::var("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
```

```rust
/// Navigation rule for the standalone window: web pages and about:blank
/// always; local files only when the window started on one.
fn preview_nav_allowed(url: &str, allow_file: bool) -> bool {
    let lower = url.to_ascii_lowercase();
    lower.starts_with("http://")
        || lower.starts_with("https://")
        || lower == "about:blank"
        || (allow_file && lower.starts_with("file://"))
}

/// Page-provided text for the terminal: control characters (escape codes,
/// line breaks) are shown escaped, and long text is cut to 300 characters.
fn safe_log(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for c in s.chars().take(300) {
        if c.is_control() {
            out.extend(c.escape_default());
        } else {
            out.push(c);
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
/// B-47: `/mission explore effort=max the auth flow` → (Max, "the auth flow").
/// Without a valid `effort=` word the effort is the default (High).
pub fn split_effort(goal: &str) -> (Effort, String) {
    let goal = goal.trim();
    if let Some(rest) = goal.strip_prefix("effort=") {
        let (word, tail) = rest.split_once(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or((rest, ""));
        if let Some(effort) = Effort::parse(word) {
            return (effort, tail.trim().to_string());
        }
    }
    (Effort::default(), goal.to_string())
}
```

### B-48 · No stderr output while the TUI runs; git off the async threads

| Field | Value |

| Priority | P3 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/main.rs` |

#### What is wrong

- `fn internal` and the snapshot error in `run_agent` (both in `src/server.rs`) print with `eprintln!`. So does the TUI's apply-edit path in `src/main.rs`. While the TUI owns the terminal, that text is drawn over the screen.
- `run_agent` calls `gitsnap::record_before_run` directly. It runs `git`, which can take seconds in a big repository, and blocks an async worker thread meanwhile. (`/undo` and `/redo` already use `spawn_blocking`.)

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:


#### Why it matters

A stray error line breaks the TUI's screen until the next full redraw, and the message is lost when the screen is redrawn. A slow `git` call blocks a worker thread that other tasks need.

#### Steps

1. Open `src/server.rs`. Replace `fn internal` (around line 506) and add a small log helper after it.

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:

```rust
fn internal<E: std::fmt::Display>(e: E) -> StatusCode {

}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
fn internal<E: std::fmt::Display>(e: E) -> StatusCode {
    // New (B-48): to the log file, not stderr (stderr draws over the TUI).
    core_log(&format!("[core] internal error: {e}"));
    StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
}

/// New (B-48): append one line to `<state_dir>/core.log`. Use this instead
/// of `eprintln!` in code that can run while the TUI owns the terminal.
pub fn core_log(msg: &str) {
    use std::io::Write;
    let path = crate::config::default_state_dir().join("core.log");
    if let Some(dir) = path.parent() {
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(dir);
    }
    let stamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&path) {
        let _ = writeln!(f, "[{stamp}] {msg}");
    }
}
```

```rust
        eprintln!("[snapshot] {e:#}");

```

Replace it with:

```rust
    // Safety net before anything mutates the workspace. Failure is not
    // fatal — snapshotting is a convenience, the run must still work.
    // New (B-48): git runs off the async threads; errors go to core.log.
    let (ws, sd) = (st.workspace.clone(), st.state_dir.clone());
    let snap = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        crate::gitsnap::record_before_run(&ws, &sd, "pre-run")
    })
    .await;
    if let Ok(Err(e)) = snap {
        core_log(&format!("[snapshot] {e:#}"));
    }
```

#### What is wrong

After a run that "changed the workspace", `run_agent` starts the automatic "ponytail" review (a second model loop, on by default via `agent.auto_review`). It decides that the workspace changed when the run made a `write`, an `edit`, or any `bash` call. So read-only commands such as `ls`, `git status` or `cargo test` also trigger a full review.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
    // Laziness Meter: did this run change the workspace at all?
    let touched = {
        let after = snapshot_stats(st, session_id);
        after.writes > before.writes
            || after.edits > before.edits
            || after.bash_runs > before.bash_runs
    };
```

#### Why it matters

Most runs use `bash` at least once, so almost every run pays for a second, slow model loop, and the review text clutters the transcript with "findings" about changes that do not exist.

#### Steps

How the fix works. Before the run, a fingerprint of the git working tree is taken (a hash of `git status` plus `git diff`). After the run it is compared with a new one. A successful `write`/`edit` still counts as a change. A `bash` run counts only when the fingerprint changed. When the workspace is not a git repository, there is nothing to compare, so `bash` counts as before.

1. Open `src/server.rs`. Add the fingerprint method at the start of the `impl AppState` block that holds `debt_report` (around line 735).


```rust
impl AppState {
    /// New (P-02): a fingerprint of the git working tree (status plus diff),
    /// or None when the workspace is not a git repository. Git runs off the
    /// async threads.
    pub(crate) async fn workspace_fingerprint(&self) -> Option<u64> {
        let ws = self.workspace.clone();
        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
            let status = crate::gitsnap::git(&ws, &["status", "--porcelain=v1", "-uall"]).ok()?;
            let diff = crate::gitsnap::git(&ws, &["diff", "--no-ext-diff", "HEAD"]).unwrap_or_default();
            let mut h = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();
            status.hash(&mut h);
            diff.hash(&mut h);
            Some(h.finish())
        })
        .await
        .ok()
        .flatten()
    }

    /// Laziness Meter report for `/debt`.
    pub fn debt_report(&self, session_id: &str) -> String {
```

### P-03 · No automatic review after an abort

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs` |

#### What is wrong

An aborted run returns `Ok("aborted")`, which `run_agent` treats as success (`ok == true`). If the run had already changed something, `run_agent` then starts the automatic review. That adds the user-style prompt "Review the current uncommitted changes …" to the transcript and shows the note "ponytail review — checking the change …". The review then stops at once, because it shares the run's abort flag, which is already set. The result is a dangling prompt and a confusing note right after the user pressed stop.

When the user aborts, they want the agent to stop. Instead the transcript gains a fake user message and a review note, and the next model call sees that dangling prompt.

### P-04 · Reuse gate: fewer false hints, one walk, honest comment

| Field | Value |

| Priority | P3 |

#### What is wrong

After every successful `write`, `reuse_gate` looks for names the new file defines that already exist elsewhere, and appends a "reuse hint" to the tool result.

1. `top_level_symbols` trims each line first, so methods and nested functions count as "top-level".
2. `find_symbol` counts the name as found when it appears as ANY word in any source file, not where it is defined. Names like `new`, `main` or `run` are everywhere, so most writes get a false hint, and the model is told to "reuse" code that does not exist.
3. It walks the workspace (up to 3,000 files) once per name.
4. The comment says "before accepting a `write`", but the gate runs after the file was written.

A hint that is almost always wrong teaches the model to ignore hints, and sometimes makes it delete or "reuse" code for no reason. The repeated walks slow down every write in a big repository.

```rust
/// New (P-04): true when a line of `text` defines `sym` (`fn sym`, `def sym`, …).
fn defines(text: &str, sym: &str) -> bool {
    const KW: [&str; 7] = ["fn ", "def ", "class ", "struct ", "function ", "interface ", "trait "];
    text.lines().any(|line| {
        KW.iter().any(|k| {
            line.find(k).is_some_and(|i| {
                let rest = &line[i + k.len()..];
                rest.starts_with(sym)
                    && !rest[sym.len()..].starts_with(|c: char| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_')
            })
        })
    })
}
```

#### What is wrong

The vendored Ponytail rules (`src/prompts/ponytail.md`, line 17) tell the model: "Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`". No such command exists. `/ponytail ultra` is sent to the model as chat, and the rules are all-or-nothing (config `agent.ponytail`).

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/agents.rs`:
```rust
    if p.ponytail {
        out.push_str("\n\n## Ponytail — lazy senior dev discipline\n\n");
        out.push_str(ponytail_rules().trim());
    }
```

#### Why it matters

The model offers a command that does nothing. Users cannot turn the rules down for a quick hack, or up for a design review, without editing the config and restarting.


Add this right before it:
```rust
/// P-05: how strongly the Ponytail rules apply in one session. `Full` is
/// the vendored default; `Off` leaves the rules out of the prompt.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PonytailLevel {
    Off,
    Lite,
    Full,
    Ultra,
}

impl PonytailLevel {
    /// `off` / `lite` / `full` / `ultra`, any case.
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match s.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "off" => Some(Self::Off),
            "lite" => Some(Self::Lite),
            "full" => Some(Self::Full),
            "ultra" => Some(Self::Ultra),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Off => "off",
            Self::Lite => "lite",
            Self::Full => "full",
            Self::Ultra => "ultra",
        }
    }

    /// The level a session starts with: config `agent.ponytail` on = full.
    pub fn from_config(enabled: bool) -> Self {
        if enabled { Self::Full } else { Self::Off }
    }
}

```

### F-01 · Retry the provider request with backoff (429 / 5xx / connection errors)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none (do it before F-02) |
| Files to change | `src/provider.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `config.example.toml` |
| Read first | `src/provider.rs`: `struct Client`, `fn new`, `fn stream`; `src/server.rs`: `fn build_state`, `fn build_state_ephemeral_skills` |

#### What is wrong

`Client::stream` in `src/provider.rs` sends the request once. A failed
connection, a 429 (rate limit) or a 5xx answer becomes an error at once.
`run_loop` and `one_shot` in `src/server.rs` (and `src/compact.rs`) pass it
up with `?`, so the whole agent run stops. Busy providers send such errors
often, and they usually go away within seconds.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/provider.rs`:
```rust
        let resp = req.send().await.map_err(|e| anyhow!(
            "provider request to {}/chat/completions failed: {e:?} \
             (tunnel down or endpoint unreachable — check the base URL / heartbeat in the header)",
            self.base_url
        ))?;
```

#### Why it matters

One short hiccup (OpenRouter rate limit, Anthropic "overloaded" 529, a
Cloudflare tunnel blip) kills a long run halfway; the user must start over.

#### Steps

The plan: a new private method `send_with_retry` sends the request and,
for temporary errors, waits and sends it again. Only the part BEFORE the
reply streams is retried. A reply that breaks halfway is never requested
again: the user has already seen part of it. New config `provider.max_retries`
(default 3). Other tasks also edit `src/provider.rs` (B-21, B-29); the blocks
below avoid their lines.

```rust
    /// Build the client from the `[provider]` config section.
    pub fn from_cfg(base_url: &str, p: &crate::config::ProviderCfg) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut c = Self::new(base_url, &p.api_key, &p.model, p.request_timeout_secs)?;
        c.max_retries = p.max_retries;
        Ok(c)
    }

    /// Send a request; return the response once its status is 2xx.
    /// Temporary failures (connection errors, 429/500/502/503/504/529) are
    /// sent again up to `max_retries` times, after 1s, 2s, 4s … (max 30s)
    /// plus jitter, or after the `Retry-After` seconds the server asked for.
    /// `build` makes a fresh request each time (a request is sent only once).
    /// Never prints: stderr output would corrupt the TUI.
    async fn send_with_retry(
        &self,
        url: &str,
        build: impl Fn() -> reqwest::RequestBuilder,
    ) -> Result<reqwest::Response> {
        let attempts = self.max_retries.saturating_add(1);
        let mut attempt: u32 = 0;
        loop {
            attempt += 1;
            // Each arm gives: error text, "worth retrying?", server's Retry-After.
            let (mut msg, retryable, retry_after) = match build().send().await {
                Ok(resp) if resp.status().is_success() => return Ok(resp),
                Ok(resp) => {
                    let status = resp.status();
                    let retry_after = retry_after_secs(resp.headers());
                    let text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
                    let msg = format!(
                        "provider returned {status}: {}",
                        text.chars().take(400).collect::<String>()
                    );
                    (msg, is_retryable_status(status.as_u16()), retry_after)
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    let msg = format!(
                        "provider request to {url} failed: {e:?} \
                         (tunnel down or endpoint unreachable — check the base URL / heartbeat in the header)"
                    );
                    (msg, is_retryable_send_error(&e), None)
                }
            };
            if !retryable || attempt >= attempts {
                if attempt > 1 {
                    msg.push_str(&format!(" (gave up after {attempt} attempts)"));
                }
                return Err(anyhow!(msg));
            }
            let wait = match retry_after {
                Some(secs) if secs > MAX_RETRY_WAIT.as_secs() => {
                    msg.push_str(&format!(
                        " (the provider asked to wait {secs}s before retrying; \
                         not waiting that long; gave up after {attempt} attempt(s))"
                    ));
                    return Err(anyhow!(msg));
                }
                Some(secs) => std::time::Duration::from_secs(secs),
                None => backoff_delay(self.retry_base, attempt) + jitter(),
            };
            tokio::time::sleep(wait).await;
        }
    }
```

```rust
/// Longest wait between two retries. A longer `Retry-After` is not waited
/// out: the request fails at once and the error says why.
const MAX_RETRY_WAIT: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(30);

/// "Busy, try again soon": rate limit, server errors, Anthropic's 529.
/// Anything else (400, 401, 404 …) means the request itself is wrong.
fn is_retryable_status(code: u16) -> bool {
    matches!(code, 429 | 500 | 502 | 503 | 504 | 529)
}

/// The connection failed or broke before the response headers. Not
/// retried: a full request timeout (it already waited) and a bad URL.
fn is_retryable_send_error(e: &reqwest::Error) -> bool {
    e.is_connect() || (e.is_request() && !e.is_timeout())
}

/// `Retry-After: <seconds>`. The rare HTTP-date form is ignored.
fn retry_after_secs(headers: &reqwest::header::HeaderMap) -> Option<u64> {
    headers
        .get(reqwest::header::RETRY_AFTER)?
        .to_str()
        .ok()?
        .trim()
        .parse::<u64>()
        .ok()
}

/// Wait before retry number `attempt` (1, 2, 3 …): base, 2×base, 4×base …
fn backoff_delay(base: std::time::Duration, attempt: u32) -> std::time::Duration {
    let factor = 1u32 << attempt.saturating_sub(1).min(16);
    base.saturating_mul(factor).min(MAX_RETRY_WAIT)
}

/// 0–249 ms extra, so many clients do not retry at the same moment.
/// `RandomState` is randomly keyed per process: enough for jitter.
fn jitter() -> std::time::Duration {
    use std::hash::BuildHasher;
    let n = std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new().hash_one(std::time::SystemTime::now());
    std::time::Duration::from_millis(n % 250)
}
```

Add this at the end of `src/provider.rs`:
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod f01_tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::time::Duration;

    #[test]
    fn retry_rules() {
        let s = Duration::from_secs;
        assert_eq!(backoff_delay(s(1), 1), s(1));
        assert_eq!(backoff_delay(s(1), 3), s(4));
        assert_eq!(backoff_delay(s(1), 6), s(30), "capped at 30s");
        assert_eq!(backoff_delay(s(1), 99), s(30), "no overflow");
        assert!([429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529].iter().all(|c| is_retryable_status(*c)));
        assert!([400, 401, 403, 404].iter().all(|c| !is_retryable_status(*c)));
        let mut h = reqwest::header::HeaderMap::new();
        assert_eq!(retry_after_secs(&h), None);
        h.insert(reqwest::header::RETRY_AFTER, "7".parse().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(retry_after_secs(&h), Some(7));
        assert!(jitter() < Duration::from_millis(250));
    }

    /// Request N gets `script[N]` (a status and an optional Retry-After);
    /// after that, a valid streamed reply "hello". Returns base URL + hit count.
    async fn scripted_provider(script: Vec<(u16, Option<&'static str>)>) -> (String, Arc<AtomicUsize>) {
        use axum::http::{header, HeaderValue, StatusCode};
        use axum::{response::IntoResponse, routing::post, Router};
        let hits = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let counter = hits.clone();
        let app = Router::new().route(
            "/v1/chat/completions",
            post(move || {
                let step = script.get(counter.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst)).copied();
                async move {
                    if let Some((code, retry_after)) = step {
                        let mut resp = (StatusCode::from_u16(code).unwrap(), "busy").into_response();
                        if let Some(v) = retry_after {
                            resp.headers_mut().insert(header::RETRY_AFTER, HeaderValue::from_static(v));
                        }
                        return resp;
                    }
                    let body = "data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"hello\"},\"finish_reason\":\"stop\"}]}\n\ndata: [DONE]\n\n";
                    ([(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "text/event-stream")], body).into_response()
                }
            }),
        );
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)).await.unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
        });
        (format!("http://{addr}/v1"), hits)
    }

    fn fast_client(base: &str, max_retries: u32) -> Client {
        let mut c = Client::new(base, "", "stub", 30).unwrap();
        c.max_retries = max_retries;
        c.retry_base = Duration::from_millis(10);
        c
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn retries_503_twice_then_streams_the_reply() {
        // The first 503 has no Retry-After (backoff path), the second says 0s.
        let (base, hits) = scripted_provider(vec![(503, None), (503, Some("0"))]).await;
        let client = fast_client(&base, 3);
        let mut s = client.stream("stub", &[], &[]).await.expect("third try succeeds");
        let mut text = String::new();
        while let Some(ev) = s.next().await {
            if let StreamEvent::Text(t) = ev.unwrap() {
                text.push_str(&t);
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(text, "hello");
        assert_eq!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn gives_up_after_max_retries_and_counts_attempts() {
        let (base, hits) = scripted_provider(vec![(503, None); 10]).await;
        let err = fast_client(&base, 2).stream("stub", &[], &[]).await.err().expect("fails");
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("gave up after 3 attempts"), "{err}");
        assert_eq!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3, "1 try + 2 retries");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn bad_request_and_long_retry_after_are_not_retried() {
        let (base, hits) = scripted_provider(vec![(400, None)]).await;
        let err = fast_client(&base, 3).stream("stub", &[], &[]).await.err().expect("fails");
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("400"), "{err}");
        assert_eq!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1);

        let (base, hits) = scripted_provider(vec![(429, Some("120"))]).await;
        let err = fast_client(&base, 3).stream("stub", &[], &[]).await.err().expect("fails");
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("120s"), "{err}");
        assert_eq!(hits.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1, "a 2-minute Retry-After is not waited out");
    }
}
```

### F-02 · Native Anthropic Messages API provider

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | L (a day or more) |
| Depends on | F-01 (`send_with_retry`, `from_cfg`), B-08 (Stage 4 edits its heartbeat code); B-04 recommended first |
| Files to change | new `src/provider/anthropic.rs`, `src/provider.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `config.example.toml` |
| Read first | `src/provider.rs`: `struct Client`, `fn stream`, `fn list_models`, `enum StreamEvent`, `struct ToolCallAccumulator` |

#### What is wrong

The client only speaks the OpenAI chat format (`POST {base_url}/chat/completions`).
Anthropic's own API (`POST {base_url}/messages`) uses a different body,
different auth headers and different stream events, so Claude models only
work through a translating proxy such as OpenRouter.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/provider.rs`:
```rust
    /// Stream a chat completion. `tools` may be empty for plain chat.
    pub async fn stream(
        &self,
        model: &str,
        messages: &[ChatMsg],
        tools: &[ToolSpec],
    ) -> Result<futures::stream::BoxStream<'static, Result<StreamEvent>>> {
```

#### Why it matters

Users with an Anthropic key cannot use it directly; proxies add cost and
their own failures. The native path also reports `max_tokens` cut-offs as
`finish_reason "length"`, which B-03 relies on.

#### Steps

The plan: new config `provider.api = "openai" | "anthropic"` (default
`"openai"`) and `provider.max_tokens` (default 8192; Anthropic requires it).
`Client::stream` keeps its signature and its `StreamEvent`s. For
`"anthropic"` it turns the OpenAI-style `ChatMsg` history into an Anthropic
request, and Anthropic's stream events back into `StreamEvent`s, so
`ToolCallAccumulator`, `run_loop`, `one_shot` and `compact.rs` do not change.

API rules this code follows (official docs, links at the end): headers
`x-api-key` and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`; body `model`, `max_tokens`,
top-level `system` string (there is no "system" role), `messages`,
`tools: [{name, description, input_schema}]`, `stream: true`; tool results
are `tool_result` blocks in a USER message and must come BEFORE any text
there; Claude 4.6+ rejects a history that ends with an assistant message;
unknown stream event types must be ignored.

Thinking: current Claude models think by default (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and
others; some cannot turn it off) and return `thinking` blocks before a tool
call. When the tool results go back, the API requires those blocks
unchanged in that assistant message, or it answers 400. This project's
history keeps only plain text, so the client saves each tool-calling reply,
thinking blocks included, in a small in-memory cache (new type `TurnCache`)
and sends the replies of the current turn (after the last user message)
back exactly as received. Older turns go without thinking, which the API
allows. We add no `thinking` parameter (the model's default is used).
Other tasks edit `src/provider.rs` too (B-21, B-29); these blocks avoid their lines.

**Stage 1 — translate the history (new file, pure functions)**

Add this new file `src/provider/anthropic.rs`:
```rust
//! F-02: Anthropic Messages API (`POST {base_url}/messages`). Turns the
//! OpenAI-style `ChatMsg` history into an Anthropic request body, and the
//! Anthropic stream back into the same `StreamEvent`s.

use super::{ChatMsg, ToolSpec};
use serde_json::{json, Value};

/// Build the JSON body for `POST {base_url}/messages`.
/// - Leading system messages become the top-level `system` string; a
///   later one (compaction summary, slash command) stays in place as user
///   text "[system note] …".
/// - Tool results become `tool_result` blocks in a user message.
/// - Messages with the same role in a row are merged.
/// - The result starts with a user message and never ends with an
///   assistant message.
/// - `turns`: tool-calling replies exactly as the model sent them (thinking
///   blocks included), keyed by `turn_key`. Assistant messages after the
///   last user message (the current turn) are sent back from there.
pub(super) fn request_body(
    model: &str,
    max_tokens: u32,
    messages: &[ChatMsg],
    tools: &[ToolSpec],
    turns: &[(String, Vec<Value>)],
) -> Value {
    let turn_start = messages.iter().rposition(|m| m.role == "user").unwrap_or(0);
    let mut system: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut out: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    for (i, m) in messages.iter().enumerate() {
        let text = m.content.clone().unwrap_or_default();
        let (role, blocks) = match m.role.as_str() {
            "system" if out.is_empty() => {
                if !text.trim().is_empty() {
                    system.push(text);
                }
                continue;
            }
            "system" => ("user", text_block(&format!("[system note]\n{text}"))),
            "user" => ("user", text_block(&text)),
            "assistant" => {
                let calls: Vec<_> = m.tool_calls.iter().flatten().collect();
                let key = turn_key(calls.iter().map(|tc| clean_id(&tc.id)));
                let saved = turns.iter().rev().find(|(k, _)| i > turn_start && !calls.is_empty() && *k == key);
                if let Some((_, blocks)) = saved {
                    ("assistant", blocks.clone()) // exactly as the model sent it
                } else {
                    let mut blocks = text_block(&text);
                    for tc in calls {
                        // `arguments` is a JSON string; Anthropic wants an object.
                        let input = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&tc.function.arguments)
                            .ok()
                            .filter(Value::is_object)
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
                        blocks.push(json!({
                            "type": "tool_use",
                            "id": clean_id(&tc.id),
                            "name": tc.function.name,
                            "input": input,
                        }));
                    }
                    ("assistant", blocks)
                }
            }
            "tool" => {
                // server.rs starts the text of a failed tool run with "[error]".
                let is_error = text.starts_with("[error]");
                let content = if text.is_empty() { "(no output)".to_string() } else { text };
                let block = json!({
                    "type": "tool_result",
                    "tool_use_id": clean_id(m.tool_call_id.as_deref().unwrap_or("")),
                    "content": content,
                    "is_error": is_error,
                });
                ("user", vec![block])
            }
            _ => continue,
        };
        push_merged(&mut out, role, blocks);
    }
    if out.first().map_or(true, |m| m["role"] != "user") {
        out.insert(0, json!({ "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "(continued)" }] }));
    }
    if out.last().map_or(false, |m| m["role"] == "assistant") {
        push_merged(&mut out, "user", text_block("Continue."));
    }
    let mut body = json!({ "model": model, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "messages": out, "stream": true });
    if !system.is_empty() {
        body["system"] = json!(system.join("\n\n"));
    }
    if !tools.is_empty() {
        let tools: Vec<Value> = tools
            .iter()
            .map(|t| {
                json!({
                    "name": t.function.name,
                    "description": t.function.description,
                    "input_schema": t.function.parameters,
                })
            })
            .collect();
        body["tools"] = json!(tools);
    }
    body
}

/// One text block, or none for blank text (Anthropic rejects empty text).
fn text_block(text: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
    if text.trim().is_empty() {
        Vec::new()
    } else {
        vec![json!({ "type": "text", "text": text })]
    }
}

/// Cache key of one tool-calling reply: its tool_use ids joined by ",".
fn turn_key(ids: impl Iterator<Item = String>) -> String {
    ids.collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",")
}

/// Anthropic ids must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`; ids made by other
/// providers may not, so other characters become `_`.
fn clean_id(id: &str) -> String {
    let s: String = id
        .chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '-' { c } else { '_' })
        .collect();
    if s.is_empty() {
        "toolu_missing".to_string()
    } else {
        s
    }
}

/// Append a message, or merge its blocks into the previous one when the
/// role repeats. `tool_result` blocks move to the front (stable sort).
fn push_merged(out: &mut Vec<Value>, role: &str, blocks: Vec<Value>) {
    if blocks.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(last) = out.last_mut() {
        if last["role"] == role {
            if let Some(arr) = last["content"].as_array_mut() {
                arr.extend(blocks);
                arr.sort_by_key(|b| b["type"] != "tool_result");
            }
            return;
        }
    }
    out.push(json!({ "role": role, "content": blocks }));
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod translate_tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::provider::{FunctionCall, ToolCallReq, ToolFnSpec};

    fn msg(role: &str, content: Option<&str>) -> ChatMsg {
        ChatMsg { role: role.into(), content: content.map(String::from), tool_calls: None, tool_call_id: None }
    }

    fn call(id: &str, args: &str) -> ToolCallReq {
        let function = FunctionCall { name: "read".into(), arguments: args.into() };
        ToolCallReq { id: id.into(), kind: "function".into(), function }
    }

    #[test]
    fn history_is_translated_to_anthropic_shape() {
        let mut asst = msg("assistant", Some("Let me look."));
        asst.tool_calls = Some(vec![call("call_1", r#"{"path":"a.rs"}"#)]);
        let mut result = msg("tool", Some("fn main() {}"));
        result.tool_call_id = Some("call_1".into());
        let history = vec![
            msg("system", Some("You are a coder.")),
            msg("user", Some("Read a.rs")),
            asst,
            result,
            msg("system", Some("[slash command expanded]")),
            msg("user", Some("Now explain it.")),
        ];
        let read = ToolFnSpec { name: "read".into(), description: "Read".into(), parameters: json!({"type": "object"}) };
        let tools = vec![ToolSpec { kind: "function".into(), function: read }];
        let body = request_body("claude-sonnet-5-5", 1000, &history, &tools, &[]);
        assert_eq!(body["max_tokens"], 1000);
        assert_eq!(body["system"], "You are a coder.");
        assert_eq!(body["tools"][0]["input_schema"]["type"], "object");
        let m = body["messages"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.len(), 3, "user / assistant / user (tool result + notes merged)");
        assert_eq!(m[1]["content"][1]["type"], "tool_use");
        assert_eq!(m[1]["content"][1]["input"]["path"], "a.rs");
        let blocks = m[2]["content"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(blocks[0]["type"], "tool_result", "tool results come first");
        assert_eq!(blocks[0]["tool_use_id"], "call_1");
        assert!(blocks[1]["text"].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("[system note]"));
        assert_eq!(blocks[2]["text"], "Now explain it.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn edge_cases_still_give_a_valid_request() {
        // Starts and ends with the assistant, bad JSON arguments, an error
        // result, a blank user message, an id Anthropic would reject.
        let mut asst = msg("assistant", None);
        asst.tool_calls = Some(vec![call("call:9", "not json")]);
        let mut failed = msg("tool", Some("[error]\nboom"));
        failed.tool_call_id = Some("call:9".into());
        let history = vec![asst, failed, msg("user", Some("  ")), msg("assistant", Some("Done."))];
        let body = request_body("m", 10, &history, &[], &[]);
        let m = body["messages"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.first().unwrap()["role"], "user");
        assert_eq!(m.last().unwrap()["role"], "user");
        assert!(body.get("system").is_none() && body.get("tools").is_none());
        assert_eq!(m[1]["content"][0]["id"], "call_9");
        assert_eq!(m[1]["content"][0]["input"], json!({}));
        assert_eq!(m[2]["content"][0]["tool_use_id"], "call_9");
        assert_eq!(m[2]["content"][0]["is_error"], true);
    }

    #[test]
    fn current_turn_is_sent_back_from_the_saved_reply() {
        let with_call = |id: &str| {
            let mut a = msg("assistant", None);
            a.tool_calls = Some(vec![call(id, "{}")]);
            a
        };
        let result = |id: &str| {
            let mut r = msg("tool", Some("ok"));
            r.tool_call_id = Some(id.into());

        };
        let history =
            vec![msg("user", Some("one")), with_call("t0"), result("t0"), msg("user", Some("two")), with_call("t1"), result("t1")];
        let saved = |id: &str| {
            let thinking = json!({ "type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": "sig" });
            (id.to_string(), vec![thinking, json!({ "type": "tool_use", "id": id, "name": "read", "input": {} })])
        };
        let body = request_body("m", 10, &history, &[], &[saved("t0"), saved("t1")]);
        let m = body["messages"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.len(), 5);
        assert_eq!(m[1]["content"][0]["type"], "tool_use", "an older turn goes without thinking");
        assert_eq!(m[3]["content"][0]["signature"], "sig", "the current turn is sent back as saved");
    }
}
```

**Stage 2 — parse Anthropic's stream into `StreamEvent`s**

3. Add the stream parser. It splits lines like `sse_event_stream` in
   `src/provider.rs`. Only `data:` lines matter: each holds JSON whose
   `type` names the event, so `event:` lines are skipped. Mapping:
   - `tool_use` block start → `ToolCallDelta` with id and name; each
     `input_json_delta` adds argument text. The block `index` is the key
     `ToolCallAccumulator` expects. A tool with no arguments may get no JSON
     at all, so `content_block_stop` then adds `"{}"`.
   - `text_delta` → `Text`, `thinking_delta` → `Reasoning`.
   - `stop_reason` → `finish_reason`: `end_turn`/`stop_sequence` → `"stop"`,
     `max_tokens` → `"length"`, `tool_use` → `"tool_calls"`, `refusal` →
     `"content_filter"`, others unchanged.
   - An `error` event, or a connection that closes before `message_delta`,
     becomes an `Err`: a cut-off reply must not look complete.
   - The parser also rebuilds the reply's content blocks (thinking text and
     `signature`, text, tool input). When `message_delta` ends a reply that
     called tools and has thinking blocks, it saves them in the `TurnCache`.

Add this at the end of `src/provider/anthropic.rs`:
```rust
use super::StreamEvent;
use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
use futures::StreamExt;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, VecDeque};

/// Tool-calling replies exactly as the model sent them (thinking blocks and
/// signatures included), keyed by `turn_key` of their tool ids. Shared by
/// all clones of one `Client`; `request_body` reads it.
pub(super) type TurnCache = std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<(String, Vec<Value>)>>>;

/// How many such replies to keep (one per agent step that used tools).
const TURN_CACHE_MAX: usize = 256;

/// Anthropic `stop_reason` → the OpenAI `finish_reason` the app understands.
fn finish_reason(stop: &str) -> String {
    match stop {
        "end_turn" | "stop_sequence" => "stop",
        "max_tokens" | "model_context_window_exceeded" => "length",
        "tool_use" => "tool_calls",
        "refusal" => "content_filter",
        other => other,
    }
    .to_string()
}

/// Append `s` to the string field `key` of a content block.
fn append(block: &mut Value, key: &str, s: &str) {
    let joined = format!("{}{s}", block[key].as_str().unwrap_or(""));
    block[key] = Value::String(joined);
}

/// What we remember while reading one stream.
#[derive(Default)]
struct SseState {
    /// The reply's content blocks so far, by block index.
    blocks: BTreeMap<usize, Value>,
    /// Argument JSON received so far for each open `tool_use` block.
    tool_json: HashMap<usize, String>,
    /// A `Done` was already sent (from `message_delta`).
    done_sent: bool,
    /// `message_stop` arrived: the reply is complete.
    finished: bool,
    /// Where a finished tool-calling reply is saved.
    turns: TurnCache,
}

impl SseState {
    /// Turn one SSE line into zero or more events.
    fn line(&mut self, line: &str) -> Result<Vec<StreamEvent>> {
        let Some(data) = line.strip_prefix("data:") else { return Ok(Vec::new()) };
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(data.trim()) else { return Ok(Vec::new()) };
        let index = v["index"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0) as usize;
        let text = |s: &Value| s.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let mut events = Vec::new();
        match v["type"].as_str().unwrap_or("") {
            "content_block_start" => {
                let block = v["content_block"].clone();
                if block["type"] == "text" && !text(&block["text"]).is_empty() {
                    events.push(StreamEvent::Text(text(&block["text"])));
                }
                if block["type"] == "tool_use" {
                    self.tool_json.insert(index, String::new());
                    events.push(StreamEvent::ToolCallDelta {
                        index,
                        id: block["id"].as_str().map(String::from),
                        name: block["name"].as_str().map(String::from),
                        args_delta: String::new(),
                    });
                }
                self.blocks.insert(index, block);
            }
            "content_block_delta" => {
                let d = &v["delta"];
                let block = self.blocks.entry(index).or_insert_with(|| json!({}));
                match d["type"].as_str().unwrap_or("") {
                    "text_delta" => {
                        let t = text(&d["text"]);
                        append(block, "text", &t);
                        if !t.is_empty() {
                            events.push(StreamEvent::Text(t));
                        }
                    }
                    "thinking_delta" => {
                        let t = text(&d["thinking"]);
                        append(block, "thinking", &t);
                        if !t.is_empty() {
                            events.push(StreamEvent::Reasoning(t));
                        }
                    }
                    "signature_delta" => block["signature"] = d["signature"].clone(),
                    "input_json_delta" => {
                        let part = text(&d["partial_json"]);
                        if !part.is_empty() {
                            self.tool_json.entry(index).or_default().push_str(&part);
                            events.push(StreamEvent::ToolCallDelta { index, id: None, name: None, args_delta: part });
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {} // citations and newer delta types
                }
            }
            "content_block_stop" => {
                if let Some(raw) = self.tool_json.remove(&index) {
                    if raw.is_empty() {
                        // A tool called with no arguments may get no JSON at all.
                        let args_delta = "{}".to_string();
                        events.push(StreamEvent::ToolCallDelta { index, id: None, name: None, args_delta });
                    }
                    let input = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&raw).ok().filter(Value::is_object);
                    if let Some(block) = self.blocks.get_mut(&index) {
                        block["input"] = input.unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
                    }
                }
            }
            "message_delta" => {
                if let Some(stop) = v["delta"]["stop_reason"].as_str() {
                    if !self.done_sent {
                        self.done_sent = true;
                        self.save_turn();
                        events.push(StreamEvent::Done { finish_reason: Some(finish_reason(stop)) });
                    }
                }
            }
            "message_stop" => {
                self.finished = true;
                if !self.done_sent {
                    self.done_sent = true;
                    self.save_turn();
                    events.push(StreamEvent::Done { finish_reason: None });
                }
            }
            "error" => {
                return Err(anyhow!(
                    "provider stream error: {}: {}",
                    v["error"]["type"].as_str().unwrap_or("error"),
                    v["error"]["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("(no message)")
                ));
            }
            _ => {} // message_start, ping, event types added later
        }
        Ok(events)
    }

    /// Keep this reply for the next request when it called tools and has
    /// thinking blocks: the API wants that turn sent back unchanged.
    fn save_turn(&self) {
        let blocks: Vec<Value> = self.blocks.values().cloned().collect();
        let kind = |b: &Value| b["type"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let ids = blocks.iter().filter(|b| kind(b) == "tool_use");
        let key = turn_key(ids.map(|b| clean_id(b["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""))));
        if key.is_empty() || !blocks.iter().any(|b| kind(b).ends_with("thinking")) {
            return;
        }
        if let Ok(mut turns) = self.turns.lock() {
            turns.retain(|(k, _)| *k != key);
            turns.push((key, blocks));
            if turns.len() > TURN_CACHE_MAX {
                turns.remove(0);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Read Anthropic's SSE bytes and yield `StreamEvent`s (same line splitting
/// and stall timeout as `sse_event_stream` in provider.rs).
pub(super) fn event_stream(
    byte_stream: impl futures::Stream<Item = reqwest::Result<bytes::Bytes>> + Send + 'static,
    stall: std::time::Duration,
    turns: TurnCache,
) -> impl futures::Stream<Item = Result<StreamEvent>> + Send + 'static {
    let src = Box::pin(byte_stream);
    let state = SseState { turns, ..Default::default() };
    futures::stream::unfold(
        (src, Vec::<u8>::new(), VecDeque::<StreamEvent>::new(), state, false),
        move |(mut src, mut buf, mut pending, mut st, over)| async move {
            loop {
                if let Some(ev) = pending.pop_front() {
                    return Some((Ok(ev), (src, buf, pending, st, over)));
                }
                if over || st.finished {
                    return None;
                }
                if let Some(pos) = buf.iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
                    let line: Vec<u8> = buf.drain(..=pos).collect();
                    let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&line).trim().to_string();
                    match st.line(&line) {
                        Ok(events) => pending.extend(events),
                        Err(e) => return Some((Err(e), (src, buf, pending, st, true))),
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                let err = match tokio::time::timeout(stall, src.next()).await {
                    Ok(Some(Ok(bytes))) => {
                        buf.extend_from_slice(&bytes);
                        continue;
                    }
                    Err(_) => anyhow!("provider stream stalled: no data for {}s", stall.as_secs()),
                    Ok(Some(Err(e))) => anyhow!("stream error: {e}"),
                    Ok(None) if st.done_sent => return None,
                    Ok(None) => anyhow!("provider closed the stream before the reply was complete"),
                };
                return Some((Err(err), (src, buf, pending, st, true)));
            }
        },
    )
}

event: content_block_start

event: content_block_start
data: {"type":"content_block_start","index":1,"content_block":{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01T1x1fJ34qAmk2tNTrN7Up6","name":"get_weather","input":{}}}

event: content_block_delta
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":1,"delta":{"type":"input_json_delta","partial_json":""}}

event: content_block_stop
data: {"type":"content_block_stop","index":1}

event: message_delta
data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null},"usage":{"output_tokens":89}}

event: message_stop
data: {"type":"message_stop"}

"#;

    /// Feed `text` in 7-byte pieces (so lines arrive split), collect the events.
    async fn run_with(text: &str, turns: TurnCache) -> Vec<Result<StreamEvent>> {
        let pieces: Vec<reqwest::Result<bytes::Bytes>> =
            text.as_bytes().chunks(7).map(|c| Ok(bytes::Bytes::copy_from_slice(c))).collect();
        let stall = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
        event_stream(futures::stream::iter(pieces), stall, turns).collect().await
    }

    async fn run(text: &str) -> Vec<Result<StreamEvent>> {
        run_with(text, TurnCache::default()).await
    }

    /// Split events into (text, tool calls, finish_reason); panics on Err.
    async fn collect(text: &str) -> (String, Vec<(String, String, Value)>, Option<String>) {
        let (mut out, mut acc, mut finish) = (String::new(), ToolCallAccumulator::default(), None);
        for ev in run(text).await {
            match ev.unwrap() {
                StreamEvent::Text(t) => out.push_str(&t),
                StreamEvent::Done { finish_reason } => finish = finish_reason,
                ev => acc.push(&ev),
            }
        }
        (out, acc.finish(), finish)
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn recorded_tool_use_stream_parses() {
        let (text, calls, finish) = collect(SAMPLE).await;
        assert_eq!(text, "Okay, let's check the weather:");
        assert_eq!(finish.as_deref(), Some("tool_calls"));
        assert_eq!(calls.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(calls[0].0, "toolu_01T1x1fJ34qAmk2tNTrN7Up6");
        assert_eq!(calls[0].1, "get_weather");
        assert_eq!(calls[0].2["location"], "San Francisco, CA");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn errors_cut_off_streams_and_tools_without_arguments() {
        let overloaded = "data: {\"type\": \"error\", \"error\": {\"type\": \"overloaded_error\", \"message\": \"Overloaded\"}}\n";
        let err = run(overloaded).await.pop().unwrap().err().expect("error event must surface");
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("overloaded_error"), "{err}");

        let cut = "data: {\"type\":\"content_block_delta\",\"index\":0,\"delta\":{\"type\":\"text_delta\",\"text\":\"Hel\"}}\n";
        let evs = run(cut).await;
        assert!(matches!(evs.first(), Some(Ok(StreamEvent::Text(t))) if t == "Hel"));
        assert!(evs.last().unwrap().is_err(), "a cut-off reply must not look complete");

        let no_args = concat!(
            "data: {\"type\":\"content_block_start\",\"index\":0,\"content_block\":{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"id\":\"toolu_1\",\"name\":\"todo\",\"input\":{}}}\n",
            "data: {\"type\":\"content_block_stop\",\"index\":0}\n",
            "data: {\"type\":\"message_delta\",\"delta\":{\"stop_reason\":\"end_turn\"}}\n",
            "data: {\"type\":\"message_stop\"}\n",
        );
        let (_, calls, finish) = collect(no_args).await;
        assert_eq!(calls[0].2, json!({}));
        assert_eq!(finish.as_deref(), Some("stop"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn thinking_tool_turn_is_saved_for_the_next_request() {
        let stream = r#"data: {"type":"content_block_start","index":0,"content_block":{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}}
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"thinking_delta","thinking":"Read it."}}
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"signature_delta","signature":"sig-1"}}
data: {"type":"content_block_stop","index":0}
data: {"type":"content_block_start","index":1,"content_block":{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_9","name":"read","input":{}}}
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":1,"delta":{"type":"input_json_delta","partial_json":"{\"path\":\"a\"}"}}
data: {"type":"content_block_stop","index":1}
data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"tool_use"}}
"#;
        let turns = TurnCache::default();
        let evs = run_with(stream, turns.clone()).await;
        assert!(matches!(&evs[0], Ok(StreamEvent::Reasoning(t)) if t == "Read it."));
        let saved = turns.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(saved.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(saved[0].0, "toolu_9");
        assert_eq!(saved[0].1[0], json!({ "type": "thinking", "thinking": "Read it.", "signature": "sig-1" }));
        assert_eq!(saved[0].1[1]["input"], json!({ "path": "a" }));
    }
}
```

```rust
use crate::config::ProviderApi;

/// Value of the `anthropic-version` header.
pub const ANTHROPIC_VERSION: &str = "2023-06-01";

/// Put the API key on a request the way the configured API expects it.
/// OpenAI-compatible: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (skipped for an empty
/// key, e.g. local Ollama). Anthropic: `x-api-key` plus `anthropic-version`.
pub fn with_auth(req: reqwest::RequestBuilder, api: ProviderApi, api_key: &str) -> reqwest::RequestBuilder {
    match api {
        ProviderApi::OpenAi if api_key.is_empty() => req,
        ProviderApi::OpenAi => req.bearer_auth(api_key),
        ProviderApi::Anthropic => {
            let req = req.header("anthropic-version", ANTHROPIC_VERSION);
            if api_key.is_empty() {
                req
            } else {
                req.header("x-api-key", api_key)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
impl super::Client {
    /// `stream()` for `provider.api = "anthropic"`: POST `{base_url}/messages`
    /// (with the F-01 retries), then parse the SSE reply.
    pub(super) async fn stream_anthropic(
        &self,
        model: &str,
        messages: &[ChatMsg],
        tools: &[ToolSpec],
    ) -> Result<futures::stream::BoxStream<'static, Result<StreamEvent>>> {
        let body = {
            let turns = self.turns.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
            request_body(model, self.max_tokens, messages, tools, &turns)
        };
        let url = format!("{}/messages", self.base_url);
        let resp = self
            .send_with_retry(&url, || super::with_auth(self.http.post(&url), self.api, &self.api_key).json(&body))
            .await?;
        Ok(Box::pin(event_stream(resp.bytes_stream(), self.stall, self.turns.clone())))
    }
}
```
