```rust
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"signature_delta","signature":"sig-1"}}
data: {"type":"content_block_stop","index":0}
data: {"type":"content_block_start","index":1,"content_block":{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_1","name":"read","input":{}}}
data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":1,"delta":{"type":"input_json_delta","partial_json":"{\"path\":\"a\"}"}}
data: {"type":"content_block_stop","index":1}
data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"tool_use"}}
"#;

    /// Reply 2, after the tool result.
    const SECOND: &str = r#"data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":"done"}}
data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}
"#;

    fn auth_ok(h: &HeaderMap) -> bool {
        h.get("x-api-key").is_some_and(|v| v == "sk-test")
            && h.get("anthropic-version").is_some_and(|v| v == crate::provider::ANTHROPIC_VERSION)
            && h.get(header::AUTHORIZATION).is_none()
    }

    type Collected = (String, Vec<(String, String, Value)>, Option<String>);

    async fn collect(mut s: futures::stream::BoxStream<'static, Result<StreamEvent>>) -> Collected {
        let (mut text, mut acc, mut finish) = (String::new(), ToolCallAccumulator::default(), None);
        while let Some(ev) = s.next().await {
            match ev.unwrap() {
                StreamEvent::Text(t) => text.push_str(&t),
                StreamEvent::Done { finish_reason } => finish = finish_reason,
                ev => acc.push(&ev),
            }
        }
        (text, acc.finish(), finish)
    }

    /// Two steps of a tool loop against a fake endpoint. The second request
    /// is only answered when the thinking block came back unchanged.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn tool_round_trip_sends_thinking_back() {
        let messages = post(|h: HeaderMap, Json(body): Json<Value>| async move {
            let echoed = &body["messages"][1]["content"][0];
            let sse = if !(auth_ok(&h) && body["system"] == "sys" && body["max_tokens"] == 321) {
                return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("unexpected: {body}")).into_response();
            } else if body["messages"].as_array().map_or(0, Vec::len) == 1 {
                FIRST
            } else if echoed["type"] == "thinking" && echoed["signature"] == "sig-1" {
                SECOND
            } else {
                return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, format!("thinking not sent back: {body}")).into_response();
            };
            ([(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "text/event-stream")], sse).into_response()
        });
        let models = get(|h: HeaderMap| async move {
            if !auth_ok(&h) {
                return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, "no key").into_response();
            }
            r#"{"data":[{"id":"claude-sonnet-5-5"}]}"#.into_response()
        });
        let app = Router::new().route("/v1/messages", messages).route("/v1/models", models);
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)).await.unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
        });

        let mut cfg = crate::config::ProviderCfg::default();
        cfg.api_key = "sk-test".into();
        cfg.model = "claude-sonnet-5-5".into();
        cfg.api = crate::config::ProviderApi::Anthropic;
        cfg.max_tokens = 321;
        let client = crate::provider::Client::from_cfg(&format!("http://{addr}/v1"), &cfg).unwrap();
        let msg = |role: &str, text: Option<&str>| ChatMsg {
            role: role.into(),
            content: text.map(String::from),
            tool_calls: None,
            tool_call_id: None,
        };
        let mut history = vec![msg("system", Some("sys")), msg("user", Some("read a"))];
        let (_, calls, finish) = collect(client.stream(&client.model, &history, &[]).await.unwrap()).await;
        assert_eq!(finish.as_deref(), Some("tool_calls"));
        assert_eq!((calls[0].0.as_str(), calls[0].1.as_str()), ("toolu_1", "read"));

        // Store the call and its result the way run_loop does, then go on.
        let mut asst = msg("assistant", None);
        let function = FunctionCall { name: calls[0].1.clone(), arguments: calls[0].2.to_string() };
        asst.tool_calls = Some(vec![ToolCallReq { id: calls[0].0.clone(), kind: "function".into(), function }]);
        let mut result = msg("tool", Some("file text"));
        result.tool_call_id = Some(calls[0].0.clone());
        history.extend([asst, result]);
        let (text, _, finish) = collect(client.stream(&client.model, &history, &[]).await.unwrap()).await;
        assert_eq!((text.as_str(), finish.as_deref()), ("done", Some("stop")));
        assert_eq!(client.list_models().await.unwrap(), vec!["claude-sonnet-5-5"]);
    }
}
```

### F-03 · MCP servers over Streamable HTTP

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | L (a day or more) |
| Depends on | B-19, B-20 (uses B-19's `cap_result` and `tool_fn_name`, and B-20's `Live` struct) |
| Files to change | new `src/mcp_http.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `src/config.rs` |
| Read first | `src/mcp.rs`: `struct Live` (from B-20), `McpConn::spawn`, `Registry::start_all`; `src/config.rs`: `struct McpServerCfg` |

#### What is wrong

`src/mcp.rs` only starts MCP servers as local child processes and talks to
them over stdin/stdout. Hosted MCP servers speak "Streamable HTTP" instead.
A `[[mcp.servers]]` entry without `command` is silently skipped:

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/mcp.rs`:
```rust
        for cfg in servers {
            if cfg.name.is_empty() || cfg.command.is_empty() {
                continue;
```

#### Why it matters

Users cannot connect hosted MCP servers (documentation search, issue
trackers, company tools) at all, and those are the most common kind.

#### Steps

The plan: optional `url` and `headers` in `[[mcp.servers]]`. With `url`, no
process starts; the new client in the new file `src/mcp_http.rs` speaks
HTTP. It has the same three operations as the stdio `Client`
(`initialize`, `list_tools`, `call_tool`). In `src/mcp.rs` a small new enum
`Transport` holds either kind, so the registry, `McpConn::call` and B-20's
`McpRoute::call` work unchanged.

Protocol rules used (official spec, links at the end): every JSON-RPC
message is its own HTTP POST to the endpoint, with
`Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. A request gets either one JSON
object or an SSE stream ending with the response that has the same `id`
(server notifications and requests such as `ping` may come first). A
notification gets `202 Accepted`. The `initialize` answer may carry an
`Mcp-Session-Id` header: send it on every later request, plus
`MCP-Protocol-Version: <version the server chose>`. A 404 to a request that
carried a session id means "session expired": `initialize` again, retry.
Version: the newest spec (2026-07-28) has NO `initialize` and no sessions.
The newest revision WITH them is 2025-11-25, so this client asks for
`"2025-11-25"` and accepts the version the server answers. Servers that
support both eras work; a server that ONLY speaks 2026-07-28 rejects
`initialize`, and the error says so (supporting it is a separate, later task).

6. Create the client. A server request that arrives on an SSE stream (such
   as `ping`) is answered with its own POST; otherwise the server waits for
   that answer and our call hangs. We announce no client features, so any
   other server request gets "method not found". Config header values are
   never put in error messages (they are often tokens).

Add this new file `src/mcp_http.rs`:
```rust
//! F-03: MCP client over Streamable HTTP (protocol revision 2025-11-25).
//! One endpoint; each JSON-RPC message is its own POST. Answers come as one
//! JSON object or as an SSE stream. The `Mcp-Session-Id` from `initialize`
//! goes on every later request, with `MCP-Protocol-Version`; a 404 then
//! means "session expired". Not supported: the optional GET stream,
//! resuming broken streams, servers that ONLY speak revision 2026-07-28.

use crate::mcp::McpTool;
use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Context, Result};
use futures::StreamExt;
use reqwest::header::{HeaderMap, HeaderName, HeaderValue, ACCEPT, CONTENT_TYPE};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::time::Duration;

/// The newest MCP revision that still starts with an `initialize` handshake.
pub const HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "2025-11-25";

const INIT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(20);
const LIST_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(20);
const CALL_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(300);

/// One MCP server reached over HTTP.
pub struct HttpClient {
    http: reqwest::Client,
    url: String,
    /// Headers from the config (for example `Authorization`), sent every time.
    extra: HeaderMap,
    next_id: i64,
    /// From the `Mcp-Session-Id` header of the `initialize` answer, if any.
    session_id: Option<String>,
    /// The protocol version the server chose in `initialize`.
    protocol: Option<String>,
}

impl HttpClient {
    /// Check the config headers. No network traffic yet; call `initialize` next.
    pub fn new(url: &str, headers: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut extra = HeaderMap::new();
        for (k, v) in headers {
            let name = HeaderName::from_bytes(k.as_bytes())
                .with_context(|| format!("bad header name `{k}` in [[mcp.servers]] headers"))?;
            let value = HeaderValue::from_str(v)
                .with_context(|| format!("bad value for header `{k}` in [[mcp.servers]] headers"))?;
            extra.insert(name, value);
        }
        let http = reqwest::Client::builder().connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).build()?;
        Ok(Self { http, url: url.to_string(), extra, next_id: 0, session_id: None, protocol: None })
    }

    /// POST one JSON-RPC message with the headers this transport needs.
    async fn post(&self, msg: &Value) -> Result<reqwest::Response> {
        let mut req = self
            .http
            .post(&self.url)
            .headers(self.extra.clone())
            .header(ACCEPT, "application/json, text/event-stream")
            .json(msg);
        if let Some(sid) = &self.session_id {
            req = req.header("Mcp-Session-Id", sid);
        }
        if let Some(version) = &self.protocol {
            req = req.header("MCP-Protocol-Version", version);
        }
        req.send().await.with_context(|| format!("mcp http request to {} failed", self.url))
    }

    /// Send a request, return its `result`. If the server forgot our session
    /// (404), start a new session and send the request once more.
    pub async fn request(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<Value> {
        if let Some(res) = self.request_once(method, &params).await? {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        self.initialize().await?;
        self.request_once(method, &params)
            .await?
            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("mcp server dropped the new session too (`{method}`)"))
    }

    /// One POST. `Ok(None)` = 404 on a request that carried a session id.
    async fn request_once(&mut self, method: &str, params: &Value) -> Result<Option<Value>> {
        let id = self.next_id;
        self.next_id += 1;
        let msg = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "method": method, "params": params });
        let resp = self.post(&msg).await?;
        let status = resp.status();
        if status == reqwest::StatusCode::NOT_FOUND && self.session_id.is_some() {
            self.session_id = None;
            return Ok(None);
        }
        if !status.is_success() {
            let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
            bail!("mcp `{method}`: server returned {status}: {}", body.chars().take(300).collect::<String>());
        }
        if method == "initialize" {
            if let Some(sid) = resp.headers().get("mcp-session-id").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()) {
                self.session_id = Some(sid.to_string());
            }
        }
        let content_type = resp.headers().get(CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());
        let reply = if content_type.is_some_and(|v| v.starts_with("text/event-stream")) {
            self.read_sse(resp, id, method).await?
        } else {
            resp.json::<Value>().await.with_context(|| format!("mcp `{method}`: answer is not JSON"))?
        };
        if let Some(err) = reply.get("error") {
            bail!("mcp `{method}` failed: {err}");
        }
        if reply.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64) != Some(id) {
            bail!("mcp `{method}`: answer has the wrong id: {reply}");
        }
        Ok(Some(reply.get("result").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)))
    }

    /// Read an SSE answer until the response with our `id` arrives.
    async fn read_sse(&mut self, resp: reqwest::Response, id: i64, method: &str) -> Result<Value> {
        let mut stream = Box::pin(resp.bytes_stream());
        let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        let mut data = String::new(); // the `data:` lines of the current event
        loop {
            while let Some(pos) = buf.iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
                let raw: Vec<u8> = buf.drain(..=pos).collect();
                let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw);
                let line = line.trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
                if let Some(d) = line.strip_prefix("data:") {
                    if !data.is_empty() {
                        data.push('\n');
                    }
                    data.push_str(d.strip_prefix(' ').unwrap_or(d));
                } else if line.is_empty() && !data.is_empty() {
                    // A blank line ends one event.
                    let event = std::mem::take(&mut data);
                    if let Some(reply) = self.handle_sse_event(&event, id).await? {
                        return Ok(reply);
                    }
                }
                // `event:`, `id:`, `retry:` and `:` comment lines are ignored.
            }
            match stream.next().await {
                Some(Ok(chunk)) => buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk),
                Some(Err(e)) => bail!("mcp `{method}`: the answer stream broke: {e}"),
                None => {
                    // The last event may lack its closing blank line.
                    let event = std::mem::take(&mut data);
                    if !event.is_empty() {
                        if let Some(reply) = self.handle_sse_event(&event, id).await? {
                            return Ok(reply);
                        }
                    }
                    bail!("mcp `{method}`: server closed the stream without an answer");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// One SSE event: returned when it is our response. Server requests are
    /// answered; notifications (progress, logs) are skipped.
    async fn handle_sse_event(&mut self, event: &str, id: i64) -> Result<Option<Value>> {
        let Ok(msg) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(event) else { return Ok(None) };
        if msg.get("method").is_some() && msg.get("id").is_some() {
            let answer = if msg["method"] == "ping" {
                json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "result": {} })
            } else {
                let error = json!({ "code": -32601, "message": "not supported by this client" });
                json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "error": error })
            };
            let _ = self.post(&answer).await; // the server replies 202
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok((msg.get("id").and_then(Value::as_i64) == Some(id)).then_some(msg))
    }

    /// Send a notification; servers answer 202 with no body.
    async fn notify(&self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Result<()> {
        let resp = self.post(&json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params })).await?;
        if !resp.status().is_success() {
            bail!("mcp notification `{method}`: server returned {}", resp.status());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Start a session: `initialize`, keep the session id and the version the
    /// server chose, then send `notifications/initialized`.
    pub async fn initialize(&mut self) -> Result<Value> {
        self.session_id = None;
        self.protocol = None;
        let params = json!({
            "protocolVersion": HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
            "capabilities": {},
            "clientInfo": { "name": "opencode-rust", "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") }
        });
        let answer = tokio::time::timeout(INIT_TIMEOUT, self.request_once("initialize", &params))
            .await
            .context("mcp initialize timed out")?;
        let res = match answer {
            Ok(Some(res)) => res,
            Ok(None) => bail!("mcp initialize: unexpected 404"),
            Err(e) => {
                // A server that only speaks 2026-07-28 rejects `initialize`
                // and names the versions it supports.
                let text = format!("{e:#}");
                if text.contains("2026-07-28") {
                    bail!("{text} (this server only speaks MCP 2026-07-28, which has no `initialize`; \
                           opencode-rust's HTTP client speaks {HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION})");
                }
                return Err(e);
            }
        };
        let version = res.get("protocolVersion").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or(HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION);
        self.protocol = Some(version.to_string()); // accept whatever the server chose
        self.notify("notifications/initialized", json!({})).await?;
        Ok(res)
    }

    /// `tools/list`, following `nextCursor` to read every page.
    pub async fn list_tools(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<McpTool>> {
        let mut tools = Vec::new();
        let mut cursor: Option<String> = None;
        for _page in 0..100 {
            let params = match &cursor {
                Some(c) => json!({ "cursor": c }),
                None => json!({}),
            };
            let res = tokio::time::timeout(LIST_TIMEOUT, self.request("tools/list", params))
                .await
                .context("mcp tools/list timed out")??;
            let arr = res
                .get("tools")
                .and_then(Value::as_array)
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("tools/list response has no `tools` array"))?;
            // One malformed entry must not drop the whole server (as in B-28).
            tools.extend(arr.iter().filter_map(|t| serde_json::from_value::<McpTool>(t.clone()).ok()));
            cursor = res.get("nextCursor").and_then(Value::as_str).map(String::from);
            if cursor.is_none() {
                break;
            }
        }
        Ok(tools)
    }

    /// `tools/call`: the text parts joined by newlines; `isError: true` comes
    /// back as `Err` with that text (same rules as the stdio client).
    pub async fn call_tool(&mut self, name: &str, args: &Value) -> Result<String> {
        let params = json!({ "name": name, "arguments": args });
        let res = tokio::time::timeout(CALL_TIMEOUT, self.request("tools/call", params))
            .await
            .context("mcp tools/call timed out")??;
        let is_error = res.get("isError").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false);
        let parts = res.get("content").and_then(Value::as_array).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        let text = parts
            .iter()
            .filter(|p| p.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("text"))
            .filter_map(|p| p.get("text").and_then(Value::as_str))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n");
        if is_error {
            bail!("{}", if text.is_empty() { "tool error" } else { text.as_str() });
        }
        Ok(if text.is_empty() { "(no output)".to_string() } else { text })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use axum::http::{header, HeaderMap, StatusCode};
    use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
    use axum::{extract::State, routing::post, Json, Router};
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

    /// What the fake MCP server remembers. `pub(super)`: Stage 3 reuses it.
    #[derive(Default)]
    pub(super) struct Fake {
        sse: bool,          // answer with SSE streams instead of JSON bodies
        session: String,    // current session id: "s1", then "s2", …
        sessions: u32,      // how many sessions were started
        expire_once: bool,  // answer the next request with 404 once
        ping_answers: u32,  // how many of our pings the client answered
    }

    pub(super) type FakeState = Arc<Mutex<Fake>>;

    async fn fake_mcp(State(st): State<FakeState>, headers: HeaderMap, Json(msg): Json<Value>) -> Response {
        let header = |name: &str| headers.get(name).and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        if header("x-test") != "1" {
            return StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED.into_response(); // the config header must arrive
        }
        let mut f = st.lock().unwrap();
        let Some(method) = msg.get("method").and_then(Value::as_str) else {
            if msg["result"].is_object() {
                f.ping_answers += 1; // the client's answer to our ping
            }
            return StatusCode::ACCEPTED.into_response();
        };
        if method == "initialize" {
            f.sessions += 1;
            f.session = format!("s{}", f.sessions);
            let result = json!({ "protocolVersion": HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION, "capabilities": { "tools": {} } });
            let reply = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "result": result });
            return ([("mcp-session-id", f.session.clone())], Json(reply)).into_response();
        }
        if f.expire_once || header("mcp-session-id") != f.session {
            f.expire_once = false;
            return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
        }
        if header("mcp-protocol-version") != HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION {
            return StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST.into_response();
        }
        if msg.get("id").is_none() {
            return StatusCode::ACCEPTED.into_response(); // notifications/initialized
        }
        let tool = |name: &str| json!({ "name": name, "inputSchema": { "type": "object" } });
        let result = match method {
            "tools/list" if msg["params"]["cursor"] == "p2" => json!({ "tools": [tool("shout")] }),
            "tools/list" => json!({ "tools": [tool("echo")], "nextCursor": "p2" }),
            "tools/call" => {
                let text = msg["params"]["arguments"]["text"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
                json!({ "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": format!("echo: {text}") }] })
            }
            _ => json!({}),
        };
        let reply = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": msg["id"], "result": result });
        if !f.sse {
            return Json(reply).into_response();
        }
        // SSE: a progress notification, a `ping` request, then the answer.
        let progress = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/progress", "params": {} });
        let ping = json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "srv-1", "method": "ping" });
        let body = format!("data: {progress}\n\nevent: message\ndata: {ping}\n\ndata: {reply}\n\n");
        ([(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "text/event-stream")], body).into_response()
    }

    /// Start the fake server; returns its endpoint URL and its state.
    pub(super) async fn start(fake: Fake) -> (String, FakeState) {
        let st: FakeState = Arc::new(Mutex::new(fake));
        let app = Router::new().route("/mcp", post(fake_mcp)).with_state(st.clone());
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)).await.unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _ = axum::serve(listener, app).await;
        });
        (format!("http://{addr}/mcp"), st)
    }

    /// The config header the fake server requires (stands in for a token).
    pub(super) fn test_headers() -> HashMap<String, String> {
        HashMap::from([("X-Test".to_string(), "1".to_string())])
    }

    async fn handshake_list_call(sse: bool) {
        let (url, st) = start(Fake { sse, ..Default::default() }).await;
        let mut c = HttpClient::new(&url, &test_headers()).unwrap();
        c.initialize().await.unwrap();
        let names: Vec<String> = c.list_tools().await.unwrap().into_iter().map(|t| t.name).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, vec!["echo", "shout"], "both pages of tools/list are read");
        assert_eq!(c.call_tool("echo", &json!({ "text": "hi" })).await.unwrap(), "echo: hi");
        if sse {
            assert_eq!(st.lock().unwrap().ping_answers, 3, "every server ping was answered");
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn json_answers_work() {
        handshake_list_call(false).await;
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sse_answers_work() {
        handshake_list_call(true).await;
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn expired_session_is_renewed_once() {
        let (url, st) = start(Fake::default()).await;
        let mut c = HttpClient::new(&url, &test_headers()).unwrap();
        c.initialize().await.unwrap();
        st.lock().unwrap().expire_once = true;
        assert_eq!(c.call_tool("echo", &json!({ "text": "again" })).await.unwrap(), "echo: again");
        assert_eq!(st.lock().unwrap().sessions, 2, "a new session was started");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn missing_header_and_bad_header_names_are_clear_errors() {
        let (url, _st) = start(Fake::default()).await;
        let err = HttpClient::new(&url, &HashMap::new()).unwrap().initialize().await.unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("401"), "{err}");
        let bad = HashMap::from([("bad name".to_string(), "x".to_string())]);
        assert!(HttpClient::new(&url, &bad).is_err());
    }
}
```

- [ ] `cargo build` shows no warnings

#### Do not

- Do not send `"2026-07-28"` as `protocolVersion` in `initialize`: that
  revision has no `initialize`, so a server may then expect stateless
  requests. Use `HTTP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` ("2025-11-25").
- Do not ignore server requests on an SSE stream: an unanswered `ping`
  leaves the server waiting and the tool call hangs until its timeout.
- Do not print header values (tokens) in errors or logs.
- Do not use plain `http://` for remote servers: tokens in `headers` would
  travel unencrypted. Use `https://` (plain `http://` only for `127.0.0.1`).
- Do not call an HTTP server while holding B-20's registry lock; go through
  `Registry::route` as B-20 does for stdio.

Sources (checked 2026-10-22): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification
(latest revision 2026-07-28: its changelog, and `basic/transports/streamable-http`,
section "Backward Compatibility") and
https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports
(Streamable HTTP: Session Management, Protocol Version Header).

#### What is wrong

The agent can navigate, read, click and type in the preview panel, but it cannot
take a screenshot. `GOALS.md` lists `browser_screenshot` as "not verified / not
built". The tool should save a PNG of the panel and return its file path.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/browser.rs`:
```rust
                .call("wait", json!({ "selector": selector, "text": text, "ms": ms }))
                .await
        }
        _ => return None,
```

#### Why it matters

Without it the agent cannot hand the user a picture of what the page looks like
(for a bug report, a before/after, a layout check).

#### Steps

Before you start:

- The capture uses WebView2's own `ICoreWebView2::CapturePreview` (no DevTools
  protocol). It exists only on **Windows**. On Linux/macOS the tool answers
  "needs the Windows desktop app". The model only gets the path and size; it
  cannot see the image.
- The new direct dependencies MUST have the versions wry already uses
  (`Cargo.lock`: `webview2-com 0.39.1`, `windows 0.62.2`). With any other version
  wry's `ICoreWebView2` and yours are different types and nothing compiles.
- This task was NOT compiled on Windows by the planner. The Windows-only
  functions were type-checked in a small separate crate against
  `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with exactly these crate versions; the rest was
  compiled and tested on Linux. Build and try it on Windows yourself.

```rust
/// New (F-04): save a PNG of what the preview shows and answer the tool with
/// its path. Windows only: WebView2's own `CapturePreview` (no DevTools
/// protocol needed).
#[cfg(windows)]
fn capture_screenshot(
    wv: &wry::WebView,
    reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<String, String>>,
) {
    use std::cell::RefCell;
    use std::rc::Rc;
    use webview2_com::CapturePreviewCompletedHandler;
    use webview2_com::Microsoft::Web::WebView2::Win32::COREWEBVIEW2_CAPTURE_PREVIEW_IMAGE_FORMAT_PNG;
    use windows::Win32::UI::Shell::SHCreateMemStream;
    use wry::WebViewExtWindows;

    // SAFETY: SHCreateMemStream has no preconditions; it returns an owned
    // in-memory COM stream (None when out of memory).
    let Some(stream) = (unsafe { SHCreateMemStream(None) }) else {
        let _ = reply.send(Err("could not create a memory stream".into()));
        return;
    };
    // The completion callback and the error path below share the reply:
    // whichever runs first sends it.
    let slot = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Some(reply)));
    let slot_cb = slot.clone();
    let stream_cb = stream.clone();
    let handler = CapturePreviewCompletedHandler::create(Box::new(move |result| {
        let out = result
            .map_err(|e| format!("capture failed: {e}"))
            .and_then(|()| read_stream(&stream_cb))
            .and_then(|png| save_screenshot(&png));
        if let Some(tx) = slot_cb.borrow_mut().take() {
            let _ = tx.send(out);
        }
        Ok(())
    }));
    // SAFETY: the webview, `stream` and `handler` are valid COM objects;
    // WebView2 calls `handler` once, on this (the UI) thread.
    let started = unsafe {
        wv.webview()
            .CapturePreview(COREWEBVIEW2_CAPTURE_PREVIEW_IMAGE_FORMAT_PNG, &stream, &handler)
    };
    if let Err(e) = started {
        if let Some(tx) = slot.borrow_mut().take() {
            let _ = tx.send(Err(format!("capture failed: {e}")));
        }
    }
}

/// New (F-04): read a whole COM stream into memory.
#[cfg(windows)]
fn read_stream(stream: &windows::Win32::System::Com::IStream) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    use windows::Win32::System::Com::{STREAM_SEEK_END, STREAM_SEEK_SET};
    let mut size = 0u64;
    // SAFETY: plain IStream calls on a valid stream; `buf` outlives `Read`.
    unsafe {
        stream
            .Seek(0, STREAM_SEEK_END, Some(&mut size as *mut u64))
            .map_err(|e| format!("reading the capture: {e}"))?;
        stream
            .Seek(0, STREAM_SEEK_SET, None)
            .map_err(|e| format!("reading the capture: {e}"))?;
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; size as usize];
        let mut read = 0u32;
        stream
            .Read(buf.as_mut_ptr().cast(), buf.len() as u32, Some(&mut read as *mut u32))
            .ok()
            .map_err(|e| format!("reading the capture: {e}"))?;
        buf.truncate(read as usize);
        Ok(buf)
    }
}

/// New (F-04): store a PNG in the temp folder and describe it for the model.
/// Platform-neutral, so it is unit-tested everywhere.
#[cfg_attr(not(windows), allow(dead_code))]
fn save_screenshot(png: &[u8]) -> Result<String, String> {
    const SIGNATURE: &[u8] = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n";
    if png.len() < 24 || &png[..8] != SIGNATURE {
        return Err("the capture is not a PNG image".into());
    }
    // The IHDR chunk always comes first: width and height, big-endian u32.
    let width = u32::from_be_bytes([png[16], png[17], png[18], png[19]]);
    let height = u32::from_be_bytes([png[20], png[21], png[22], png[23]]);
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("opencode-rust-screenshots");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", dir.display()))?;
    let stamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let path = dir.join(format!("shot-{stamp}.png"));
    std::fs::write(&path, png).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(serde_json::json!({
        "ok": true,
        "path": path.display().to_string(),
        "width": width,
        "height": height,
        "bytes": png.len(),
    })
    .to_string())
}

fn tracing_boot(boot_ms: u128, addr: std::net::SocketAddr, session: &str) {
    eprintln!("[habi] ready in {boot_ms}ms \u{b7} core at http://{addr} \u{b7} session {session}");
}
```

### F-05 · Git-worktree isolation for worker subagents and team workers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | L (a day or more) |
| Depends on | B-06 (one call passes B-06's abort flag; see the note in step 9) |
| Files to change | `src/worktree.rs` (new), `src/lib.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `src/subagent.rs`, `src/team.rs`, `config.example.toml` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `struct LoopOpts`, `pub async fn run_loop`, `async fn execute_routed`, `fn tool_detail`, `async fn run_parallel`; `src/subagent.rs`: `pub async fn spawn_subagent`; `src/team.rs`: `async fn run_worker_agent`; `src/gitsnap.rs`: `pub fn git` |

#### What is wrong

Parallel `worker` subagents (several `spawn` calls in one turn) and `/team`
workers all edit the same working tree at the same time. Two workers can
overwrite each other's edits, and a half-done worker leaves its changes
straight in the user's files. Only `/parallel` uses git worktrees today, and
there is no option to isolate workers.

#### Where it is

The per-run settings have no folder of their own. Every run's tools use
`st.workspace`, the session workspace (`src/server.rs`, around line 914):

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
/// Per-run loop configuration (who is running and with what privileges).
pub struct LoopOpts {
    /// Fully composed system prompt.
    pub system: String,
    /// Emit ToolStarted/ToolFinished to the event bus (main agent: yes,
    /// team workers/subagents: no — their summary comes back as text).
    pub emit_activity: bool,
    /// Restrict the run to these tool names (subagent role). `None` = the
    /// session's plan/build mode decides the base restriction.
    pub allow: Option<Vec<String>>,
    /// May this run call the `spawn` tool? Only the top-level agent can.
    pub can_spawn: bool,
    /// M7: this run is a spawned subagent — status goes to the agents panel.
    pub agent: Option<AgentInfo>,
}
```

#### Why it matters

Two workers that touch the same file produce a mix of both edits that nobody
asked for. A worker that goes wrong cannot be thrown away cleanly: its edits
are already mixed with the user's own uncommitted work.

#### Steps

How it works (read this first):

- New config `agent.isolate_workers` (default `false`). When it is on and the
  workspace is a git repository with at least one commit, every `worker`
  subagent and every team worker gets its own git worktree under
  `<state_dir>/workers/`. (A worktree is a second checkout of the same
  repository in another folder, on its own branch.)
- The worktree starts from a snapshot of the CURRENT files: a temporary commit
  built with a private index file (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`). So uncommitted and new
  files are included, and the user's own index and files are never touched.
  This matters because the parent agent often writes files just before it
  spawns workers.
- When the worker is done, its changes are saved with `git diff --binary` to
  `<state_dir>/worker-patches/<name>.patch`. The worker's summary gets the
  patch path, the exact `git apply` command and a `--stat` summary. Nothing is
  applied: the parent agent decides, and its `bash` call goes through the
  normal approval. The same report reaches the user as a `ServerEvent::Note`
  in the parent session.
- The worktree and its branch are always removed. If the patch cannot be
  saved, the worktree is kept and the report says where. If the run is
  aborted (or fails), the worktree is removed and its changes are dropped.
- No git repository (or no commit yet, or the state dir lies inside the repo):
  the worker runs in the real workspace as today, and the report says why.
- How a child run gets another folder: a new field `workspace` in `LoopOpts`.
  `run_loop` uses it for the file and shell tools and for permission details.
  Not an ephemeral `AppState` like `/parallel` uses: that state has its own
  approvals map, event bus, database and MCP processes. Worker approval
  prompts would never reach the UI (they time out as denials), the agents
  panel would stay empty, the child session would vanish, and every worker
  would start its own MCP servers. With the field, the worker shares all of
  that with the parent; only its folder changes.
- MCP servers and the browser act on the real workspace, so an isolated worker
  only gets the built-in tools (the names from `tools::tool_specs()`).
- Other tasks: B-18 rewrites `worker()` and the top of `run_worker_agent` in
  `src/team.rs`; this task only adds code further down, so either order works.
  B-25 fixes `/parallel` and may reuse `worktree::Worktree`; no dependency.
- Known limits: the git commands run synchronously (as `/parallel` does
  today), so in a very large repository a worker takes a moment to start. Big
  untracked files that are not in `.gitignore` are copied into the snapshot too.

```rust
//! F-05: git-worktree isolation for `worker` subagents and team workers.
//!
//! With `agent.isolate_workers = true`, each worker gets its own git worktree
//! under the state dir. The worktree starts from a snapshot of the CURRENT
//! files (uncommitted and untracked files included). When the worker is
//! done, its changes are saved as a patch file and described in its summary.
//! Nothing is applied to the real workspace: the parent agent or the user
//! decides. The worktree and its branch are removed afterwards.

use crate::gitsnap::git;
use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Context, Result};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

/// One worker's private checkout. Dropping it removes the worktree and its
/// branch, unless `keep` is set (the changes could not be saved).
pub struct Worktree {
    /// Root of the real repository. Git commands run here; patch paths are
    /// relative to it.
    root: PathBuf,
    /// The worktree folder, under `<state_dir>/workers/`.
    dir: PathBuf,
    /// Where the workspace sits inside the repo: "" or "sub/dir".
    prefix: String,
    /// The commit the worktree starts from (a snapshot of the current files).
    base: String,
    branch: String,
    name: String,
    keep: bool,
}

/// Run git with a private index file and a fixed identity, so the user's
/// real index is never touched and `commit-tree` works without a git user.
fn git_private_index(cwd: &Path, index: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String> {
    let out = Command::new("git")
        .args(args)
        .current_dir(cwd)
        .env("GIT_INDEX_FILE", index)
        .env("GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "opencode-rust")
        .env("GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL", "opencode-rust@localhost")
        .env("GIT_COMMITTER_NAME", "opencode-rust")
        .env("GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL", "opencode-rust@localhost")
        .output()
        .with_context(|| format!("running git {}", args.join(" ")))?;
    if !out.status.success() {
        bail!("git {} failed: {}", args.join(" "), String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim());
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned())
}

impl Worktree {
    /// Make a worktree for one worker. The error text says why not (shown to
    /// the parent and the user): no git repository, no commit yet, ...
    pub fn create(workspace: &Path, state_dir: &Path, label: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let inside = git(workspace, &["rev-parse", "--is-inside-work-tree"])
            .map(|s| s.trim() == "true")
            .unwrap_or(false);
        if !inside {
            bail!("the workspace is not a git repository");
        }
        let head = git(workspace, &["rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD"])
            .map_err(|_| anyhow!("the repository has no commit yet"))?
            .trim()
            .to_string();
        let root = PathBuf::from(git(workspace, &["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"])?.trim());
        let prefix = git(workspace, &["rev-parse", "--show-prefix"])?
            .trim()
            .trim_end_matches('/')
            .to_string();
        let workers = std::path::absolute(state_dir.join("workers"))?;
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&workers)?;
        // `git add -A` below must never pick up our own worktrees.
        let canon = |p: &Path| std::fs::canonicalize(p).unwrap_or_else(|_| p.to_path_buf());
        if canon(&workers).starts_with(canon(&root)) {
            bail!("the state dir {} is inside the repository", state_dir.display());
        }
        static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
        let stamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_millis())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        let name = format!("{label}-{stamp}-{}", COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed));
        let dir = workers.join(&name);
        let index = workers.join(format!("{name}.index"));
        // Snapshot the current files (changes and untracked files, not ignored
        // ones) as a commit, through the private index.
        let snapshot = (|| -> Result<String> {
            git_private_index(&root, &index, &["read-tree", &head])?;
            git_private_index(&root, &index, &["add", "-A"])?;
            let tree = git_private_index(&root, &index, &["write-tree"])?;
            let args = ["commit-tree", "--no-gpg-sign", tree.trim(), "-p", head.as_str(), "-m", "worker base"];
            Ok(git_private_index(&root, &index, &args)?.trim().to_string())
        })();
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&index);
        let base = snapshot?;
        let branch = format!("ocrs/{name}");
        let dir_arg = dir.to_string_lossy().to_string();
        let _ = git(&root, &["worktree", "prune"]); // forget worktrees whose folder is gone
        git(&root, &["worktree", "add", "-b", &branch, &dir_arg, &base])?;
        Ok(Self { root, dir, prefix, base, branch, name, keep: false })
    }

    /// The folder the worker works in: the worktree plus the same subfolder
    /// the real workspace has inside the repository.
    pub fn workspace(&self) -> PathBuf {
        if self.prefix.is_empty() {
            self.dir.clone()
        } else {
            self.dir.join(&self.prefix)
        }
    }

    /// Save the worker's changes as a patch and describe them for the parent.
    /// If saving fails, the worktree is kept so no work is lost.
    fn report(&mut self, patch_dir: &Path) -> String {
        match self.save_patch(patch_dir) {
            Ok(text) => text,
            Err(e) => {
                self.keep = true;
                format!(
                    "[isolated worktree] could not save the changes as a patch ({e:#}). \
                     They are kept in {} on branch {}.",
                    self.dir.display(),
                    self.branch
                )
            }
        }
    }

    fn save_patch(&self, patch_dir: &Path) -> Result<String> {
        git(&self.dir, &["add", "-A"])?;
        let patch_dir = std::path::absolute(patch_dir)?;
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&patch_dir)?;
        let patch = patch_dir.join(format!("{}.patch", self.name));
        let output = format!("--output={}", patch.display());
        let mut diff = vec!["diff", "--cached", "--binary", output.as_str(), self.base.as_str()];
        let mut stat = vec!["diff", "--cached", "--stat", "--stat-count=20", self.base.as_str()];
        if !self.prefix.is_empty() {
            // Only changes inside the workspace folder come back.
            diff.extend(["--", self.prefix.as_str()]);
            stat.extend(["--", self.prefix.as_str()]);
        }
        git(&self.dir, &diff)?;
        if std::fs::metadata(&patch).map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0) == 0 {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&patch);
            return Ok("[isolated worktree] no file changes.".to_string());
        }
        let stat = git(&self.dir, &stat)?;
        let (p, r) = (patch.display(), self.root.display());
        Ok(format!(
            "[isolated worktree] changes saved as a patch, NOT applied to the workspace yet.\n\
             Patch: {p}\n\
             To apply: run `git -C \"{r}\" apply --check \"{p}\"`, then the same without --check.\n\
             If it does not apply cleanly, tell the user instead of forcing it.\n{}",
            stat.trim_end()
        ))
    }
}

impl Drop for Worktree {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.keep {
            return;
        }
        let dir = self.dir.to_string_lossy().to_string();
        let _ = git(&self.root, &["worktree", "remove", "--force", &dir]);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.dir);
        let _ = git(&self.root, &["worktree", "prune"]);
        let _ = git(&self.root, &["branch", "-D", &self.branch]);
    }
}

/// A worker's isolation: its worktree, or the reason it runs without one.
pub enum Isolation {
    Worktree(Worktree),
    Skipped(String),
}

impl Isolation {
    /// Never fails. When no worktree can be made, the worker runs in the real
    /// workspace as before, and the reason is reported.
    pub fn start(workspace: &Path, state_dir: &Path, label: &str) -> Self {
        match Worktree::create(workspace, state_dir, label) {
            Ok(wt) => Isolation::Worktree(wt),
            Err(e) => Isolation::Skipped(format!("{e:#}")),
        }
    }

    /// The folder for the worker's tools. `None` = the real workspace.
    pub fn workspace(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        match self {
            Isolation::Worktree(wt) => Some(wt.workspace()),
            Isolation::Skipped(_) => None,
        }
    }

    /// Why there is no worktree (`None` when the worker is isolated).
    pub fn skipped(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Isolation::Skipped(reason) => Some(reason.as_str()),
            Isolation::Worktree(_) => None,
        }
    }

    /// Text for the worker's summary: the patch report, or why the worker
    /// was not isolated. Removes the worktree.
    pub fn finish(self, state_dir: &Path) -> String {
        match self {
            Isolation::Worktree(mut wt) => wt.report(&state_dir.join("worker-patches")),
            Isolation::Skipped(reason) => {
                format!("[not isolated: {reason}; this worker changed the workspace directly]")
            }
        }
    }
}

/// System-prompt text for a worker that runs in its own worktree.
pub fn isolation_prompt(ws: &Path) -> String {
    format!(
        "\n\n## Isolated copy\n\nYou work in a private git worktree at {}: a full copy of \
         the project. Use this folder instead of any other workspace path named above. Use \
         relative paths and stay inside this folder. Do not commit. When you finish, your \
         changes are collected as a patch for the main agent.",
        ws.display()
    )
}

/// Tools an isolated worker may use: the built-in ones. MCP servers and the
/// browser act on the real workspace, so they would break the isolation.
pub fn local_tool_names() -> Vec<String> {
    crate::tools::tool_specs().into_iter().map(|s| s.function.name).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn temp(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let stamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap()
            .as_nanos();
        let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ocrs-wt-{tag}-{}-{stamp}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&p).unwrap();
        p
    }

    fn read(p: &Path) -> String {
        std::fs::read_to_string(p).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// A worker starts from the current files, its changes come back as a
    /// patch that applies on the real (dirty) workspace, and nothing is left.
    #[test]
    fn worker_changes_come_back_as_a_patch() {
        let repo = temp("repo");
        let state = temp("state");
        git(&repo, &["init", "-q"]).unwrap();
        git(&repo, &["config", "user.email", "t@t"]).unwrap();
        git(&repo, &["config", "user.name", "t"]).unwrap();
        git(&repo, &["config", "commit.gpgsign", "false"]).unwrap();
        git(&repo, &["config", "core.autocrlf", "false"]).unwrap(); // exact bytes on Windows too
        std::fs::write(repo.join("a.txt"), "one\n").unwrap();
        git(&repo, &["add", "-A"]).unwrap();
        git(&repo, &["commit", "-q", "-m", "init"]).unwrap();
        // Uncommitted work the worker must see.
        std::fs::write(repo.join("a.txt"), "two\n").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(repo.join("u.txt"), "untracked\n").unwrap();
        let status_before = git(&repo, &["status", "--porcelain"]).unwrap();

        let iso = Isolation::start(&repo, &state, "worker");
        let ws = iso.workspace().expect("a git repo gets a worktree");
        assert_eq!(read(&ws.join("a.txt")), "two\n");
        assert_eq!(read(&ws.join("u.txt")), "untracked\n");
        let status_now = git(&repo, &["status", "--porcelain"]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(status_now, status_before, "real index and files untouched");

        // The "worker": edit one file, add another.
        std::fs::write(ws.join("a.txt"), "three\n").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(ws.join("new.txt"), "from worker\n").unwrap();
        let report = iso.finish(&state);
        assert!(report.contains("NOT applied"), "{report}");
        assert!(report.contains("2 files changed"), "{report}");
        assert!(!ws.exists(), "worktree folder removed");
        let branches = git(&repo, &["branch", "--list", "ocrs/*"]).unwrap();
        assert!(branches.trim().is_empty(), "branch deleted: {branches}");
        assert_eq!(read(&repo.join("a.txt")), "two\n", "nothing applied yet");

        let patch = report
            .lines()
            .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("Patch: "))
            .expect("patch path in the report")
            .to_string();
        git(&repo, &["apply", &patch]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read(&repo.join("a.txt")), "three\n");
        assert_eq!(read(&repo.join("new.txt")), "from worker\n");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&repo);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&state);
    }

    /// No git repository: the worker runs as before, and the summary says so.
    #[test]
    fn non_git_workspace_runs_without_isolation() {
        let dir = temp("plain");
        let state = temp("plain-state");
        let iso = Isolation::start(&dir, &state, "worker");
        assert!(iso.workspace().is_none());
        let reason = iso.skipped().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        assert!(reason.contains("not a git repository"), "{reason}");
        assert!(iso.finish(&state).contains("not isolated"));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&state);
    }
}
```

9. Add these helpers right after the closing brace of `async fn execute_routed`
   (around line 1569), before the doc comment
   `/// Flatten a tool's input to a human-readable detail string for rules + display.`:

```rust
/// F-05: built-in tools that take the workspace folder (cwd for `bash`,
/// base for relative paths). Only these are moved into a worker's worktree.
const WORKSPACE_TOOLS: [&str; 7] = ["bash", "read", "write", "edit", "glob", "grep", "list"];

/// F-05: like `execute_routed`, but a run with its own workspace (an
/// isolated worker) runs the workspace tools in that folder.
async fn execute_for(
    st: &Shared,
    session_id: &str,
    opts: &LoopOpts,
    name: &str,
    input: &Value,
    abort: &AtomicBool,
) -> (String, bool) {
    if let Some(ws) = &opts.workspace {
        if WORKSPACE_TOOLS.contains(&name) {
            return match tools::execute(name, input, ws, abort).await {
                Ok(out) => (out, true),
                Err(e) => (format!("error: {e}"), false),
            };
        }
    }
    execute_routed(st, session_id, name, input, abort).await
}

/// F-05: like `tool_detail`, but paths are made relative to the run's own
/// workspace when it has one, so permission rules like `src/*` still match.
fn tool_detail_for(st: &Shared, opts: &LoopOpts, tool: &str, input: &Value) -> String {
    match (&opts.workspace, tool) {
        (Some(ws), "read" | "write" | "edit" | "glob" | "grep") => {
            let p = input.get("path").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
            normalize_path_detail(ws, p)
        }
        _ => tool_detail(st, tool, input),
    }
}
```

#### Do not

- Do not branch the worktree from `HEAD` alone, the way `/parallel` does. The
  worker would miss uncommitted and new files, and its patch might not apply
  to the user's working tree.
- Do not build the snapshot with `git stash` or with `git add` on the user's own
  index. Use the private index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) exactly as written.
- Do not apply the patch automatically. The parent agent or the user decides.
- Do not give an isolated worker MCP or browser tools. They work on the real
  workspace and would bypass the isolation.
- Do not use `git diff --relative`, and do not run `git apply` inside a
  subfolder of the repo. Patch paths are relative to the repository root;
  apply with `git -C <root>`.

### F-06 · GUI: Stop button, multiline composer, IME guard

| Field | Value |
|---|---|

#### What is wrong

- The GUI has no way to stop a run. The only way is to send another message,
  which silently replaces the running work.
- The composer is a one-line `<input>`. Multi-line prompts (code, lists) are
  impossible, and the `Shift+Enter` check in the key handler does nothing.
- Enter sends even while an input method (IME, used for Chinese, Japanese,
  Korean) is still composing a word, so half-typed text is sent.

#### Where it is

```js
        if (ev.key === "Enter" && !ev.shiftKey) {
          ev.preventDefault();
          submitMessage();
        }
      });
```

#### Why it matters

A run that goes the wrong way (wrong files, endless loop) keeps working until it
ends. A follow-up typed while it runs throws away its work without asking.

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (F-06): ask the run of chat `session_id` to stop. Same effect as
/// `POST /api/sessions/{id}/abort`: set the run's abort flag. A run started
/// a moment ago may not be registered yet, so look for up to one second.
/// Returns false when no run showed up.
async fn request_stop(st: &server::AppState, session_id: &str) -> bool {
    for _ in 0..10 {
        if let Some(flag) = st.busy.read().await.get(session_id) {
            flag.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
            return true;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
    }
    false
}
```

<!-- TASK:F-07 -->
### F-07 · Automatic compaction near the context limit

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | B-05 (safe compaction; this task calls `compact::compact` from the agent loop and edits a line B-05 wrote) |
| Files to change | `src/config.rs`, `src/compact.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `config.example.toml` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn run_loop`, `fn build_chat_messages`; `src/compact.rs`: `fn compact`, `fn render_transcript` |

#### What is wrong

Compaction only happens when the user types `/compact`. A long agent run
keeps adding tool output until the request no longer fits the model's
context window. Many local servers then cut the start of the prompt (often
the system prompt and the task), and the model loses track. The repo's own
Kaggle setup (`kaggle_setup_cell.py`) runs Ollama with an 8,192-token
context, which a few file reads already fill.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
            return Ok("aborted".into());
        }
        let msgs = build_chat_messages(st, session_id, &opts.system)?;
```

#### Why it matters

With a small context the agent silently forgets its instructions in the
middle of a run. Compacting a little early keeps the task, the decisions and
the recent tail.

#### Steps

New setting `agent.context_tokens` (new): the model's context size in
tokens. `0` (the default) turns the feature off. When it is set, the agent
loop estimates the size of the next request (characters / 4, for the
messages that `build_chat_messages` produces plus the tool list). At 80% or
more it compacts first and shows a Note in the chat. If compaction is not
possible (too few messages, summarizer error), it notes that once and does
not retry until the session has new messages.

```rust
/// Serialize the prefix for the summarizer, keeping the *most recent* part
/// when it exceeds the budget (recent context matters most).
pub fn render_transcript(lines: &[String]) -> String {
    let text = lines.join("\n");
    if text.len() <= BUDGET {
        return text;
    }
    let mut start = text.len() - BUDGET;
    while !text.is_char_boundary(start) {
        start += 1;
    }
    format!("… [older transcript truncated]\n{}", &text[start..])
}
```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// Serialize the prefix for the summarizer, keeping the *most recent* part
/// when it exceeds the budget (recent context matters most).
pub fn render_transcript(lines: &[String]) -> String {
    render_transcript_within(lines, BUDGET)
}

/// [`render_transcript`] with an explicit byte budget.
pub fn render_transcript_within(lines: &[String], budget: usize) -> String {
    let text = lines.join("\n");
    if text.len() <= budget {
        return text;
    }
    let mut start = text.len() - budget;
    while !text.is_char_boundary(start) {
        start += 1;
    }
    format!("… [older transcript truncated]\n{}", &text[start..])
}
```

```rust
/// F-07: rough size of the next request in tokens: about 4 characters per
/// token for the messages and the tool list. Good enough to decide when to
/// compact; not a billing number.
fn estimate_tokens(msgs: &[ChatMsg], specs: &[crate::provider::ToolSpec]) -> usize {
    let mut chars = serde_json::to_string(specs).map_or(0, |s| s.len());
    for m in msgs {
        chars += m.role.len() + m.content.as_deref().map_or(0, str::len) + 8;
        for c in m.tool_calls.iter().flatten() {
            chars += c.function.name.len() + c.function.arguments.len() + 16;
        }
    }
    chars / 4
}

/// F-07: compact the session when the next request would use 80% or more
/// of `agent.context_tokens`. A failed attempt is remembered per session
/// (by message count), so it is not retried on every step.
async fn auto_compact_if_needed(
    st: &Shared,
    session_id: &str,
    system: &str,
    specs: &[crate::provider::ToolSpec],
    abort: &AtomicBool,
) {
    static FAILED_AT: std::sync::OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, usize>>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    let limit = st.cfg.agent.context_tokens;
    if limit == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let Ok(msgs) = build_chat_messages(st, session_id, system) else { return };
    let used = estimate_tokens(&msgs, specs);
    if used.saturating_mul(5) < limit.saturating_mul(4) {
        return;
    }
    let failed = FAILED_AT.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
    let tried_here = failed
        .lock()
        .map(|m| m.get(session_id) == Some(&msgs.len()))
        .unwrap_or(false);
    if tried_here {
        return;
    }
    let text = match crate::compact::compact(st, session_id, abort).await {
        Ok(o) => {
            if let Ok(mut m) = failed.lock() {
                m.remove(session_id);
            }
            format!(
                "context is ~{used} of {limit} tokens: compacted {} older message(s) into a summary",
                o.removed
            )
        }
        Err(e) => {
            if let Ok(mut m) = failed.lock() {
                m.insert(session_id.to_string(), msgs.len());
            }
            format!("context is ~{used} of {limit} tokens: automatic compaction skipped ({e})")
        }
    };
    let _ = st.events.send(ServerEvent::Note { session_id: session_id.to_string(), text });
}
```

#### What is wrong

After a run that changed files, nothing checks that the project still builds
or that its tests pass. The agent says "done", and the user finds the broken
build later. There is no setting for a check command.

#### Where it is

`run_agent` goes from the main run straight to the auto review and then to
`RunFinished` (around line 637). There is no check step.

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust

        // outside-the-diff senior-dev pass BEFORE the turn is declared done.
```

(If P-03 is already done, the `if` line right below this comment also checks
`!aborted`. That is expected.)

#### Why it matters

A model that "finishes" with failing tests hands broken code to the user. With
a check in the loop, the agent sees the failure output and fixes it while it
still has the context.

#### Steps

What you build:

- New config keys under `[agent]`: `verify_command` (string, unset = off),
  `verify_max_rounds` (default 2) and `verify_timeout_secs` (default 600).
- After a top-level run that succeeded, changed files (`touched`) and was not
  aborted, the command runs in the workspace (`sh -c` on Linux/macOS,
  `cmd /C` on Windows) with the timeout.
- Exit code 0: a note says it passed. Otherwise a user message
  "[verify] `<cmd>` failed (exit N). Output (last 4000 chars): … Fix the
  failures, then stop." is added and the agent runs again. Then the check runs
  again. After `verify_max_rounds` fix rounds a note says it still fails.
- Deny rules for `bash` still apply to the command. There is no "ask" prompt:
  the user wrote this command into the config.
- Every step is shown to the user as a `ServerEvent::Note` starting with `[verify]`.
- Never after an abort. The abort flag is checked before and after every step,
  and a running check is killed when the run is aborted.

The command runs through a small helper of its own, not through the `bash`
tool. Reason: task B-06 changes the signature of `tools::execute`, and the
helper also gives the exit code directly.

```rust
/// F-08: marks the user message that hands a failed check back to the agent.
pub const VERIFY_PREFIX: &str = "[verify]";

/// F-08 verification loop. After a top-level run that changed files, run
/// `agent.verify_command` in the workspace. When it fails, hand the output
/// back to the agent as a user message and run the agent again — at most
/// `agent.verify_max_rounds` times. Each step shows up as a `Note`.
async fn verify_after_run(st: &Shared, session_id: &str, abort: &Arc<AtomicBool>) {
    let Some(cmd) = st.cfg.agent.verify_command.as_deref().map(str::trim) else {
        return;
    };
    if cmd.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    let note = |text: String| {
        let _ = st.events.send(ServerEvent::Note { session_id: session_id.to_string(), text });
    };
    // Deny rules still apply. There is no "ask" prompt: the user set this command.
    if st.engine.evaluate("bash", cmd, |_, _| false).action == Action::Deny {
        note(format!("{VERIFY_PREFIX} skipped: a deny rule blocks `{cmd}`"));
        return;
    }
    let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(st.cfg.agent.verify_timeout_secs.max(1));
    let max_rounds = st.cfg.agent.verify_max_rounds;
    let mut round = 0;
    loop {
        if abort.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return;
        }
        note(format!("{VERIFY_PREFIX} running `{cmd}`…"));
        let result = run_verify_command(cmd, &st.workspace, timeout, abort).await;
        if abort.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return;
        }
        let (code, output) = match result {
            Ok(r) => r,
            Err(e) => {
                note(format!("{VERIFY_PREFIX} could not run `{cmd}`: {e:#}"));
                return;
            }
        };
        if code == Some(0) {
            note(format!("{VERIFY_PREFIX} `{cmd}` passed"));
            return;
        }
        let status = match code {
            Some(c) => format!("exit {c}"),
            None => "timed out or was killed".to_string(),
        };
        if round >= max_rounds {
            note(format!(
                "{VERIFY_PREFIX} `{cmd}` still fails ({status}) after {round} fix round(s) — over to you"
            ));
            return;
        }
        round += 1;
        note(format!("{VERIFY_PREFIX} `{cmd}` failed ({status}) — fix round {round} of {max_rounds}"));
        let msg = format!(
            "{VERIFY_PREFIX} `{cmd}` failed ({status}). Output (last 4000 chars):\n```\n{}\n```\n\
             Fix the failures, then stop.",
            tail_chars(&output, 4000)
        );
        if let Err(e) = agent_inner(st, session_id, &msg, abort).await {
            note(format!("{VERIFY_PREFIX} fix round failed: {e}"));
            return;
        }
    }
}

/// F-08: run the check in the workspace with a timeout. Returns the exit code
/// (`None` = timed out or killed) and stdout + stderr. Stops early on abort.
async fn run_verify_command(
    cmd: &str,
    workspace: &std::path::Path,
    timeout: std::time::Duration,
    abort: &AtomicBool,
) -> Result<(Option<i32>, String)> {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let mut command = {
        let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new("cmd");
        c.arg("/C").arg(cmd);
        c
    };
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let mut command = {
        let mut c = tokio::process::Command::new("sh");
        c.arg("-c").arg(cmd);
        c
    };
    command
        .current_dir(workspace)
        // S-05 spirit: child processes never get the provider API key.
        .env_remove("OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY")
        .stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())
        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())
        .kill_on_drop(true);
    let child = command.spawn().context("starting the verify command")?;
    let out = tokio::select! {
        r = tokio::time::timeout(timeout, child.wait_with_output()) => match r {
            Ok(r) => r.context("waiting for the verify command")?,
            Err(_) => {
                return Ok((None, format!("(stopped: no result after {}s)", timeout.as_secs())));
            }
        },
        _ = async {
            while !abort.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
            }
        } => anyhow::bail!("aborted"),
    };
    let mut text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).into_owned();
    text.push_str(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr));
    Ok((out.status.code(), text))
}

/// The last `max` characters of `s` (never splits a character).
fn tail_chars(s: &str, max: usize) -> &str {
    let count = s.chars().count();
    if count <= max {
        return s;
    }
    let start = s.char_indices().nth(count - max).map(|(i, _)| i).unwrap_or(0);
    &s[start..]
}
```

### F-09 · Loop guard: refuse the third identical tool call in a row

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P2 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn tool_allowed`, `pub async fn run_loop`, `fn finish_tool_call` |

#### What is wrong

A weak model sometimes asks for the same tool call again and again: the same
`read` of one file, or the same failing `bash` command. `run_loop` runs every
call, so the loop spins until `agent.max_steps` (40 by default) is used up.
GOALS.md item B-B5 asks for a guard ("identical tool+args 3× in a row → error
back to the model"). It was never built.

#### Where it is

The batch loop in `run_loop` (around line 1153) runs each call through the
role gate and the permission gate, then runs it. Nothing compares a call with
the one before.

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
        // Execute each tool call: role gate → permission gate → route.
        // `spawn` calls run concurrently with each other — the agents panel
        // shows the parallel work — everything else keeps its call order.
        // (Concrete boxed type: a `dyn Future + Send` here deadlocks the
        // auto-trait proof for the run_loop ↔ spawn recursion.)
        let mut spawns = Vec::new();
        for (id, name, input) in calls {
```

#### Why it matters

A stuck model burns 40 model calls (time and money) and fills the history
with copies of the same result. In default mode the user also gets the same
approval prompt again and again.

#### Steps

Rules of the guard. Keep them exactly:

- "Identical" means the same tool name and the same arguments. Arguments are
  compared as canonical JSON (object keys sorted), so key order does not matter.
- Every call the model asks for counts, in call order. That includes calls in
  the same batch and `spawn` calls. A refused call still counts, so a 4th copy
  is refused too.
- Any call that differs (other tool or other arguments) resets the count to 1.
- The 3rd identical call in a row is not run and gets no approval prompt. The
  model gets a tool error result that tells it to change its approach.
- Each `run_loop` call has its own guard. A spawned subagent runs its own
  `run_loop`, so its calls never count for the parent. A new user message
  starts a new run, so the count starts fresh.

1. Open `src/server.rs`. Find the function `tool_allowed` (around line 1032).
   Add this code right after the closing brace of `fn tool_allowed`, before the
   doc comment `/// The agent loop: load history, call model, execute tools, repeat until done.`:

```rust
/// F-09 loop guard: the third identical call in a row (same tool, same
/// arguments) is refused instead of run.
pub(crate) const LOOP_GUARD_LIMIT: u32 = 3;

/// F-09: remembers the last tool call of one run and how many times in a
/// row the model asked for exactly that call.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct LoopGuard {
    last: Option<String>,
    streak: u32,
}

impl LoopGuard {
    /// Count one requested call. Returns the error text for the model when
    /// this is the LOOP_GUARD_LIMIT-th identical call in a row (or later).
    /// Any different call resets the count.
    pub(crate) fn check(&mut self, name: &str, input: &Value) -> Option<String> {
        let key = format!("{name} {}", canonical_json(input));
        if self.last.as_deref() == Some(key.as_str()) {
            self.streak += 1;
        } else {
            self.last = Some(key);
            self.streak = 1;
        }
        if self.streak < LOOP_GUARD_LIMIT {
            return None;
        }
        Some(format!(
            "loop guard: you asked for `{name}` with exactly the same arguments {} times \
             in a row, so it was not run again. Repeating it gives the same result. \
             Change your approach: use what the earlier results told you, try different \
             arguments or another tool, or stop and tell the user what blocks you.",
            self.streak
        ))
    }
}

/// JSON text with object keys sorted at every level, so `{"a":1,"b":2}`
/// and `{"b":2,"a":1}` give the same text.
fn canonical_json(v: &Value) -> String {
    match v {
        Value::Object(map) => {
            let mut keys: Vec<&String> = map.keys().collect();
            keys.sort();
            let fields: Vec<String> = keys
                .into_iter()
                .map(|k| format!("{}:{}", Value::String(k.clone()), canonical_json(&map[k])))
                .collect();
            format!("{{{}}}", fields.join(","))
        }
        Value::Array(items) => {
            let items: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(canonical_json).collect();
            format!("[{}]", items.join(","))
        }
        other => other.to_string(),
    }
}

/// F-09: run one batch of calls past the loop guard, in call order. A
/// refused call gets its error result right away (started/finished events,
/// stats, saved tool message) and is left out; the rest come back in order.
fn apply_loop_guard(
    st: &Shared,
    opts: &LoopOpts,
    session_id: &str,
    loop_guard: &mut LoopGuard,
    calls: Vec<(String, String, Value)>,
) -> Result<Vec<(String, String, Value)>> {
    let mut keep = Vec::with_capacity(calls.len());
    for (id, name, input) in calls {
        let Some(msg) = loop_guard.check(&name, &input) else {
            keep.push((id, name, input));
            continue;
        };
        let detail = tool_detail(st, &name, &input);
        tool_started(st, opts, session_id, &id, &name, &detail);
        if opts.emit_activity {
            let _ = st.events.send(ServerEvent::Note {
                session_id: session_id.to_string(),
                text: format!("loop guard: stopped a repeated `{name}` call"),
            });
        }
        finish_tool_call(st, opts, session_id, &id, &name, &input, msg, false)?;
    }
    Ok(keep)
}
```
