### F-10 · Context7 + ast-grep MCP setup (config, docs, skill), Serena note

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P3 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | B-19 (start-up time limits, provider-safe tool names), B-20 (parallel MCP calls) |
| Files to change | `config.example.toml`, new `docs/mcp-servers.md`, new `.opencode/skills/code-research/SKILL.md`, `src/mcp.rs` (one test) |
| Read first | `config.example.toml`; `src/config.rs`: `struct McpCfg`, `struct McpServerCfg`; `src/skills.rs`: `fn load_dir` |

#### What is wrong

opencode-rust can already run MCP servers (`[[mcp.servers]]` with `name`, `command`, `args`), but `config.example.toml` does not show how, and there is no guidance for the model on when to use them. Two free servers help a coding agent a lot:
- **Context7** gives current library documentation. MIT licence, by Upstash. npm package `@upstash/context7-mcp`, tools `resolve-library-id` and `query-docs`. The API key is optional (higher rate limits) and is read from `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` or `--api-key`.
- **ast-grep MCP** gives structural code search. Tools `find_code`, `find_code_by_rule`, `dump_syntax_tree`, `test_match_code_rule`. It needs the `ast-grep` CLI and `uv`. GitHub shows an MIT `LICENSE` file, although the README itself does not mention a licence. Check that file yourself before redistributing anything; running it as a separate program needs nothing.

These facts were checked on the projects' GitHub pages and the Context7 docs (October 2026).

#### Where it is

The config format already exists, documented only in a code comment:

Find this code in `src/config.rs`:
```rust
/// M2: MCP servers to launch over stdio at boot.
///
/// ```toml
/// [[mcp.servers]]
/// name = "files"
/// command = "node"
/// args = ["/path/to/server.js"]
/// ```
```

#### Why it matters

Without a ready example, users either never enable these servers or get the Windows `npx` detail wrong, and the model does not know when the extra tools are worth calling.

#### Steps

1. Open `config.example.toml`. Add the MCP section at the end of the file. The entries are commented out, so nobody starts programs they have not installed. (A `[[mcp.servers]]` table may stand anywhere in a TOML file, so the end is fine.)

Add this at the very end of `config.example.toml`:
```toml
# MCP servers (optional). Each runs as its own program; its tools reach the
# model as mcp__<name>__<tool>. Run each command once in a terminal first:
# the first start downloads packages and can take longer than the 20-second
# start-up limit. Remove the leading "# " to enable an entry.

# Context7 - current library docs (MIT). Needs Node.js. Optional API key for
# higher rate limits: set CONTEXT7_API_KEY before starting opencode-rust.
# Windows (npx is a .cmd script, so start it through cmd):
# [[mcp.servers]]
# name = "context7"
# command = "cmd"
# args = ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]
# macOS / Linux:
# [[mcp.servers]]
# name = "context7"
# command = "npx"
# args = ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]

# ast-grep - structural code search. Needs the ast-grep CLI and uv (uvx).
# [[mcp.servers]]
# name = "ast-grep"
# command = "uvx"
# args = ["--from", "git+https://github.com/ast-grep/ast-grep-mcp", "ast-grep-server"]
```

2. Create the documentation page.

Create the new file `docs/mcp-servers.md` with this content:
```markdown
# MCP servers

opencode-rust starts each server in `[[mcp.servers]]` (see `config.example.toml`)
as a separate program and talks to it over stdin/stdout. A server's tools reach
the model as `mcp__<name>__<tool>`. Calls to MCP tools go through the normal
permission prompt, because they are unknown tools ("ask" by default). To allow
one without asking, add for example `"mcp__context7__query-docs" = "allow"`
under `[permissions.defaults]`.

## Context7 (library documentation)

- Install Node.js. Windows: `command = "cmd"`, `args = ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]`.
  macOS/Linux: `command = "npx"`, `args = ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]`.
- Optional API key (higher rate limits): set the environment variable
  `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` before starting opencode-rust. MCP servers inherit
  opencode-rust's environment, so the server sees it.
- Tools: `resolve-library-id` (find the library), `query-docs` (ask its docs).

## ast-grep (structural code search)

- Install the ast-grep CLI and uv. Then `command = "uvx"`,
  `args = ["--from", "git+https://github.com/ast-grep/ast-grep-mcp", "ast-grep-server"]`.
- Tools: `find_code`, `find_code_by_rule`, `dump_syntax_tree`, `test_match_code_rule`.

## First start

Run the exact command once in a terminal before adding it to the config. The
first run downloads packages; if that takes longer than 20 seconds, opencode-rust
gives up on the server for that session (the log says `[mcp] failed to start`).

## Serena

Serena is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Use it only as a separate MCP server
process configured in `[[mcp.servers]]` (follow Serena's own README for the
command). Never copy Serena code into this MIT-licensed repository.

## Skill

`.opencode/skills/code-research/SKILL.md` tells the model when to use these
tools. To use it in every project, copy the folder to
`%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode-rust\skills\` (Windows) or
`~/.config/opencode-rust/skills/` (macOS/Linux).
```

3. Create the skill. The skill loader reads `*/SKILL.md` in `.opencode/skills/` and uses the `name` and `description` lines.

Create the new file `.opencode/skills/code-research/SKILL.md` with this content:
```markdown
---
name: code-research
description: When to use the Context7 docs tools and the ast-grep code-search tools
---

# Code research with MCP tools

Use this skill only when tools whose names start with `mcp__context7__` or
`mcp__ast-grep__` are in your tool list. If they are not there, ignore it.

## Library documentation (Context7)

Use it before writing code against a third-party library when you are not sure
your knowledge is current: the version in Cargo.toml or package.json is newer
than you know, or the compiler says a function or field does not exist.

1. Call `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` with the library name and pick the
   best match.
2. Call `mcp__context7__query-docs` with that id and a short, specific question.
3. Follow each tool's input schema for the argument names.

Do not use it for this project's own code, or for the Rust or Python standard
library when you already know the answer.

## Structural code search (ast-grep)

Use it when plain `grep` gives too many false hits, for example "every call to
`foo` with two arguments" or "every `unwrap()` inside an async function".

1. If you are not sure how a construct looks to ast-grep, call
   `mcp__ast-grep__dump_syntax_tree` on a small code sample first.
2. Search with `mcp__ast-grep__find_code`. In patterns, `$NAME` matches one
   syntax node and `$$$ARGS` matches any number of them.
3. For conditions such as "inside" or "not inside", write a YAML rule, check it
   with `mcp__ast-grep__test_match_code_rule` on a sample, then run
   `mcp__ast-grep__find_code_by_rule`.

Use the normal `grep` tool for simple text searches; it is faster.
```

```rust
/// Per-session todo store in SQLite, so a restart keeps the list.
/// `new()`/`default()` keep it in memory; `open(path)` uses a database file.
pub struct TodoStore {
    conn: Mutex<Connection>,
}

const TODO_SCHEMA: &str = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    completed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_todos_session ON todos(session_id, created_at);";

impl Default for TodoStore {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl TodoStore {
    /// In-memory store (tests, ephemeral runs).
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let conn = Connection::open_in_memory().expect("in-memory SQLite");
        conn.execute_batch(TODO_SCHEMA).expect("todo table");
        Self { conn: Mutex::new(conn) }
    }

    /// Store kept in the database file at `path` (the same file as `Db`).
    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
        let conn = Connection::open(path)?;
        conn.execute_batch(TODO_SCHEMA)?;
        Ok(Self { conn: Mutex::new(conn) })
    }
```

6. Replace `list_all` and add the SQL helpers (new: `row_item`, `list_sql`,
   `exec_sql`) after the end of `impl TodoStore`.

Find this code in `src/todo.rs`:
```rust

Replace it with:
```rust
    pub fn list_all(&self, session_id: &str) -> Vec<TodoItem> {
        let conn = self.conn.lock().unwrap();
        list_sql(&conn, session_id).unwrap_or_default()
    }
}

fn row_item(r: &rusqlite::Row) -> rusqlite::Result<TodoItem> {
    Ok(TodoItem { id: r.get(0)?, content: r.get(1)?, completed: r.get::<_, i64>(2)? != 0 })
}

fn list_sql(conn: &Connection, session_id: &str) -> rusqlite::Result<Vec<TodoItem>> {
    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(
        "SELECT id, content, completed FROM todos WHERE session_id=?1 ORDER BY created_at, rowid",
    )?;
    let rows = stmt.query_map(params![session_id], row_item)?;
    rows.collect()
}

fn exec_sql(conn: &Connection, session_id: &str, op: TodoOp) -> rusqlite::Result<TodoResult> {
    let find = |id: &str| {
        conn.query_row(
            "SELECT id, content, completed FROM todos WHERE session_id=?1 AND id=?2",
            params![session_id, id],
            row_item,
        )
        .optional()
    };
    Ok(match op {
        TodoOp::Add { content } => {
            let item = TodoItem { id: next_id(), content, completed: false };
            let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
                .map(|d| d.as_millis() as i64)
                .unwrap_or(0);
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO todos (id, session_id, content, completed, created_at) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,0,?4)",
                params![item.id, session_id, item.content, now],
            )?;
            TodoResult::Added { item }
        }
        TodoOp::List => TodoResult::Listed { items: list_sql(conn, session_id)? },
        TodoOp::Complete { id } => {
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE todos SET completed=1 WHERE session_id=?1 AND id=?2",
                params![session_id, id],
            )?;
            match find(&id)? {
                Some(item) => TodoResult::Completed { item },
                None => TodoResult::NotFound { id },
            }
        }
        TodoOp::Remove { id } => {
            let n = conn.execute("DELETE FROM todos WHERE session_id=?1 AND id=?2", params![session_id, id])?;
            if n > 0 { TodoResult::Removed { id } } else { TodoResult::NotFound { id } }
        }
    })
}
```

### F-12 · HTTP API parity: mode, model, permission mode, approvals list, rename/delete

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P3 |
| Size | M (2–4 hours) |
| Depends on | S-01, B-06, B-09 |
| Files to change | `src/server.rs`, `src/db.rs` |
| Read first | `src/server.rs`: `fn router` and its handlers, `fn set_mode`, `fn set_model`, `fn set_perm_mode`; `src/db.rs`: `fn set_session_title` |

#### What is wrong

The HTTP API can only create and list sessions, read messages, send a prompt, abort, answer one approval, and stream events. Everything else the TUI and GUI can do happens only in-process. An external client cannot switch plan/build mode, the model or the permission mode, list the approvals that are waiting, or rename or delete a session.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
pub fn router(state: Shared) -> Router {
    Router::new()
        .route("/api/sessions", post(create_session).get(list_sessions))
        .route("/api/sessions/{id}/messages", get(get_messages))
```

#### Why it matters

Scripts, editor plugins and other agents can only drive opencode-rust through HTTP. Without these routes they cannot switch to plan mode, stop a turbo run's permissions, or clean up sessions.

#### Steps

1. In `fn router`, add these routes. All of them are protected by the S-01 token automatically, because the middleware wraps the whole router.

| Method and path | Body | Answer | Calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/sessions/{id}/mode` | none | `{"mode":"plan"\|"build"}` | `mode_for` |
| `PUT /api/sessions/{id}/mode` | `{"mode":"plan"}` | same; 400 for an unknown mode | `AgentMode::parse`, `set_mode` |
| `GET /api/model` | none | `{"current":"…","available":["…"]}` | `current_model`, `available_models` |
| `PUT /api/model` | `{"model":"id"}` | `{"current":"id"}` | `set_model` |
| `GET /api/permission-mode` | none | `{"mode":"default"\|"manual"\|"turbo"}` | `perm_mode().as_str()` |
| `PUT /api/permission-mode` | `{"mode":"turbo"}` | `{"mode":"turbo","released":["apr_…"]}`; 400 for unknown | `PermissionMode::parse`, `set_perm_mode` |
| `GET /api/approvals` | none | array of `ApprovalNeeded` events | `pending_approvals` (B-09) |
| `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` | `{"title":"…"}` | the updated `Session`; 404 if unknown | `db.set_session_title` |
| `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` | none | 204; 404 if unknown | `abort_run` (B-06), wait until `run_active` is false (up to 10 s, else 409), then new `Db::delete_session` |

Use `axum::routing::{patch, put, delete}` the same way as `get` and `post`, e.g. `.route("/api/sessions/{id}/mode", get(get_mode_route).put(put_mode_route))`. Name the handlers `*_route`, so they are not confused with the `AppState` methods.

2. Write one handler per row, in the same style as `create_session`.

Add this handler right after `fn decide_approval` in `src/server.rs` (the other handlers follow the same pattern):
```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ModeReq {
    mode: String,
}

/// New (F-12): `PUT /api/sessions/{id}/mode`.
async fn put_mode_route(
    State(st): State<Shared>,
    AxPath(id): AxPath<String>,
    Json(req): Json<ModeReq>,
) -> Result<Json<Value>, StatusCode> {
    st.db.get_session(&id).map_err(internal)?.ok_or(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND)?;
    let mode = AgentMode::parse(&req.mode).ok_or(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
    st.set_mode(&id, mode);
    Ok(Json(json!({ "mode": mode.as_str() })))
}
```

3. In `src/db.rs`, add `pub fn delete_session(&self, id: &str) -> Result<bool>`. It deletes the session's messages and then the session in ONE transaction, and returns false when the id is unknown. Task B-38 also works in `db.rs` (transactions, foreign keys); apply this after it and use its transaction style.

Start the server with `serve_with_token(st, 0, "t".into())` (from S-01) and send requests with `reqwest::Client::builder().no_proxy().build()` and `.bearer_auth("t")`. Check the status code and the JSON for one good and one bad request each.

- [ ] Without the token, every new route answers 401

#### Do not

- Do not add routes outside `/api/`, and do not exempt any of them from the token.
- Do not let `DELETE` remove the session while its run is still writing messages; abort first.
- Do not return the API key or the config in any answer.

#### Steps

1. If you skipped F-04, add its `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]` section to

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
/// Submit the composer and name the chat after its first message. Shared by

```

Replace it with:
```rust
/// New (F-13): hold an exclusive lock on `<state_dir>/gui.lock` while the
/// window is open. The OS drops it when the process ends, even after a crash.
/// Needs Rust 1.89 or newer (`File::try_lock`).
fn single_instance_lock(state_dir: &std::path::Path) -> std::result::Result<std::fs::File, String> {
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(state_dir);
    let path = state_dir.join("gui.lock");
    let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .truncate(false)
        .write(true)
        .open(&path)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot open {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    match file.try_lock() {
        Ok(()) => Ok(file),
        Err(std::fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => {
            Err("Another Habi window is already open. Use that one, or close it first.".to_string())
        }
        Err(std::fs::TryLockError::Error(e)) => Err(format!("cannot lock {}: {e}", path.display())),
    }
}

/// New (F-13): show a fatal error to a user who may have no console window.
fn show_fatal_dialog(title: &str, msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("[gui] {title}: {msg}");
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        use windows::core::HSTRING;
        use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{MessageBoxW, MB_ICONERROR, MB_OK};
        // SAFETY: a plain Win32 call with valid wide strings that outlive it.
        unsafe {
            MessageBoxW(None, &HSTRING::from(msg), &HSTRING::from(title), MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR);
        }
    }
}

/// Submit the composer and name the chat after its first message. Shared by
/// the CLI prefill and the typed-send path so a prefilled launch names its
/// chat identically (it used to skip this and stay "New chat"). Returns the
```

/// Open the desktop app. Blocks until the window closes (mirrors `tui::run`).
pub async fn run(
    state: Arc<server::AppState>,
    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,
    prompt: Option<String>,
    boot_ms: u128,
) -> Result<()> {
    // F-13: one desktop window per state directory (two would write the same
    // database), and a readable message when WebView2 is missing.
    let _instance_lock = match single_instance_lock(&state.state_dir) {
        Ok(lock) => lock,
        Err(msg) => {
            show_fatal_dialog("Habi is already running", &msg);
            anyhow::bail!(msg);
        }
    };
    if let Err(e) = wry::webview_version() {
        let msg = format!(
            "Habi needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, and it was not found ({e}).\n\n\
             Install it from https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/ \
             and start Habi again."
        );
        show_fatal_dialog("WebView2 Runtime missing", &msg);
        anyhow::bail!(msg);
    }

````markdown
# opencode-rust

A lightweight AI coding agent written in Rust. It talks to any
**OpenAI-compatible** chat endpoint (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, Gemini's
OpenAI endpoint, or a local mock) and works inside your project folder. It can
read, search and edit files and run commands. It asks before risky actions
unless you allow them.

Three ways to use it:

| Mode | Command |
|---|---|
| Terminal UI (default) | `opencode-rust` |
| One prompt, no UI | `opencode-rust --headless "fix the failing test"` |
| Desktop app with a browser panel (Windows, WebView2) | `opencode-rust --gui` |

## Features

- Tools for the model: `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `list`, `glob`, `grep`,
  `webfetch`, `todo`, tools from MCP servers (stdio), and browser tools in the
  desktop app.
- Permissions: allow / ask / deny per tool, pattern rules, approval prompts,
  "always allow".
- Plan mode (read-only) and build mode. Turbo mode (no prompts — use with care).
- Subagents (`explore`, `worker`), `/team` (planner → workers → reviewer → summary),
  `/mission` briefings.
- Sessions stored in SQLite: fork, resume, diff, export to Markdown, `/compact`.
- Git-snapshot `/undo` and `/redo` of the agent's changes.
- Inline `/edit` with a diff preview.
- Skills and slash-command templates from Markdown files; `AGENTS.md` project
  instructions.
- "Ponytail" lazy-senior-dev discipline and an automatic review after changes
  (see Credits).

## Build

You need Rust (stable) and git.

- **Windows:** `cargo build --release` → `target\release\opencode-rust.exe`.
  The desktop app needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (preinstalled on
  Windows 11 and most Windows 10).
- **Linux:** the default build includes the desktop window and needs GTK/WebKit:
  `sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev` (Ubuntu 24.04).
  Without them, build the terminal UI and headless mode only:
  `cargo build --release --no-default-features`.
- **macOS:** not tested.

## Configure

Copy `config.example.toml` to `~/.config/opencode-rust/config.toml`
(Windows: `C:\Users\<you>\.config\opencode-rust\config.toml`), or point the
environment variable `OPENCODE_RUST_CONFIG` at any file. The smallest config:

```toml
[provider]
base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
api_key = "your-key"
model = "openai/gpt-4o"
```

Environment variables override the file: `OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY`,
`OPENCODE_RUST_BASE_URL`, `OPENCODE_RUST_MODEL`.

Sessions, snapshots and the crash log live in `%APPDATA%\opencode-rust`
(Windows) or `~/.local/share/opencode-rust` (Linux/macOS).

## Use

Run `opencode-rust --help` for all options. Common ones:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--headless "prompt"` | Run one prompt, print the result, exit |
| `--gui` | Desktop app instead of the terminal UI |
| `--model NAME` / `--base-url URL` | Override the provider for this run |
| `--port N` | Port of the local API (default: random, loopback only) |
| `preview <url>` | Open a standalone preview window |

Inside the terminal UI, type `/` for the command palette or press F1:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/build`, `/plan` | Normal mode / read-only plan mode |
| `/clear`, `/new` | Clear the view (history kept) / start a fresh session |
| `/compact` | Summarize old history, keep the recent tail |
| `/debt` | Laziness Meter: lines added/deleted, reuse hints |
| `/diff [id\|n]`, `/fork`, `/resume <id\|n>`, `/sessions` | Work with sessions |
| `/edit <file> <what>` | Inline edit with a diff preview |
| `/export [path]` | Write the transcript to Markdown |
| `/help` | Command and key reference |
| `/init` | Create a starter `AGENTS.md` |
| `/mission [kind] <goal>` | Run a briefing (Explore / Commit / Merge PR / Custom) |
| `/model [id]` | Show or switch the model |
| `/parallel <task>` | Run one task in two isolated git worktrees |
| `/review` | Senior-dev review of the uncommitted changes |
| `/skill install <path\|url>`, `/skills` | Install / list skills |
| `/team <goal>` | Plan → parallel workers → review → summary |
| `/todos` | Show this session's todo list |
| `/turbo [prompt]` | Full access, no approvals (careful) |
| `/undo`, `/redo` | Restore / re-apply the last git snapshot |
| `/quit` | Exit |

## Permissions and safety

By default `read`, `list`, `glob` and `grep` are allowed; `bash`, `write`,
`edit` and `webfetch` ask first; unknown tools ask. Change this in
`[permissions.defaults]` and add rules:

```toml
[[permissions.rules]]
tool = "bash"
pattern = "cargo test*"
action = "allow"
```

In headless mode nobody can answer a prompt — see `opencode-rust --help` for
how approvals are handled there. Turbo mode skips prompts entirely; only
`deny` rules still apply.

## Extending

- **Project instructions:** put an `AGENTS.md` in your project root (`/init` makes one).
- **Skills:** `.opencode/skills/<name>.md` or `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
  with optional frontmatter (`name`, `description`). User-wide:
  `~/.config/opencode-rust/skills/`.
- **Command templates:** `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`; `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced
  by what you type after `/<name>`.
- **MCP servers:**

```toml
[[mcp.servers]]
name = "my-server"
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "some-mcp-server"]
```

## Development

```
cargo build
cargo test
```

End-to-end runs without a real model: start the mock with
`cargo run --example mock_llm -- 18080`, then run opencode-rust with
`OPENCODE_RUST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1` and `OPENCODE_RUST_MODEL=mock`.

Desktop page tests: `bash tests/gui/run.sh` (needs Microsoft Edge).

Plans and history: `GOALS.md`, `M2-REPORT.md` … `M6-REPORT.md`, `FIX_PLAN.md`.

### H-02 · Make the desktop GUI an optional cargo feature

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/gui.rs`, `src/browser.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| Read first | `src/lib.rs`; `src/main.rs` function `run`; `src/gui.rs` function `detect_dev_server` |

> Verified: these exact edits were applied to commit 1f90442 and built with and
> without the feature. Default build: 184 tests pass. Without the GUI: 161 pass.
> In both, the only failure is the known Linux-only test (B-17).

#### What is wrong

`tao` and `wry` (the window and WebView libraries) are always compiled. On
Linux they need the GTK and WebKit development packages, so the crate cannot
build at all on a plain Linux machine or a CI runner without them — even
though the terminal UI and headless mode never use a window. The core also
reaches into the GUI module for one small helper, `detect_dev_server`.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `Cargo.toml`:
```toml
tao = "0.37"
wry = "0.57"
```

Find this code in `src/server.rs`:
```rust
        if let Some(url) = crate::gui::detect_dev_server(&output) {
```

#### Why it matters

You cannot run tests on Linux CI or a headless server without installing a
desktop stack. A cargo **feature** (an on/off switch in `Cargo.toml`) fixes
this: `gui` stays on by default, and `cargo build --no-default-features` builds
without it.

#### Steps

1. In `Cargo.toml`, make the two GUI crates optional and add the feature.

Find this code in `Cargo.toml`:
```toml
tao = "0.37"
wry = "0.57"
```

Replace it with:
```toml
tao = { version = "0.37", optional = true }
wry = { version = "0.57", optional = true }

[features]
# `gui` = the desktop window (`--gui`) and the `preview` subcommand.
# Without it (`cargo build --no-default-features`) the crate needs no
# GTK/WebKit on Linux; the terminal UI and headless mode still work.
default = ["gui"]
gui = ["dep:tao", "dep:wry"]
```

2. In `src/lib.rs`, compile the two window modules only with the feature.

Find this code in `src/lib.rs`:
```rust
pub mod gui;
```

Replace it with:
```rust
#[cfg(feature = "gui")]
pub mod gui;
```

Find this code in `src/lib.rs`:
```rust
pub mod preview;
```

Replace it with:
```rust
#[cfg(feature = "gui")]
pub mod preview;
```

3. Move `detect_dev_server` from `src/gui.rs` to `src/browser.rs`.
   `browser.rs` does not use `tao` or `wry`, so it is always compiled. First
   delete the function (with its doc comment) from `src/gui.rs`.

Find this code in `src/gui.rs`:
```rust
/// First `http://localhost:<port>` / `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` in tool output.
///
/// Dev servers print their URL in whatever shape the framework likes
/// ("Local: http://localhost:5173/", "listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000"),
/// so this scans rather than parses. Returns the origin only — the chip and
/// the CTA want something navigable, not a log line.
pub fn detect_dev_server(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    const PREFIXES: [&str; 2] = ["http://localhost:", "http://127.0.0.1:"];
    for (i, _) in text.char_indices() {
        let Some(tail) = text.get(i..) else { continue };
        for p in PREFIXES {
            let Some(rest) = tail.strip_prefix(p) else { continue };
            let port: String = rest.chars().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
            if port.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            return Some(format!("{p}{port}"));
        }
    }
    None
}
```

Replace it with nothing (delete it, plus the empty line after it).

<!-- TASK:H-03 -->
### H-03 · Add GitHub Actions CI (Linux + Windows)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P1 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | B-17 (otherwise the Linux job fails on a Windows-only test), H-02 (for the "core only" job) |
| Files to change | new `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| Read first | `Cargo.toml`, `tests/gui/run.sh` (first 30 lines) |

#### What is wrong

Nothing checks the code automatically. The milestone reports say every
test run was local (`M2-REPORT.md`: "no remote … no CI checks ever ran").
Because the repository is now on GitHub, a CI workflow can build and test
every push and pull request on Linux and Windows.

#### Where it is

There is no `.github/` folder yet.

#### Why it matters

A change that breaks the Windows build, or one that only works on the author's
machine, gets caught within minutes instead of weeks later.

#### Steps

1. Create the folder `.github/workflows/`.
   PowerShell: `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .github\workflows | Out-Null`.
   bash: `mkdir -p .github/workflows`.

2. Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with exactly this content:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep the "0 warnings" rule honest. If a new Rust release adds a lint that
  # breaks the build, fix the warning (or remove this line for a while).
  RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings

jobs:
  linux:
    name: Linux (full build, GUI included)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install GTK/WebKit (needed by tao and wry)
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo build --locked --tests
      - run: cargo test --locked

  linux-core:
    name: Linux (core only, no GUI feature)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo test --locked --no-default-features

  windows:
    name: Windows (full build + GUI page tests)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo build --locked --tests
      - run: cargo test --locked
      - name: GUI page tests (headless Edge)
        # Not yet proven on GitHub runners: remove continue-on-error once green.
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: bash tests/gui/run.sh || [ $? -eq 2 ]
```

3. Commit and push the branch. Open a pull request on GitHub and watch the
   three jobs under the "Checks" tab.

#### Tests to add

None. The workflow runs the existing tests.

#### Check you are done

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists with the content above (YAML is indentation-sensitive: 2 spaces, no tabs)
- [ ] On the pull request, the jobs "Linux (full build, GUI included)", "Linux (core only, no GUI feature)" and "Windows (full build + GUI page tests)" all run
- [ ] The two Linux jobs and the Windows build/test steps are green
- [ ] If a job is red, open its log, copy the first error into your report, and stop — do not "fix" CI by deleting tests or steps

#### Do not

- Do not remove `--locked`. It makes CI use exactly the versions in `Cargo.lock`.
- Do not add secrets or API keys to the workflow. The tests use local mock servers.
- Do not change the apt package list unless the log shows a missing library. These packages were checked on Ubuntu 24.04.

### H-05 · tests/gui/run.sh: also run on Linux/macOS

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Priority | P3 |
| Size | S (under 1 hour) |
| Depends on | none |
| Files to change | `tests/gui/run.sh` |
| Read first | `tests/gui/run.sh` (whole file, 88 lines) |

#### What is wrong

The page tests only run in Git Bash on Windows:

- the browser search knows only two Windows paths of Edge and the `msedge` command;
- `win()` uses `pwd -W`, which exists only in Git Bash/MSYS; elsewhere the page
  URL is broken and every suite reports "page produced no results";
- `head -n -2` (drop the last two lines) is GNU-only; macOS `head` refuses it.

#### Where it is

Find this code in `tests/gui/run.sh`:
```bash
# Chromium wants a Windows path when the page is on another drive.
win() { cd "$(dirname "$1")" && printf '%s/%s' "$(pwd -W)" "$(basename "$1")"; }
```

#### Why it matters

CI on Linux (task H-03) and developers on macOS cannot run the GUI tests, so GUI
regressions slip through.

#### Steps

1. Update the header comment.

Find this code in `tests/gui/run.sh`:
```bash
# Two suites, both run in real Microsoft Edge (no Node, no Playwright):
#   panel.js   — gui.html behaviour: URL bar, nav buttons, geometry, approvals
#   runtime.js — the JS injected into the preview webview (snapshot/click/type/wait)
#
# Usage: tests/gui/run.sh        (set EDGE=/path/to/msedge to override)
```

Replace it with:
```bash
# Two suites, both run in a real headless Chromium browser (Edge, Chrome or
# Chromium; no Node, no Playwright):
#   panel.js   — gui.html behaviour: URL bar, nav buttons, geometry, approvals
#   runtime.js — the JS injected into the preview webview (snapshot/click/type/wait)
#
# Usage: tests/gui/run.sh   (Windows Git Bash, Linux, macOS)
#        EDGE=/path/to/msedge or CHROME=/path/to/chrome picks the browser.
```

2. Find a browser on all three systems.

Find this code in `tests/gui/run.sh`:
```bash
edge=${EDGE:-}
if [ -z "$edge" ]; then
  for c in "/c/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe" \
           "/c/Program Files/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe"; do
    if [ -f "$c" ]; then edge=$c; break; fi
  done
fi
if [ -z "$edge" ]; then
  edge=$(command -v msedge || true)
fi
if [ -z "$edge" ]; then
  echo "SKIP: Microsoft Edge not found (set EDGE=/path/to/msedge)"
  exit 2
fi
```

Replace it with:
```bash
browser=${EDGE:-${CHROME:-}}
if [ -z "$browser" ]; then
  for c in "/c/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe" \
           "/c/Program Files/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe" \
           "/c/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe" \
           "/Applications/Microsoft Edge.app/Contents/MacOS/Microsoft Edge" \
           "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
           "/Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium"; do
    if [ -f "$c" ]; then browser=$c; break; fi
  done
fi
if [ -z "$browser" ]; then
  for name in msedge microsoft-edge microsoft-edge-stable google-chrome \
              google-chrome-stable chromium chromium-browser chrome; do
    if command -v "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then browser=$(command -v "$name"); break; fi
  done
fi
if [ -z "$browser" ]; then
  echo "SKIP: no Edge/Chrome/Chromium found (set EDGE= or CHROME= to its path)"
  exit 2
fi
```

3. Build the page URL without `pwd -W`. In Git Bash `cygpath -m` turns
   `/c/Users/...` into `C:/Users/...`; elsewhere the normal path is right.

Find this code in `tests/gui/run.sh`:
```bash
# Chromium wants a Windows path when the page is on another drive.
win() { cd "$(dirname "$1")" && printf '%s/%s' "$(pwd -W)" "$(basename "$1")"; }

run() {
  local name=$1 page=$2 out

```

Replace it with:
```bash
# file:// URL for a local file. Git Bash needs the Windows form (C:/...);
# Linux and macOS paths are already right.
file_url() {
  local dir
  dir=$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)
  if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'file:///%s' "$(cygpath -m "$dir/$(basename "$1")")"
  else
    printf 'file://%s/%s' "$dir" "$(basename "$1")"
  fi
}

run() {
  local name=$1 page=$2 out
  out=$("$browser" --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --window-size=1280,800 \
        --dump-dom "$(file_url "$page")" 2>/dev/null \
```

Find this code in `tests/gui/run.sh`:

```

Replace it with:

  sed '$d' "$root/src/gui.html" | sed '$d'   # drop </body></html> (portable)

## Appendix A — Things that look odd but are intentional (do NOT "fix" these)

1. **Reasoning is shown but never sent back to the model** on the OpenAI-compatible path. `Part::Reasoning` is stored for the transcript only. Keep it that way. One deliberate exception: the native Anthropic provider from task F-02 resends the thinking blocks of the current turn's tool-calling replies, unchanged. Current Claude models require that during a tool loop.
2. **Unknown tools default to "ask"** (`permissions.rs`). This is the safe default; tasks only make it stricter.
3. **The core HTTP server binds to `127.0.0.1` only**, and port `0` means "random free port". S-01 adds a token; it does not open the server to the network.
4. **The desktop browser panel is a native child WebView2 drawn over the HTML**, not an `<iframe>` (GOALS.md D1: many sites refuse to load in iframes). A native view cannot be covered by HTML, which is why the code hides it whenever a modal or overlay opens.
5. **No Chromium fork, no BrowserOS, no CDP dependency** (GOALS.md D2; B-B1 "replaced"). Browser tools work through the panel's own JavaScript bridge.
6. **MiroFish is AGPL-3.0** and must only ever run as a separate program that we talk to over HTTP. Never copy its code into this MIT repository.
7. **Ponytail prompts are vendored third-party text (MIT).** Keep `src/prompts/ponytail*.md` unchanged, license header included. Change behaviour in code (`agents.rs`, `server.rs`) instead.
8. **`panic = "abort"` in the release profile.** On a panic, `Drop` guards do not run, but the panic hook does. That is why B-16 restores the terminal in the hook.
9. **Turbo mode skips approvals on purpose**; only `deny` rules still apply. Tasks make it safer and clearer, never remove it.
10. **A new prompt on a busy session replaces the running run** (`kick_run`). The UIs should make this visible (F-06), not secretly queue prompts.
11. **`/undo` restores files in the working tree, not git commits**, and snapshots skip git-ignored files. B-39 documents this; it is not a bug to "fix" by touching commits.
12. **Tool-call arguments that are not valid JSON become `{"raw": …}`**, so a broken call never writes anything by accident. Tasks may improve the message to the model, not remove this safety.
13. **The UIs call `AppState` directly instead of the HTTP API.** The API is for outside programs. That is fine.
14. **`src/gui.html` is one file with no build step**, embedded with `include_str!`. Keep it that way: no npm, no bundler.
15. **Plan mode is enforced twice**: the tool list sent to the model is filtered, and every call is checked again before it runs. Keep both checks.

### Run against the mock model (no API key needed)

The mock answers with a scripted reply. By default it asks to **write a file
called `e2e-marker.txt`**, so run the agent from an empty temporary folder, not
from the repository.

PowerShell — terminal 1 (leave it running):
```
cargo run --example mock_llm -- 18080
```

PowerShell — terminal 2:
```
cargo build
$repo = (Get-Location).Path
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $env:TEMP\ocr-e2e | Out-Null
Set-Location $env:TEMP\ocr-e2e
$env:OPENCODE_RUST_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1"
$env:OPENCODE_RUST_MODEL = "mock"
$env:OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY = "none"
& "$repo\target\debug\opencode-rust.exe" --headless "hello"
```

bash — terminal 1: `cargo run --example mock_llm -- 18080`

bash — terminal 2:
```bash
cargo build
repo=$(pwd)
mkdir -p /tmp/ocr-e2e && cd /tmp/ocr-e2e
OPENCODE_RUST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1 OPENCODE_RUST_MODEL=mock OPENCODE_RUST_API_KEY=none \
  "$repo/target/debug/opencode-rust" --headless "hello"
```

After task S-02, headless mode denies tool calls unless you add `--yes`. With
the mock, use `--headless --yes "hello"` to see the write go through.

Special mock prompts: `parallel-agents …` makes the mock spawn two subagents.
`browser-smoke` asks for a `browser_navigate` (needs the GUI).

`bash tests/gui/run.sh`. It needs Microsoft Edge. Until H-05 it only works in
Git Bash on Windows. It prints PASS/FAIL per assertion and exits 0 (pass),
1 (fail) or 2 (skipped: no browser found).

## Appendix D — Glossary

| Word | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| **Workspace** | The project folder the agent works in: the folder you started opencode-rust from |
| **Session** | One conversation, stored in SQLite; can be forked, resumed, exported |
| **Run** | One answer cycle: the user prompt, then model calls and tools, until the model stops |
| **Tool call** | The model asks to run a tool (`bash`, `read`, …) with JSON arguments |
| **Permission rule / default** | allow / ask / deny decision for a tool (and a pattern such as a path or command) |
| **Approval** | When the decision is "ask": the UI shows a prompt; the answer is allow once, always, or deny |
| **Event bus** | `AppState.events`, a broadcast channel; every UI listens to it |
| **SSE** | Server-Sent Events: a streaming HTTP response made of `data: …` lines (used by model APIs and `/api/events`) |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol: a standard way to plug outside tool servers into an agent |
| **Subagent** | A child agent started with the `spawn` tool; runs in its own session and returns a summary |
| **Team** | `/team`: a planner splits the goal, workers run in parallel, a reviewer checks, a summary is written |
| **Mission** | `/mission`: a prepared briefing prompt (Explore, Commit, Merge PR, Custom) with an effort level |
| **Turbo** | Mode with no approval prompts (deny rules still apply), which continues on its own |
| **Ponytail** | Vendored "lazy senior developer" prompt rules + an automatic review after changes |
| **Compaction** | Replacing old messages with a summary so the conversation fits the model's context |
| **Snapshot** | A copy of changed files taken before a run, so `/undo` can restore them |
| **Headless** | Running one prompt without any UI (`--headless`) |
| **Child webview** | The second, native browser view inside the desktop window (the preview panel) |
| **IPC** | Messages between the web page (`gui.html`) and the Rust code (`window.ipc.postMessage`) |
| **Cargo feature** | An on/off switch in `Cargo.toml` that includes or leaves out code and dependencies |

*End of plan.*
